mr president, the promotion of a real functioning single market is one of the priorities of the european union and also one of the areas on which most of us would easily be in agreement. that is why we should promote competition and remove distortions and barriers. if we do so, this will be to the benefit of our economies and our people. let me mention three areas in which we should make progress: the energy sector, which is suffering a market fragmentation, distortion and different levels of national support; the telecoms market, where we should maintain competition and allow the development of a vibrant digital economy; and transport – better road transport will mean huge benefits for people, as we can see, for example, in my country. on the other hand, let me ask that one be cautious about using the term ‘social dumping’. the fact that that someone is getting lower wages is disturbing, but this does not necessarily mean there is any social dumping, because of the different cost structure and wages in the economy. i would also like to highlight the area of taxation, where the commission and parliament have made substantial progress. we are missing only one thing – namely bold action taken by the council. lastly, let me thank the commissioner and the commission for their very robust actions and very courageous approach. at the same time, let me say that we are not calling for more sanctions, but for better rules and for respect for the rules.
mr president, the purpose of european competition rules is to ensure a level playing field and fairness for all businesses, regardless of their size or the marketing capacity with which they can reach consumers. therefore, even from a fair market perspective, possible differences in seemingly identical products raise a number of questions. the question is whether consumer expectations are met in the case of so-called dual quality and how consumers' choices are determined by the brand under which a different product is sold. i trust that the european parliament will repeatedly support the provision calling on the commission to investigate possible differences in the composition of branded products and to assess whether they have negative consequences for the functioning of the internal market and also for the competitiveness of its actors, in particular smes. i would like to thank my colleagues in the committee on the internal market and consumer protection and the committee on economic and monetary affairs for supporting this amendment of mine. i hope that the commission will finally take this matter seriously.
madam president, i too very much appreciate the united line that has emerged from the discussions here. i am a little bit disappointed in the council in its position, because i think it is disrespectful to the european parliament not to be here on such an important issue. however, i think the fundamental error occurred when the unrealistic tests from the laboratory conditions were applied to the operation or were to be applied to the operation. i think that was a fundamental failure. i, on the other hand, appreciate the commission's approach, which has been expressed here today. i think that the approval of the objection, which we should approve according to the proposals of the petitioners, would have the opposite effect than they want. that means i object to the objection that has been raised here. i, of course, value quality in health, consumer protection, environmental protection, but this cannot be done in the interests of sustainable development.
in writing. the commission's proposal to increase the nox emission limits is an unprecedented step backwards in the field of health and environmental protection. for the first time in history, the proposal would increase nox emissions from diesel engines by 110% compared to the original plan. at a time when the world is buzzing with the dieselgate scandal and the paris agreement, such a proposal seems like a bad joke. moreover, a general derogation from the applicable emission limits is incompatible with the objective and content of regulation (ec) no 715/2007 and exceeds the implementing powers provided for therein. it is typical for this commission that the decision was approved by the member states' representatives in the technical committee for motor vehicles instead of the ordinary legislative process. producers always claim that they need a long-term perspective and stable conditions. in this case, they had nine years to adapt to the new requirements, and some manufacturers are meeting the limits set. that's why i say that you can't change the law to punish the honest for the dishonest. we are now hearing that if we do not accept this commission proposal, the next one will be even weaker, that it is better to have this proposal than no proposal because it would have an even greater impact on the environment. it's a blackmail, if you ask me. once set, the objectives must be respected, implemented and enforced. parliament has no choice but to veto the entire bill.
i would like to stress, madam president, that the european parliament's report on intercultural dialogue is not only important for its timeliness, but also because of the threat of radicalism and conflict. so it cannot be just a response to this momentary threat, but it must be systematic work, which is the best prevention against national conflicts and intolerance and against the rise of violence. european values are not artificial. these are inherently common human values, and it is therefore important that we, the citizens of the european union, understand and share them. the european union is growing from the roots of judaism, christianity and antiquity, but it is made up of very different peoples and cultures, it is affected by globalisation, by migration, and therefore it is necessary to work on better understanding and sharing of these values. the report contains many important findings and suggestions, which is why i decided to support it, as it stresses the need for ethical education and values, citizenship education, knowledge of foreign languages, which is essential for joint activities and dialogue and must be promoted. education must be guided not only by rights but also by responsibilities. i think that the solidarity shown today by hundreds of volunteers is proof that european human values in general are alive and worth promoting.
on behalf of the alde group.– madam president, i am pleased with the outcome of this report. it comes at a key moment where we move from a regulation designed primarily to repair the legislative holes which were so evident in the crisis, towards the capital markets union, which aims to encourage more investment and growth in europe. the key aspect of the stocktaking report is the call for the commission to undertake cumulative impact assessments and, at regular intervals, of all of the new legislation enacted in the aftermath of the crisis. i fully support this call. in my view it is imperative that the impact assessment looks at how different pieces of european legislation in the area of financial services interact with each other. are there any gaps or loopholes? are there any unintended consequences? how has europe’s competitiveness been affected globally? we must gain a full understanding of the new legislation, at which point we can focus on building a robust and competitive capital markets union. there are a number of points which i have pushed during the negotiation. firstly, in order to ensure europe’s competitiveness on a global level, we must have a coherent framework in place with regard to dealing with third countries, for example in ucits. secondly, access to finance for smes is key in order to bring europe back to sustained growth. we must ensure that the regulation in place does not hinder this process, and must reduce as much as possible any barriers for smes’ financing which are due to excessive regulation.
mr president, i would like to give my full support to this report, which has been presented to us, because after a thorough study i believe that it really reflects the real situation in which european financial services find themselves. i think it also reflects how different the situation is in the european union and the united states. we really need to ensure access to finance, to investment, to innovation for our industry, for our services, for our financial sector. it is of course essential that the policy we wish to implement is not just a tool, but also contains the target effects, that is, where we really want to go in deregulating the markets. i quite disagree with the idea that one of my colleagues on the left of the spectrum has expressed here, who is not in favor of deregulating markets and at the same time misses the fact that a decentralized banking system has not been achieved. i think it goes hand in hand.
in writing. today we were discussing the obstacles to women entrepreneurs. it's an interesting topic, but i don't think it's the key. the situation of women, who are most at risk of poverty, have more problems in the labour market than men and the problem of how to combine personal, family and professional life are certainly more pressing problems that women 'burn' much more than the question of their entrepreneurial potential. i am skeptical about the content of this report from the outset, as i do not think it offers any solution to the problems raised. i don't even think that the solution to empowering women should be to increase their involvement in private enterprise. i don't think this is the answer.
in writing.– i would like to congratulate the rapporteur, mr plura, for his excellent report. the report focuses on key issues that seek to improve skills policies in europe with a view to fighting youth unemployment. youth are affected by unemployment more than any other age group – approximately 7.5 million young europeans are currently neither in employment nor in training. to reduce youth unemployment, several actions should be taken. first, we need to build stronger partnerships between authorities, educational institutions and businesses to better forecast future skills needs. second, a new impetus should be given to stem skills and vocational education. best practices should be exchanged between member states. third, young people’s employability can be further improved by adopting new teaching and training methods. schools should put more focus on soft skills to prepare youngsters for real ‘work-life’. also, entrepreneurship education should be fostered from an early age. last but not least, it should be the young people themselves who take their future in their hands. the biggest skill that a young man or a woman can have is the sense of initiative and self-responsibility. only like this can we really strive for the dreams we all have!

in writing. ‒ youth unemployment is a long-term eu problem that needs to be addressed as quickly as possible. i am in favour of deeper cooperation between schools and employers, leading to the adaptation of teaching to the specific needs of the current labour market. only creative teaching in schools and highly trained teachers can impart skills to make it easier for young people to enter the labour market. i have long supported youth entrepreneurship, especially in the form of start-ups, through which fresh projects of talented young people are given a chance. i believe that it is necessary to link theoretical training with practical training, which significantly facilitates the transition from the educational process to the employment process.

in writing. ‒ although presumption of innocence is a fundamental principle of law enshrined in the eu charter of fundamental rights, there are still reports of violations of this principle by some member states. this new directive seeks to better ensure that the right to be presumed innocent until proven guilty in criminal proceedings is respected in the eu. it significantly improves citizens’ rights to a fair trial as well as the provisions on public statement about accused persons. moreover, member states should ensure appropriate presentation of the person so as not to create an impression of guilt. these changes will help to avoid any arbitrariness and abuse during criminal proceedings.

in writing. ‒ today we voted on a report that is part of a package of three proposals for directives aimed at strengthening procedural rights in the eu. these three directives will allow the finalisation of the european legal system that exists in the area of the rights of defence of suspects, accused persons or persons charged in criminal proceedings throughout the european union. these are key instruments that should guarantee a fair trial throughout the european union and full respect for the rights of the defence as guaranteed by the european treaties, the european charter of fundamental rights and the european convention on human rights. i therefore welcome the european commission's proposal for a directive to strengthen certain aspects of the presumption of innocence and the right to be present at criminal proceedings. the presumption of innocence is a fundamental right and a fundamental principle which serves to exclude arbitrariness and any abuse in criminal proceedings and is the principle underpinning the protection of the right to a fair trial in accordance with article 6 of the european convention on human rights, article 48 of the charter of fundamental rights of the european union, the international covenant on civil and political rights and the universal declaration of human rights. that's why i voted for the motion.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the agreement reached on the directive on the presumption of innocence. this directive aims to ensure that the principle of the presumption of innocence is applied throughout the eu and the member states must act accordingly until the guilt of the suspect has been proved. the text adopted recognises that the burden of proof must lie with the prosecution and that the accused must have the benefit of any doubt. additionally, the right to remain silent must not be used against individuals, a european parliament press release explains. once formally adopted by the council, the member states will have two years to transpose the text.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the regulation on the safety of personal protective equipment such as life jackets or bicycle helmets. since 1989, the placing of personal protective equipment (ppe) on the eu market has been fully harmonised through council directive 89/686/eec. in the intervening 25 years, this directive has enabled a functioning single market. despite this, the existing ppe legislation is in need of updating in line with the new legislative framework (nlf) which is a package of measures designed to streamline and simplify regulations of goods across the single market. in particular, in response to concerns that current regulatory requirements are confusing and duplicative, the regulation clarifies the role of economic operators, reinforces cooperation between actors and introduces common definitions. the common approach under the nlf also clarifies the powers of market surveillance authorities enabling the tracking and returning of unsafe goods placed on the single market.

in writing. i did not support the objection to the commission regulation on the compositional and information requirements for cereal-based infant formulae and foods for infants. unfortunately, the objection was eventually passed, albeit by a slim majority, and the commission regulation was vetoed. the regulation, which set the optimum sugar intake for infants, corresponded to the nutritional requirements set out in the world health organisation (who) framework. the opinion of the czech government, which i had at my disposal, also spoke in favour of the commission's regulation. the positive aspect is that the resolution dropped the requirement of zero tolerance for pesticides, which was illusory in the face of reality. the commission monitors the permitted levels of pesticides closely and its decisions are based on the recommendations of the european food safety authority, which i consider to be a sufficient guarantee. i had no factual or technical reason for rejecting the implementing regulation and therefore did not vote for it. the commission will now have to present a new regulation.
in writing. ‒ i opposed the objection raised by the greens/efa group on the draft delegated act by the commission on the specific compositional and information requirements for processed cereal-based food and baby food. according to regulation no 609/2013 on foods for specific groups, the commission is responsible for drafting specific compositional and information requirements for processed cereal-based food and baby food. current compositional requirements are about 20 years old and were agreed based on studies dating back to 1989-1990. the commission draft, which is opposed by this objection, complies with the most recent relevant codex alimentarius standards from 2006. although some of the findings may be outdated it is already a considerable improvement on the current situation and i find it regrettable that its entry into force will be delayed until a new study is published.

in writing. the series of terrorist attacks that took place in france in 2015 culminated in november of that year in paris. following these attacks, france formally invoked the principle of mutual defence enshrined in article 42 (7) of the treaty on european union. in this context, the european parliament adopted a resolution confirming the european union's willingness to meet its mutual defence commitments and proposing several instruments to strengthen mutual defence at european level. i have long been one of those who have called for the strengthening of european mutual defence instruments. unfortunately, the situation around the eu's borders has deteriorated and so we need to strengthen its hard power. we cannot pretend that our security is guaranteed by nato alone. i therefore agree with the need for a greater and really effective exchange of information between european intelligence services and the creation of european command structures. it would not be a replacement or a limitation of nato, on the contrary, all these defence initiatives should be closely coordinated with nato. the czech republic is undoubtedly ready to meet its commitments in the framework of common european defence. as one of the few member states to provide specialists and material to contribute to the common european defence, also during the current migration crisis.

in writing. ‒ i was very pleased to support the motion for a resolution on article 42 (7) in response to the terrorist attacks in paris. implementing article 42 (7) which guarantees aid and cooperation to our french allies who rightly feel threatened is our moral obligation. but it is important to remember that these terrorist attacks were not just an attack on france or the people of paris, but were intended as an aggression against the whole of the european union and the ideals of liberal democracy; the indirect targets of the terrorists were therefore all those who identified with european culture and civilization. it is therefore essential to respond with a single european voice. this proposal is also important because it sets a precedent for the future eu's common foreign and security policy. one of the reasons for the success of these terrorist attacks was the fact that european intelligence and security services were not able to cooperate and coordinate effectively. the common security policy will not compete with or replace nato structures; the aim of the new regulation is to improve and deepen cooperation between the defence forces of the member states. by working together across the eu, we will be better able to confront a bloodthirsty enemy like the islamic state, and we will be better able to stand up to russian aggression or to tackle the complex challenges of the refugee crisis.
in writing. i supported today's resolution on the mutual defence clause (article 42 (7) of the treaty on european union) as the right response to the impulse given by the french government to invoke this clause after the terrorist attacks of november last year. the french government was the first government ever to do so and it has been shown that there is no established or basic procedure for responding to the application of this clause and that the consequent measures are taken ad hoc. the french call is thus intended to provide an impetus for the development of the potential of all the provisions of the treaties relating to security and defence, which can gradually create a more unified approach for the union in these areas. in the meantime, however, there is a need to strengthen the intelligence sharing and operational cooperation between the national security services responsible for advancing the security and defence of the union.

in writing. the un human rights committee is an organization that is criticized from perhaps every angle, which is certainly one of the indicators that it is doing its job well. one of the most important guidelines for the un human rights committee is also the european parliament's resolution on the matter, which represents the ep's priorities in the field of human rights protection in the world. i voted for the resolution without reservation. however, i abstained on the question of creating humanitarian corridors for refugees to eu countries. at this point, it is not clear what is meant by the much-debated establishment of humanitarian corridors. on the one hand, it can be an effective tool to facilitate the escape of people from war-threatened areas, and on the other hand it can be a 'highway' to europe rather than the intended catalyst of economic migration. this would ultimately make the situation worse for those refugees who are actually fleeing for their lives. i certainly welcome the mention of the need to define climate refugees. there is no doubt that ongoing climate change is threatening many central africans, and they are moving toward more climate-friendly areas. in view of the potential mass nature of this movement, it is necessary to prepare and develop an appropriate legal framework for climate migration now.

in writing. i supported the report on the establishment of a european platform to strengthen cooperation in preventing and deterring undeclared work. the draft council and ep decision is based on a coercive approach, involving enhanced cooperation to combat labour law violations, tax evasion and breaches of social protection requirements. in particular, the purpose of the platform is to develop a reliable and efficient system for the rapid exchange of information in addressing undeclared work and to improve the capacity of national labour inspection systems to carry out checks and to address cross-border aspects of undeclared work through measures such as joint operations, relevant databases and staff exchanges. it is therefore a support instrument complementary to existing national instruments, as the fight against illegal employment and business is a primary responsibility of the member states.
in writing. undeclared work accounts for up to 30% of gross domestic product in some eu member states. the implications for the national budgets, which subsequently finance the necessary policies, including, for example, education, infrastructure or employment, cannot therefore be underestimated. nor can the consequences of undeclared work for the perpetrators themselves be underestimated. they are often exposed to unfair conditions, low wages, and a complete lack of social security. i voted in favour of the report on the establishment of a european platform to strengthen cooperation in preventing and deterring undeclared work, as these activities of the shadow and grey economy are unacceptable to both sides. i also supported the platform to make european social partners equal partners and to involve all eu member states, because this is not a problem for a few selected countries. it concerns everyone and therefore requires a coordinated approach at european, national and regional levels. in this regard, the platform should serve as an optimal venue for the exchange of information and sharing of good practices between states. not only to boost the current relatively low economic growth but also to combat deflation, undeclared work needs to be reported as soon as possible, preferably by introducing both restrictive and proactive measures.
in writing. i supported the draft decision establishing a european platform to strengthen cooperation on the prevention and deterrence of undeclared work, as it is an important step towards addressing the range of undeclared work problems affecting millions of workers in the eu undignified to unsafe working conditions, lower wages, loss of social security or social rights in general. i consider the strength of the platform to be that it will involve a wide range of stakeholders, in particular representatives of the member states and the social partners, and will operate on the basis of the exchange of experience and best practice. i also expect the platform to become a place of enhanced cooperation in order to prepare and implement effective enforcement and support measures in the area of undeclared work.
in writing. i supported the report on the establishment of a european platform to strengthen cooperation in the prevention of undeclared work. the european parliament proposes by this resolution to amend the commission proposal at first reading. this is the creation of a coordination platform composed of representatives of the national authorities of the member states, representatives of the commission and also of a number of social partners. the european foundation for the improvement of living and working conditions (eurofound), the european agency for safety and health at work (eu-osha) and a representative of the international labour organisation (ilo) will also be present. i consider that enhanced cooperation between member states at eu level is necessary to enable member states to prevent undeclared work more effectively. this should be done through the exchange of best practices and information and the provision of expertise and analysis at eu level between the responsible persons and institutions. in order to make the platform effective, it is proposed that member states should be obliged to participate. i think it's important to be efficient and to have the least cost to put on this platform. undeclared work is a growing phenomenon with many causes and interconnections and has negative effects on the labour market and public budget revenues. it ultimately harms both the employer and the employee.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on establishing a european platform to enhance cooperation in the prevention and deterrence of undeclared work. this report recommended the establishment of a european platform to enhance the cooperation at union level in tackling undeclared work. this mean the prevention, deterrence and combating of undeclared work as well as encouraging and promoting declared work. if properly implemented, the overriding objective of the platform shall be to provide value-added input at union level to the efforts of member states and union institutions to successfully tackle the complex problem of undeclared work and its manifold implications and consequences including encouraging and promoting declared work. the platform shall, to that end, contribute to an improvement in union and national law, help to achieve the union’s employment targets providing a more effective union framework for employment and workplace health and safety.

in writing. the adoption of a bilateral safeguard clause to the association agreement between the european union and the republic of moldova will allow both parties to temporarily suspend tariff preferences in the event of a significant increase in imports causing economic injury to the domestic industry of the importing party. for example, this clause will help to protect the european market from a large increase in imports of certain agricultural products without a clear justification of their origin. the agreement also includes a so-called anti-circumvention mechanism, which is a kind of guarantee to protect the eu market, but it is worth remembering that in practice the eu has never had to use this type of clause.

in writing. the adoption of a bilateral safeguard clause to the association agreement between the european union and georgia will allow both parties to temporarily suspend tariff preferences in the event of a significant increase in imports causing economic injury to the domestic industry of the importing party. article 27 of the agreement contains a so-called anti-circumvention mechanism which provides for the possibility to re-impose a duty rate under the most-favoured-nation clause if imports of certain processed agricultural products originating in georgia exceed a certain threshold (average annual volume of imports) without duly justifying their exact origin. the inclusion of the circumvention clause is necessary to prevent imports of non-georgian products into the union via georgia benefiting from the provisions of the agreement and, in particular, to prevent countries which have concluded a bilateral free trade agreement with georgia, such as turkey and the europmed countries, from using the agreement with the union to circumvent the 'rules of origin'. this provision also serves as a mechanism to protect georgian producers against possible abuse and unprecedented competition by non-georgian producers.
in writing. ‒ the agreement between the european union and georgia, signed in june 2014 and endorsed by the european parliament on 18 december 2014, is a significant means for georgian exporters to access european markets and thus relieve themselves of pressure from their russian neighbour. the association agreement, which has also been offered to armenia and moldova, introduces an important preferential regime between the eu and georgia and allows georgian exporters to access the european single market on better terms. it should be noted that the eu market is the most important export destination for georgia. the amendment we're debating here is an important part of the signed agreement, specifically article 27, which contains the so-called anti-circumvention mechanism. i am in favour of the inclusion of a circumvention clause to prevent non-compliance with the wording of the agreement and to prevent falsification of the rules of origin. this provision is intended to protect both georgian and european producers and to prevent the use of favourable rules and imports of non-georgian products under the said agreement. it is our duty to uphold the agreements we have signed and to ensure that both parties involved respect the rules of the game. i would also like to support the proposal for a reporting obligation which this proposal establishes for the commission, whereby the commission submits to the co-legislators an annual report on the implementation of that regulation, which it subsequently publishes.

in writing. i voted against the motions to raise objections to the authorisation of genetically modified soybeans. all three species for which authorisation is concerned are herbicide resistant and therefore have good conditions for effective cultivation. the applications were also subject to scientific risk assessment at both european level (gmo panel of the european food safety authority (efsa)) and national level, which was favourable. i therefore regard the statement of objections as a position motivated by political rather than factual and professional reasons.
‒ the subject of genetically modified crops is a highly technical one and therefore, in my view, it should be primarily up to experts in the field of biology and genetics to assess whether a given genetically modified food is dangerous or not. in the three cases voted on today by the european parliament, namely mon 87708, 89788, 87705, 89788 and fg72 soybeans, the conclusions of the european food safety authority are available, and the crops were then examined in the czech republic by the scientific committee for gm food and feed. none of these professional bodies see any health risks. while i believe that restraint and caution are needed when genetically modified food is placed on the market, because the field of genetics is still developing, albeit very rapidly, i also believe that european legislation is sufficiently prudent in this respect and that the standards for placing genetically modified food on european markets are sufficiently strict. if the european food safety authority has, in accordance with the legislative procedure, recognised the crops concerned as not being harmful on the basis of the research, i see no reason to withdraw the commission's draft implementing decisions.

in writing. ‒ i voted together with the majority of the parliament to reject the objection on emissions from passenger and commercial vehicles. this vote enabled us to clear the way to the second real driving emissions package, to avoid any uncertainties and will now oblige the industry to meet the strict deadlines foreseen by legislation. furthermore, it will help us to prevent that jobs are lost in the sector and that measures are taken immediately to safeguard air quality. the outcome of the vote means that the manufacturers will need to bring down the discrepancy to a ‘conformity factor’ of a maximum of 2.1 (110%) for new vehicle models by september 2017, and as a second step, lower the discrepancy to a factor of 1.5 (50%) by january 2020 for all new vehicle models. commissioner bieńkowska has made a further commitment today to bring down the conformity factor to 1 by 2023.
in writing. – although the majority of the european parliament’s members did not object, the compromise proposed by eu member states stating that, following the entry into force of a more accurate testing method of car emission next year, new models would be allowed to emit nitrogen oxide at a rate of 168 milligrams per kilometre, despite an eu limit of 80mg/km, i decided to refuse this compromise. by endorsing this proposal, the european parliament basically allowed diesel cars to emit double the legal emission limit of nitrogen oxide until 2020. the result of the vote is, i think, a blanket derogation from our emission limits. i believe it is urgent that stricter rules for car emissions testing apply in europe.
in writing. it is understood that when the emission measurement procedure is changed (measurement in normal operation), the engines will show different (higher) emissions. the transitional measures proposed by the commission to allow cars with emissions above 80 mg nox per km to pass the test are therefore understandable. acceptance of the objection would imply a de facto tightening of the standard, but without a proper examination. i voted against it.
in writing. ‒ after careful consideration, i have decided to abstain, although i am not happy with the commission's decision to introduce emissions tests in normal operation and consider the permitted deviations in emission measurements to be unduly benevolent. i rely on the commission's promise to apply the review clause to bring emissions levels as close as possible to the approved figures with minimum deviations. this requires the speedy elimination of technical irregularities in the pems measurement software that may be partly responsible for deviations in emission measurements.
in writing. in its objection, the european parliament criticises the commission for having made changes beyond its competence in the draft implementing decision concerning, in particular, the introduction of a new real-use emission measurement (rde) system and for having increased the nitrogen emission limit for 2019 and 2020 above the target value of 80 mg/km, namely 168 and 120 mg/km respectively. the current value is around 600 mg. the eu should strive for the highest possible emission reductions, the real value of emissions (where our desire to improve the environment is on the one hand, the technological capabilities of manufacturers and the 'life cycle' of innovation in the automotive industry on the other) have been and will be discussed. but above all, it is important for us to have an rde testing system in place as soon as possible, which will provide us with important and much more accurate information. although i am very dissatisfied with the form in which the commission has proposed the amendments, and in this respect the objection is entirely justified, i am also aware that the adoption of the objection would dramatically delay the introduction of the rde and would have a negative impact on both the environment and the manufacturer.
in writing. i voted to reject the objection to the compromise agreement on the new testing rules. delaying this decision to increase the emission limits for diesel vehicles for nitrogen oxides would only increase the legal uncertainty for both manufacturers and approval authorities. any delay in the implementation of this legislation would leave very little time for the necessary changes and would ultimately delay the desired positive environmental impacts.
in writing. ‒ the european parliament rejected a resolution objecting to a compromise on testing of car emissions and demanding a greater say in the eu’s decision-making process on this issue. the resolution was motivated mainly by efforts to limit air pollution from car emissions, namely by introducing a narrower margin for testing emissions on the road. while i believe that stricter rules for car emissions testing should apply, i am however convinced that approval of the resolution would put the entire process into question, create uncertainty for car-making industry and citizens by prolong the process of introducing stricter norms in real driving conditions with very uncertain outcome. therefore, i decided to vote against this resolution. now i however expect the car industry to embrace the new rules and work with us to improve car emissions testing. car producers had a long time to do something about this situation, and it is now time they start taking this issue very seriously. i expect the revision clause to be used in 2017 in order to introduce an even stricter conformity factor within just a very limited period of time.
in writing. - i voted against the objection. i consider the decision of my colleagues to be unnecessary and very wrong. now, of all things, the automotive industry needs uncertainty and decision-making delay. the original agreement between the member states was already sufficiently harsh. the excessive aggressiveness of parliament will not solve anything and will rather make the situation worse. it will mean delays and eventually, perhaps even harsher demands on the automobile industry. the european commission has already partially met the requirements of the objection, when it presented revised legislation tightening supervision of laboratories last week.
madam president, i am quite fascinated by the way some of my colleagues say their minute and then walk away, not knowing the facts at all. i don't know of any example of a state that, if it fences itself, increases its employment, increases its gdp productivity. with all due respect to my predecessors, europe is the truly significant service provider, it's maybe 40% of our gdp that we provide, and that's our competitive advantage. liberalisation of this space is in our vital interest. it will certainly increase employment. our aim should be to liberalise this environment and to protect what is important. these public services are excluded from this liberalisation for the time being by international agreements and we can continue to protect them. for me, for example, it was essential that municipalities and their jurisdiction were not discriminated against in any way by this agreement. we're at the beginning, we should finish this negotiation, this is just a mandate for this negotiation.
in writing. – negotiations for a trade in services agreement (tisa), under way since april 2013, aim at establishing international minimum rules for trade in sectors such as financial, digital and transport services between 23 wto members – eu included, accounting for 70% of global trade in services. these rules will facilitate and liberalise their trade in services. this report defines the european parliament priorities for the european commission’s mandate for negotiation. through this report, we made it clear to that these negotiations should deliver a deal that tisa should afford more rights to our citizens at home and remove some obstacles to our companies abroad. if the final agreement does not reflect the european parliament’s priorities, we have the right to veto the text.
in writing. i voted for the report presented because i think it creates a very good platform for the negotiations themselves on the proposed trade in services agreement (tisa). the document sets out clear guidelines, compliance with which should prevent the risks inherent in tisa (privatisation of public sector services, misuse of data in the field of information services, deregulation of financial services, etc.). the document voted today is the most progressive report to come out of the committee on international trade in recent years, even according to many critics of the agreements in the making. it is only to be hoped that the negotiations of other free trade agreements, such as ttip and ceta, will be treated in a similar way.
in writing. ‒ in general, i am in favour of liberalising trade in services as far as possible. but i voted against because an amendment was added to the ilo standards where i cannot agree, for example, to tell employers who they can and cannot hire or how they can rate a worker. if the market is to be genuinely liberalised, it is therefore not possible to discriminate against drivers and road hauliers, for example, and to restrict their access to the market. i voted against it.
in writing. ‒ i supported the report on the services agreement (tisa) because i am a supporter of efforts to liberalise services. i am pleased that the ep is playing an active role in the negotiation process and is clearly supporting the european negotiators. it is in our interest to negotiate an ambitious agreement that includes fast-growing economies, including china. for this reason, the negotiations should also focus on the full compatibility of tisa with gats, so that there are no obstacles to its integration into the wto framework. the objective should be to extend the application of advanced rules on trade in services, including rules in the area of digital trade or to facilitate cross-border movement of persons for the purpose of trade, to the widest possible extent.
in writing. ‒ the services market is the backbone of the european economy. as a social democrat, i am particularly interested in improving working conditions and public services. the current rules on the services market are outdated and not very functional, so we need new, clear and effective rules. a new and meaningful agreement on trade in services was to be established as soon as possible. but we will ensure that the rights of employees are not restricted or the level of public and cultural services. the agreement shall not jeopardise the ability of the eu or the member states to ensure and protect labour standards and functional regulations. the commission is given a new mandate by parliament which, among other things, emphasises the requirements of a global level playing field and reciprocity in market access. if this mandate is not respected, the european parliament may exercise its right of veto. as a member of the itre committee, i will monitor in particular the telecommunications and energy services sectors, which are of vital importance to citizens and contribute to the creation of quality jobs.
in writing. i supported the european parliament's motion for a resolution containing a european parliament recommendation to the commission on the negotiation of a trade in services agreement (tisa), which should strengthen the importance of services to the world economy. the agreement should contribute to greater progress in financial services, national regulation, telecommunications and other services. the tisa agreement will have a positive impact on the services sector by facilitating access to the services market of third countries and enhancing transparency, and will contribute to intensifying cooperation with non-european countries in this field. tisa can bring more rights and lower prices to consumers, more job opportunities and protection for workers. in the area of services, it will also bring, inter alia, better quality, safety, affordability and equal treatment.
in writing. ‒ it voted in favour of the report on tisa (trade in services agreement) negotiations today, which started in spring 2013. the trade in services agreement is a multilateral trade agreement currently being negotiated by 23 members of the world trade organisation (wto), including the eu – with the aim to liberalise trade in services among those parties. with this report, the european parliament aims to provide the commission with guidelines on the parliament’s priorities for the remainder of the tisa negotiations. indeed, tisa represents an opportunity for the european market to ensure reciprocity for european companies and will thus benefit european consumers and workers.
in writing. ‒ i have decided to support this report, which contains very detailed recommendations from the european parliament to the european commission, and i believe that the commission should certainly include these proposals in the tisa agreement. i consider the recommendations on personal data protection to be very important, as the commission is obliged to ensure that personal data can only be transferred outside the union if the provisions of eu data protection law on transfers to third countries are respected. furthermore, it should only negotiate provisions on the flow of personal data if the application of eu data protection legislation is fully guaranteed and respected. i also agree with the need to exclude existing and future services of general interest, including services of general economic interest (including, but not limited to, health, social services, etc.), from eu obligations.

european parliament, i welcome the opportunity to join you today to discuss an important topic on behalf of the high representative federica mogherini: the situation in libya, the advances made so far and the challenges that are still lying ahead. we have seen considerable progress since the last debate in this chamber. the libyan political agreement was signed in skhirat on 17 december, a presidency council has been formed and is meeting and working, and the government of national accord has been announced and the temporary security council has been appointed. as soon as she could, on friday 8 january, the high representative travelled to tunis to meet the presidency council to express the eu’s political support for their action and to discuss with all its members, all together, about the immediate and longer-term assistance the european union can provide to the new libyan authorities. she reminded them that the european union’s eur 100 million aid package for libya has been ready for a while and that all it takes for its full implementation is for the government of national accord to start working in the country. on the ground, promising new truces were signed recently between the municipalities: between misrata and the neighbouring tawergha, finally putting an end to an enmity dating back to the 2011 revolution; and between zawiya and zintan west of tripoli, in sorman, again just west of tripoli and in the south, although it remains shaky between the tebus and the touareg, who have been fighting for months in obari. the house of representatives voted on 25 january to approve the libyan political agreement, albeit conditionally. the recognition of the un-brokered process is the sole genuine political process in libya. at the same time the house of representatives did not approve the ministerial appointments in the proposed gna. further discussions are required, but eventually we hope and expect that libyan decision-makers will realise that there is no alternative to a unity government representing all the regions and all the social and political groups and that only such a government will give real hope to the libyan people that their country can finally tackle, hopefully once and for all, the spread of terrorism, an economy on the brink and threats to libya’s integrity and development. when the unity government is endorsed by parliament, the priority will be the security of the population and the fight against daesh. tripoli’s security must be essentially enforced by the libyans themselves. libyans will provide the core of the new security apparatus and the international community can provide further training and assistance should the new government request it. the european union is also actively engaged in this security effort. our liaison and planning cell in tunis has been active and will continue to support the united nations and the new libyan authorities in drafting plans. member states have agreed to bolster the cell and also to reinforce civilian planning capacity through a reactivated and expanded eu-bam mission. it should become operational in the next few weeks and provide capacity on a broad spectrum of police support including counter-terrorism, customs, border security and migration. mr president, honourable members, the democratic transition in libya is a difficult and complicated process, but a un-brokered libyan political agreement has made important progress and deserves our continued support. the alternative is simply chaos – a country on the brink of economic catastrophe – and all this can still be avoided. it is our duty as libya’s neighbours to continue supporting the united nations process and the gna, and we are fully committed to continuing doing exactly that.

in writing. although unemployment in europe is gradually declining, up to 23 million active citizens are still out of work. there is one figure that i find even more frightening, and that is the 123 million europeans at risk of or affected by poverty and social exclusion. it is therefore necessary that member states do not overlook this problem. the eu budget must not continue to be drained of every euro. instead, we must ensure that investments are directed to the areas that need them most and where they will bring the greatest added value. the youth employment initiative can serve as an example in this respect. i do not want to tolerate any further widening of the gap between the inhabitants of the poorest and the richest regions, because in the long term this will only bring further instability to the european continent. the problem of european unemployment goes far deeper than just choosing the right investments from the european or national budgets. policies need to be properly coordinated not only in national negotiations but also at the highest european level. i would therefore like to see a joint meeting of the employment, social policy, health and consumer protection council and the economic and financial affairs council. breaking down the wall between these two formations can help create quality jobs and a fairer distribution of wealth.
i would like to thank rapporteur heinz becker and all the shadow rapporteurs for their really excellent cooperation. the negotiations on the final version of the report took quite a long time and i myself tabled over 100 amendments. we must also thank the luxembourg presidency, which has much to be thanked for finding a final agreement. the eures portal is now available, which responds to the current requirements of the labour market and can be an effective tool to promote employment and mobility. the main achievements are the extension of the portal to include positions for trainees and apprentices, or the inclusion of offers from private employers and private recruitment agencies. for many of us, the possibility of dreaming of working abroad, of choosing to work abroad, and of doing so from the comfort of our own home, was for many years completely out of reach and unimaginable. today, free movement of labour is one of the european union's greatest benefits, yet labour mobility in the eu is still ten times lower than in the united states. i believe that the new eures will be the right impetus to launch a new approach to work abroad for europeans, especially young people. i am convinced that the modernised eures portal is one of the right ways to remove barriers and address labour market problems across europe. we owe it to our young people.
i would like to thank mr becker in particular for his hard work on the eures report. the final text, which was supported by a large majority in the empl committee vote, clearly demonstrates that it is a sound text and deserves this support. i am also pleased that the amendments have been adopted, including the amendment i tabled in the sense of applicants who meet the requirements and criteria for authorisation so that the member state can issue the authorisation. so that there is no doubt that the authorisation can be issued. i am therefore very pleased with this clear definition in the report. i also welcome the fact that this labour market policy remains fully within the competence of the member states, that subsidiarity is respected and that, of course, the aim is to reduce bureaucracy and ensure good implementation. i therefore welcome the statement by the commissioner, who has promised to monitor implementation and report back. thank you all for your good work.
facilitating the mobility of workers within the european union can certainly be seen as a positive step that can effectively and flexibly address inequalities in the labour market. but there is a downside. unfortunately, with huge differences in wage levels between countries, there is an outflow of skilled workers from poorer european countries to richer ones. this is causing huge problems in some industries. i will take the health sector as an example, where countries that leave under better conditions have an acute shortage of health workers, and this directly threatens the availability of health care. public colleges provide education here, but graduates soon leave the country. is the solution for these countries to import health workers from even poorer parts of the world? is this a sustainable model of the european labour market? i guess not. this is not the problem of the eures network.
i would also like to point out that 1.1 million eu citizens are currently employed in crossborder work. also, 7 million eu citizens are employed in other eu member states. that's, i think, very substantial. i think that shows the values that need to be mentioned at this time, namely the freedom of establishment and the freedom to work guaranteed by the four fundamental freedoms of the eu. and so this also gives rise to a number of induced criteria that can be evaluated, and that is gdp growth. on the other hand, what mrs sehnall said is also true, namely that there is an outflow of qualified personnel. this is also something that member states have to deal with, and to some extent they have to fight this eu value in their legal systems. it is essential to me that eures has been reformed and reformed in a way that still further enforces greater participation of skilled labour in the labour market.

in writing. i supported today's report by the european parliament on the annual report on the activities of the european ombudsman for 2014, as i think that the overall conclusion of satisfaction with the activities of the european ombudsman can be agreed. the ombudsman plays an important role in the system of eu institutions, since eu citizens have a right to good administration, even vis-à-vis the institutions of the european union. the european ombudsman contributes to improving the performance of the administration at union level not only through his activities responding to citizens' complaints but also through his own-initiative inquiries addressing some of the most important issues in the area of good administration, such as access to documents, conflicts of interest or the transparency register. the usefulness of the european ombudsman can be documented by the example of the european citizens' initiative, where the ombudsman's office drew attention to the need to change some rules in order to make the initiative an effective and publicly accessible and understandable tool.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of approving the annual report for 2014 on the activities of the european ombudsman in 2014. the ombudsman plays a vital role in helping eu institutions become more open, effective and citizen-friendly, thus strengthening citizens’ confidence in the union. i particularly welcome the ombudsman’s push in 2014 for more transparency within the eu institutions, in lobbying and clinical trials, and for more citizen participation in eu decision-making. finally, i am also pleased that the ombudsman achieved concrete results in 2014, opening 325 inquiries on the basis of complaints as well as 17 own-initiative inquiries and closing 387 complaints-based inquiries as well as 13 own-initiative inquiries.

in writing. in the czech republic, the 'school milk' programme has been in operation since 1999. at present, some 3 100 schools, including nursery, primary and secondary schools, are involved in the programme. milk and milk products are supported partly by eu, partly by national resources and partly by the parents of the children involved in the programme. fruit and vegetables for schoolchildren is a younger project, running in the czech republic since 2010 (in the eu since 2007). from the outset, the project has included a training element, a national strategy has been developed and the possibility of financing accompanying measures is added. as regards the administrative burden, the suppliers, not the schools, apply for the aid, so that the administrative and organisational burden on the schools is minimal. i am very supportive of both projects and consider them important, especially from the point of view of the children's eating habits. however, i do not agree with the adaptation of the school fruit and milk programmes at eu level. i believe that this is a matter of national competence and that the principle of subsidiarity should be respected. i see no reason for this issue to be decided at european level.

in writing. - i voted against it. the hicp is inherently inaccurate because each country has a different culture, a different level of income and therefore a different structure of household expenditure. harmonised indices thus always give a distorted picture of price developments. constant changes in the methodology reduce the comparability of the price level over time. the new generation requirements will put a burden on both the national statistical authorities and the eu budget.
in writing. i supported the report on harmonised indices of consumer prices (hisc) and house prices (icbn) at union, national and sub-national level. the hisc provides a measure of inflation, which is used inter alia for wages, rent, interest rates and thus forms the basis for economic and monetary policy decisions. it is therefore essential that those statistics are objective, error-free and comparable across all member states and product areas. i agree that member states will not be required to produce or provide sub-indices of the hicp whose weight represents less than one percentile of the total expenditure included in the hicp. given the importance of the implementation of monetary policy, i consider it useful for euro area member states to submit flash hicp estimates at monthly intervals.
in writing. ‒ statistical data are of vital importance in the formulation of any policy. the economy is no exception. that is why i supported the report on harmonised consumer price indices to measure inflation. it is necessary to establish a common framework for the development, production and dissemination of harmonised indices at union and national level and to complement them with any other relevant indicators, including better integration of house price indices. as we have seen over the past few years, it is highly desirable that information, even if provisional, be provided in good time and that it is possible to make flash estimates of the evolution of price stability. it is therefore more than logical that the commission should adopt measures to allow it to consider possible changes in the collection of this relevant information.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of gender mainstreaming in the work of the european parliament, as i believe it is an essential step towards achieving real equality between men and women. this report has the ambition of integrating a gender perspective into the content of the laws and promoting gender equality in the administration and the decision-making process surrounding the law. while i believe that the european parliament should set an example for other european and national institutions to follow, i decided to vote against the creation of a post of standing rapporteur on gender mainstreaming as i do not see the added value and it would create more bureaucracy.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report because i believe there has to be special attention paid to women refugees, especially those fleeing their countries of origin together with their children, as they are more vulnerable and they face many challenges throughout their very risky journey. it has to be said that cases of physical violence, abuse or other forms of discrimination were registered. our goal should be to point out such cases and make sure women refugees get the appropriate level of protection they need. on the other hand, i could not support some of the proposals of the rapporteur concerning reserves on lack of solidarity between the member states when it comes to their approach to refugees and asylum seekers. those statements are not objective, fact-based and, above all, are not within the scope of the report. also, i do not fully share the report’s call for full access of asylum seekers to public services with regard to education or employment services during the asylum process. these should be granted, but only to those whose asylum procedure has been concluded successfully.
in writing. ‒ although i do not support the eu’s general approach towards the refugee crisis, i voted in favour of this report. this report calls for the new eu migration and asylum policies and procedures to include gender-sensitive measures to ensure the safety of women seeking asylum, many of whom travel with young children. the text rightly highlights the vulnerable situation women refugees are facing. these women often fled gendered forms of persecution – including rape, sexual violence, female genital mutilation, forced marriage in their country of origin, undertaking a perilous journey during which they may be victims of sexual violence, trafficking or other violent crimes. concretely, the report calls for member states to ensure women’s and children’s specific needs are met throughout the asylum process and in reception centres.

madam president, i speak as chairman of the committee on legal affairs, whose remit includes improving the drafting of legislation. it's certainly a positive thing that we now have a new agreement. however, the european parliament has already expressed certain views on this matter in the past, which were only partially incorporated in the final text. so a few notes on a few aspects. firstly, impact assessment is an important tool for assessing the quality of legislation. such assessment shall include ensuring that the new rules do not create an excessive administrative burden for their users. the independence of impact assessments remains one of our highest priorities, which has not yet been fully achieved. secondly, the new agreement requires further follow-up to, for example, delegated and implementing acts. only then will the deal be complete. finally, we must also monitor the implementation of the agreement as a whole, because only then will we have a truly functional instrument that fulfils its role. the committee on legal affairs will therefore, together with the committee on constitutional affairs, monitor the interpretation and implementation of the new agreement, both through own-initiative reports and through a joint working group.

mr president, i admit that this vote was not easy for me, nor for many of my colleagues. i'm not a big fan of the european union talking into criminal justice policy. on the other hand, the positive aspects of the proposal that i have mentioned outweigh certain reservations i have about the scope of the directive, such as the guaranteed rights. and that is why i have finally decided to support this draft report. it's important to me that this ensures a basic equality of arms for children, which is balanced by their young age. that the safeguards that are being put in place are precisely to balance the way in which they can and cannot proceed in this criminal proceeding. and it is a fact that the extension to 21 years is not the happiest, on the other hand, czech criminal law also knows the concept of the age of near-teenagers, so in this sense too i finally decided to support this report.
in writing. ‒ this regulation is particularly important precisely because it is aimed at the most vulnerable in our society children. i agree that children under investigation for criminal offences (or suspected of committing them) should be given a fair trial. due to their young age and immaturity, they are more vulnerable during criminal proceedings, and i therefore support the idea of unifying procedural rights in this matter and overlapping standards of child protection. children need to be treated with dignity and fairness. i consider the right to information to be absolutely essential, and i also welcome the right to legal aid, the presence of legal representation during proceedings or the protection of privacy.
in writing. children who are suspects or accused persons in criminal proceedings are at a very vulnerable age when they can easily turn to the wrong path. therefore, special attention must be paid to them in order to preserve their inherent development potential and subsequently to promote their reintegration into society. the directive aims to introduce procedural safeguards to ensure that children, that is to say persons under the age of 18, who are suspects or accused persons in criminal proceedings, are able to understand and observe those proceedings and to exercise their right to a fair trial, and to prevent children from re-offending and to promote their social integration. this objective is indicative enough that the establishment of common minimum rules for the protection of procedural rights of suspected or accused children should strengthen the confidence of member states in the criminal justice systems of other member states and thus improve mutual recognition of decisions in criminal matters. each child who is a suspect or accused person in criminal proceedings should have the right to an individual assessment aimed at identifying their specific needs, as set out in article 7 of this directive. it is also essential that member states ensure that children are adequately informed about the rights set out in this directive.
in writing. - i got held up. i understand the requirement that persons under 18 accused of crimes be treated with care, sensitivity and with regard to their age, maturity and intellectual capacity, and that they should take into account the communication difficulties of the children. i also agree that 'criminal proceedings concerning children should be conducted in a way that does not intimidate children and that is sensitive to them.' on the other hand, i do not want the eu to impose on member states how they should treat juvenile defendants.
in writing. ‒ i am convinced that, in line with european tradition, children and young people should be entitled to greater legal protection in criminal proceedings, taking into account their vulnerability and lower degree of maturity. in particular, i welcome the amendment to the right to privacy, which requires member states to ensure that court proceedings involving children are normally closed to the public or to allow courts or judges to decide whether such proceedings are closed to the public. i have a reservation about the provision adopted whereby member states, with full regard for freedom of expression and information and freedom and pluralism of the media, invite the media to adopt self-regulatory measures in order to achieve the objectives of protecting the privacy of children. first, it is a provision which is not enforceable by law. in addition, the call for self-regulatory measures falls short of the level of legal protection, for example in the czech republic, where there is a direct ban on the publication of the names and surnames of juveniles in criminal proceedings and information leading to their identification.
in writing. ‒ more than one million children in the european union face criminal charges every year. that's 12% of the total number of criminal justice procedures. it should be noted that a child is considered in this context to be any individual under the age of 18. the proposed directive aims to set minimum common standards for the rights and treatment of children who are prosecuted or accused. common rules should include the right to be represented by a lawyer during all interrogations, which should be simultaneously recorded in such cases. alternatives to detention should always be preferred, and if detention is necessary for any reason, due care and consideration must be guaranteed. i don't want to advocate for perpetrators of any age, but there are many, many cases where a criminal act is committed by a child who is being abused, or in self-defense. we need to keep that in mind and guarantee them a fair and dignified treatment by the law. i think the directive is a good one and will result in regulating the disproportionate psychological burden on these children.
in writing. i supported the report on the first reading of the draft directive which aims to establish a minimum standard of rights for children accused or suspected of criminal offences. the legal regulation of this issue varies from one member state to another, some states have a specialised court, others do not, the training requirements for those involved in child proceedings vary, and i could go on. the harmonisation of rules is important for strengthening trust between states in cross-border judicial cooperation. the directive ensures in particular the right of the child to information relevant to the exercise of other rights , to a fair defence, to the protection of privacy, to the protection of personal liberty, to a timely and proper hearing, and so on. i consider the emphasis on the protection of children's privacy or on the minimal use of the institution of detention to be crucial, as this limits the risks of excluding children from society by the conduct itself. the proposed amendment also develops cross-border procedural rules in relation to the european arrest warrant. in the czech republic, there are already a number of procedural safeguards for children in criminal proceedings, but the directive develops, for example, the rights of the holder of parental responsibility or puts more emphasis on the individual assessment of the case. i believe that the specific contribution to czech law will be the mandatory training of lawyers who will defend children in communication with children and in child psychology.
in writing. i supported the proposal for a directive on procedural safeguards for children who are suspects or accused persons in criminal proceedings. the european commission estimates that more than one million children are exposed to criminal proceedings in the eu every year. they are significantly disadvantaged by their young age and therefore need to be guaranteed procedural rights reflecting their specific needs in criminal proceedings. to date, only a few member states have specific legislation on the criminal proceedings against children, and it is often fragmented. a set of minimum standards, which would be accompanied and adapted to the specific requirements of the children throughout the procedure, seems to be the appropriate solution. i welcome the introduction of a single list of procedural rights throughout the eu and have therefore voted in favour of this proposal containing it. in particular, these include the right to the mandatory assistance of a lawyer, the right to information for parents or other designated persons, the right to be accompanied during criminal proceedings or the possibility for the court to decide that the proceedings are not public.
in writing. ‒ 1 million children undergo criminal proceedings every year, which is 12% of all offenders. this is why i believe it to be fundamental that we agree on minimum and equal standards to guarantee that every child receives a fair trial, as standards currently vary enormously. this will also prevent children from reoffending and enable them to reintegrate into society more easily. although member states have already signed the charter of fundamental rights of the european union and other international conventions protecting children’s rights, experience has shown that, at present, children’s rights are not being sufficiently protected at the various stages in criminal proceedings. the czech republic is one of only 6 member states to have a dedicated juvenile prosecution service.

in writing. in the context of this report, i would like to recall that in the budgets for 2015 and 2016, the commission has in many cases not requested additional payment appropriations for a number of its crisis responses (eur 2 billion for greece, first migration initiatives) and instead has resorted to reallocating already existing resources. this has increased the pressure on payment appropriations in 2016 and beyond, potentially leading to a situation where there may again be insufficient funds to cover the actual needs of financial programmes across the different headings, with a direct impact on projects and citizens. there is thus a legitimate concern that, in addition to the delayed start of implementation of the 2014-2020 programmes, the situation at the end of the last mff is likely to be repeated in the form of an unprecedented level of outstanding commitments and an unsustainable accumulation of pending payment applications. it is therefore appropriate to consider whether unforeseen payment needs should not be covered by new appropriations.
