in writing. ‒ i supported the report on veterinary medicines, which improves the existing legislation and creates conditions for better veterinary care. i consider it an important element in the fight against antibacterial resistance, which is a growing concern for farmers and breeders. i consider it correct that the prescription of a veterinary medicinal product is subject to the establishment of a veterinary diagnosis on the basis of a clinical examination of the animal and that continuous medical surveillance is not sufficient.
in writing. ‒ healthy animals are an essential prerequisite for europe’s agriculture, public health and environment. however, veterinary products have been difficult to access in small markets, their use plagued by heavy and sometimes unnecessary administration and there has been worrying resistance to antibiotics. in addition, medicine for animals and humans has been put into the same category, which is very confusing. i believe that the commission’s proposal is an important step forward to remedy to this, which is why i voted in favour of it. it provides a good balance between consumer needs by improving access to medicinal products, simplifying administration while simultaneously providing incentives for the veterinary industry to encourage innovation, which is needed in this small and quite fragmented market. it will also work on ensuring a functioning internal market. more importantly, it will tackle the growing antibiotic resistance by limiting the use of antibiotics, but also by allowing the use of homeopathic alternatives, and by defining who is entitled to prescribe veterinary medicine.
in writing. i supported the report amending the draft regulation on veterinary medicinal products (vmp) at first reading. the proposed regulation replaces the existing union regulation on veterinary medicinal products, which is contained in directive 2001/82/ec and regulation (ec) no 726/2004, and responds to criticism of the existing regulation by the pharmaceutical industry, farmers and veterinarians. union regulation of this issue is necessary to ensure a high level of protection of human and animal health and the environment, as well as for the functioning of the internal market. the proposed regulation contains a new regulation on the marketing authorisation of medicinal products, aiming to reduce the administrative burden associated with the authorisation. the regulation also addresses a key and topical issue, namely the effort to limit the rise of antimicrobial resistance. the control of antibiotic use in veterinary medicine is particularly important, as overuse of antibiotics also negatively affects their effectiveness in treating humans. the new regulation promotes research into new products, for example by extending the term of protection of technical documentation, which makes the investment in the development of vlp more profitable. the regulation also includes modifications to the rules for the production and distribution of vlps, the rules for regulatory authorities and the revision of the so-called pharmacovigilance , i.e. post-registration monitoring of vlps , which is intended to serve, for example, as a single database for all registered vlps in the eu.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of amending the regulation on the european medicine agency (ema), to make sure that it is capable of effectively implementing new regulations and ensuring that all medicines available on the eu market are safe, effective and of high quality. while the authorisation for veterinary medicinal products is now part of a new regulation, this amendment clarifies that the ema is still responsible for the central authorisation procedure for human and the veterinary products, that it is line with the new financial regulations, and that it has a role to play in increasing access to medicine. increasing cooperation and exchange of scientific information with the agency for health technology assessment bodies will be useful for the latter. i particularly agree with the idea that ema should be also able to provide member states with a comparative evaluation of medicinal products for humans, which can then be taken into consideration on a voluntary basis.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this resolution because i believe that a strong european role in the data-driven economy will be vital to our economic growth in the future. while we must always support the right to privacy by default, there are real opportunities for europe if we are active in the development of big data, cloud computing, connected vehicles, and the internet of things. a data-driven economy can make our cities cleaner, help bring smart solutions to real problems and create new jobs. in short, a connected world will be an important part of making life better and easier for our citizens and i hope we will not let this chance slip by.

in writing. - in the context of this resolution, i find it alarming that only 1.7% of enterprises are making full use of advanced digital technologies, despite the benefits that digital tools can bring to all economic sectors. it is therefore urgent that the commission and the member states put in place a digital strategy targeting business operators. the european digital economy hubs should also be established to address the use of big data and other data technologies by entrepreneurs, smes and innovative companies, and to include researchers and the wider economy. the establishment of innovation spaces and clusters should be promoted to help develop skills and create competitive advantage in the area of intellectual capital and to better understand the prospects and limitations of big data technology.
in writing. i supported the report on the data-driven economy, as data, as an integral part of our lives, can bring new opportunities for growth and employment. i also supported the report because of the benefits of data for consumers, government, medicine and crime prevention. i am aware that the use of data carries significant risks, and therefore the building of a digital single market cannot be done without adequate data protection. this should be ensured by a uniform legal framework. a data-driven economy can lead to greater prosperity, economic growth, research and innovation. but it is equally important for the european commission and the member states to remember that it is the promotion of research and innovation that is essential to building a data-driven economy. i therefore voted in favour of using european and national funding to strengthen european research and innovation in this area.
in writing. ‒ as a member of the committee on regional development, i am in favour of increasing employment by all possible means. in the context of the current work programme of the european commission, the digital single market is a key objective that can make the future thriving data-driven economy an opportunity for jobs and growth, inter alia by enabling the emergence of new business models and services. on our common journey towards a thriving economy, the data-driven economy represents a future that requires, in addition to connectivity, common standards, high-speed networks and equally powerful computing infrastructures. i am in favour of the european union's member states making more use of big data and being financially supported by the union, as well as the council supporting the creation of uniform electronic identification rules. i think that decisions that are based on big data can contribute to productivity and competitiveness, which ultimately contribute to gdp growth in the european union member states.
in writing. the resolution on the road to a thriving data-driven economy is, in my view, a balanced contribution to the issue of big data, which has the potential to increase economic productivity and improve consumer and public services. already, big data is enabling consumers to benefit from certain services that increase convenience, efficiency and savings, for example in transport. i think it is important that the resolution recognises the potential opportunities for the development of a data-driven economy, but also points out that the development of these opportunities must be conditional on preserving trust and confidence and on the effective enforcement of consumer rights. that's why i voted for the resolution.
in writing. ‒ big data represents an immense opportunity to both our businesses and our societies, which is why i voted in favour of this resolution. by making use of the economy of scale, big data will be able to significantly improve productivity and encourage new and innovative business models and services. big data and the economy of scale will be particularly beneficial for smes, who will be more apt to compete with big businesses. i am also hopeful that this will create a significant number of new jobs in europe in the coming years, as the use of big data requires many new advanced skills. in that sense, raising awareness and providing widespread training to deal with big data and new technologies is crucial. moreover, big data can also be a big step for improving the way we live (smart cities), the quality of our science and medicine (mhealth), and for preventing disasters and fighting crime more effectively. moreover, it will bring new opportunities for consumers in terms of convenience, efficiency and savings, and can allow government administrations to work more efficiently and closer to citizens through e-government.
in writing. i supported this resolution because it is the future thriving data-driven economy that can be an opportunity for economic growth and higher employment in the union as well as for increasing its external competitiveness. i also agree that in this area, all the principles laid down by the european union's data protection legislation, such as fairness and lawfulness, purpose limitation, legal basis for processing, must be respected when processing personal data. i also support the initiative mentioned in the resolution concerning the call to the commission and the member states to set up european digital economy centres to deal with the use of big data by entrepreneurs and smes. the development of a data-driven economy also needs to be accompanied by better ict education, not only in schools but also in lifelong learning.

in writing. ‒ the economic crisis that hit europe in 2008 led not only to a catastrophic loss of jobs, but also to a major loss of confidence in the market and our national banking institutions. in response, we created the banking union, which has been indispensable in restoring stability and confidence in euro area banks, strengthening our monetary union, and above all leading to market confidence, boosting jobs and investment. while, eight years later, our recovery remains modest and the risks high, the banking union remains the best instrument to put the european economy on the right path again. this is why i voted in favour of the banking union’s 2015 report. i particularly welcome the creation of the single supervisory mechanism (ssm), which aims to ensure a uniform and homogeneous supervision of european banks, creating a level playing field in the banking market, and contributing to its safety and soundness, while endorsing the idea that the administrative burdens caused by this instrument must be kept to a minimum.

in writing. i supported the report by the european parliament amending the proposal for a regulation on zootechnical and genealogical conditions for trade in and imports into the eu of breeding animals and their germinal products. this regulation aims to promote a free internal market, simplify import conditions, while maintaining the level and quality of breeding programmes in the eu and protecting european biodiversity. the draft regulation maintains the existing main and well-functioning rules of eu zootechnical legislation. the amendment consists in creating a single legal framework which guarantees the same principles for the recognition of breed societies and societies, the approval of their breeding programmes, furthermore it establishes the same criteria for official controls and clearly defines the relationship between breeders and breed societies. the regulation also harmonises terminology and introduces new definitions of 'breed' and 'breeding programme'. i consider it important that this draft regulation is based on regular consultations with experts and responds to differences in the implementation of the basic directives in the various member states, which are brought to the attention of the member states themselves during the regular meetings of the standing committee on zootechnology with the commission.

in writing. ‒ more than 20 years after its creation, the single market is still fragmented. it is high time to move towards a fully-fledged single market based on the principle of shared responsibility, which is why i voted in favour of this regulation. a functioning single market will benefit european citizens by stimulating competitiveness, job creation, growth and sme development, while delivering a high level of consumer protection. an important aspect is to ensure that policies are decided at the most appropriate level, be it local, regional, national or european. legislation needs to be effective, efficient, and its impact should be assessed before, after and during the time it becomes law. we should also avoid unnecessary regulation and administrative burden. stakeholders should be consulted on a regular, transparent and open basis when drafting laws. moreover, we need to ensure proper implementation of this legislation, which remains one of our weak spots.
in writing. i decided to support the european parliament's report entitled 'towards better regulation of the single market' because i believe that good legislation, including market regulation, is good for the citizens of the european union, because it boosts competitiveness, leads to the creation of new jobs and promotes economic growth and the development of small and medium-sized enterprises. i am sure that these regulations also guarantee a high level of consumer protection. i also consider it crucial that the principle of subsidiarity is the starting point for the formulation of regulatory policy. in this respect, i consider it important that the principle of proportionality should also be taken into account when the relevant legislation is being prepared. the main objective of regulation, then, in my view, should be to achieve maximum simplicity, transparency and coherence.

in writing. i supported the release of the european globalisation adjustment fund for the kingdom of sweden. in this member state, there has been a massive redundancy of employees who will have to be reintegrated into the local labour market. the production and export of heavy goods vehicles and commercial vehicles in the european union has been replaced by production in asia. this is evidenced by statistics confirming a european decline of up to 10% and, conversely, an upward trend in asian markets. the critical situation in vehicle manufacturing in europe is further confirmed by the fact that 22 applications for assistance from the european globalisation adjustment fund have already been submitted. sweden has fulfilled all the necessary formal criteria to qualify for the necessary aid of approximately eur 1,8 million. the aid from the european union should in this particular case optimally complement the measures taken by the swedish authorities after the redundancies in 2015 to support the return of the dismissed workers to an optimal supply and demand situation on the labour market.

in writing. ‒ on wednesday 13 april, we voted on our objection to the renewal of the approval of the herbicide glyphosate for use in the eu. first of all, i have to say that i'm very disappointed with the overall outcome of the vote. having to vote against your text is never a pleasant experience. our objection was distorted by right-wing factions who proposed amendments to weaken the total ban on glyphosate in the eu. and unfortunately, they were able to accept it. the amendment finally succeeded, calling on the commission to renew the authorisation of glyphosate for a further 7 years without further evaluation. this is a blank check for the commission from the original text, which was supposed to say no to the use of glyphosate in the eu, in the sense that if you allow its use for 7 years, we don't care what the basis is. the only consolation is that the proposal calls on the commission to restrict the use of this substance to professionals. glyphosate is carcinogenic to both animals and probably to humans and its authorisation should not, in my view, be renewed in any way. this is a disgusting gamble on the health of european citizens. it is also completely against the will of more than two-thirds of the citizens of the european union. since the text adopted has completely lost its original meaning, i was obliged to vote against this proposal.
in writing. i voted against it. in voting against the objection raised by the environment committee, i de facto supported the decision of the european commission to renew the authorisation for the chemical glyphosate. the chemical glyphosate is commonly used in horticulture and agriculture to control pests. the substance has no proven unquestionable adverse effects on human health and i am in favour of its continued use and its effects on human health being further investigated.
in writing. there's been a heated debate in europe for months about glyphosate. this herbicide is used not only to kill weeds but also to dry out, for example, beets, corn, sunflowers, grains, and other crops before harvest. research from 2013 showed that up to 60% of the population of the czech republic has glyphosate in their urine. so we have to take scientific studies that show that this substance is probably carcinogenic very seriously. the objection, which was approved by the european parliament this week, will have the effect of stopping the use of glyphosate-containing products near public playgrounds and parks or in gardens and orchards. the authorisation for its use will then have to be renewed every seven years, as opposed to the original 15 years proposed by the commission. but it's certainly not a massive success, because the changes are not enough. i would of course like to see substances like glyphosate, which raise more than legitimate concerns for the health of european union citizens, simply withdrawn from the market. the amendments tabled by the ppe group in particular have failed to make some of the original proposals stick and i can only speculate whether the softening of the original text by the ppe was not the result of persuasion by the agrotechnical giant monsanto, whose flagship product roundup contains this most widespread pesticide. but as social democrats, we must not abandon the battlefield when it comes to the health of our citizens.
in writing. i supported the european parliament's resolution on glyphosate as amended by my ppe group's proposals. we know that in the past year, the safety of glyphosate, used primarily for herbicides, has been investigated by both the international agency for research on cancer and the european food safety authority. these institutions have reached different conclusions and therefore this matter needs to be addressed, also in the light of the precautionary principle. it should also be noted that the european food safety authority, which found no danger to human health in glyphosate, submitted its conclusions to a public debate, with the contribution of experts from eu countries. in view of the above circumstances and also taking into account the opinion of the czech ministry of agriculture, i consider it correct to adopt a compromise solution, i.e. not to ban glyphosate completely, but to keep its use more under control as a precaution. the european parliament proposes to restrict the use of glyphosate to professionals who should be provided with the necessary information and to place strict restrictions on its use immediately before harvest. i also voted to reduce the time that glyphosate should be allowed to be extended to seven years.

in writing. on the 13th, we voted on the motion for a resolution on the zika virus epidemic. as a co-author of the adopted text, i was able to contribute to its drafting from the very beginning. in discussing the proposal, i relied on information provided to me by the european centre for disease prevention and control (ecdc) as the european parliament's contact person. sadly, it is becoming almost a rule that we encounter a new, terrible epidemic of some virus every year or so. last year it was ebola, today it's zika. contrary to initial reports of this virus, today we are learning the shocking truth that zika is an even bigger problem than initially thought. in addition to severe developmental disorders, such as brain or head stunted growth (microcephaly), the virus is also thought to cause other brain disorders and damage. i'm glad the bill welcomes a greater release of resources to study this virus and its effects on the human body. we need to find out as quickly as possible what exactly causes zika and how to successfully fight it. the text also included a call for further investigation of the effects of the pesticide pyriproxifen on the virus and its link to microcephaly. i'm very glad that we were able to come up with a balanced text that i could finally support.
in writing. i supported the resolution which, in the context of the zika virus epidemic, points to weaknesses both in the response of public health systems, especially at the primary care level, and in the provision of reproductive health services and the rights of women and girls in affected countries, especially with regard to information and care during and after pregnancy termination. simply recommending that a pregnancy be postponed until more is known about zika is not an adequate and satisfactory response. given that there is currently no prevention, treatment or vaccine to protect against this viral infection and that there may be a risk of local transmission in europe during the summer season of 2016, the commission should rapidly carry out an analysis of insecticides with regard to human health and efficacy against mosquitoes vectors of the infection.
in writing. i support the adoption of a report to propose preventive measures to prevent the spread of the zika virus. on 1 february 2016, the world health organisation designated the zika virus epidemic as a public health emergency of international concern. zika virus has been reported sporadically in the past in two european regions, martinique and french guiana. later, it appeared outside its native range, leading to an outbreak in micronesia and, a few years later, in french polynesia. in addition, it has been discovered that this virus can cause neurological diseases. although no case of transmission of this disease has been reported on the european continent, adequate precautions must be taken to prevent the spread of the virus. the need for prevention and adequate resources to combat this virus is particularly important given the possible link between zika virus infection in pregnant women and the increase in microcephaly. unfortunately, there is no specific treatment for microcephaly or zika virus, and there is a particular need to raise awareness among citizens and experts on how to protect themselves from infection. in the context of this report, i also welcomed the commission's decision to allocate eur 10 million for zika virus research.
in writing. ‒ i supported the resolution which stressed the need for zika virus research and the need for rapid diagnosis, treatment and vaccination. the zika virus epidemic is a global health threat and measures must be taken to stop it. its effects are made all the more serious by the fact that it affects primarily pregnant women and newborns. last but not least, it also highlights the seriousness of the problem of complex access to contraception in the least developed areas of the world.
in writing. ‒ the european parliament's motion for a resolution, which draws attention to the current and serious problem of the zika virus epidemic, has been ideologically abused. i couldn't support him after all. the resolution focuses on scientific research, its promotion and coordination. intensive development of vaccines and drugs is necessary, and research should also help to identify zika virus more clearly from other diseases based on symptoms, and also to clarify why a virus first reported in humans as early as 1952 has now emerged as an epidemic of this magnitude. the resolution calls on the commission to consider increasing the amount to be allocated to the fight against zika virus. even in a rough comparison, €10 million seems insufficient to the billions of dollars that are to be released in the us to fight the virus. the proposal also targets practical issues such as disinfection on the way from infected countries and public awareness. on all these points, the resolution has my clear support. however, amendments were voted on in the resolution, which i do not agree with. the resolution, in its final form, also contained generalizations in favor of abortion. it is not the first time that these amendments have devalued resolutions, and this practice has a negative impact on the outcomes of the european parliament. the resolution as it was finally adopted was therefore adopted without my support.

in writing. ‒ the new eu data protection rules will meld different legal approaches in eu member states into one single european rulebook and will give people back control of their personal information. citizens will be able to decide which of their personal information they want to share. the new regulation includes, among other things, provisions on the right to be forgotten, the ‘clear and affirmative consent’ to the processing of private data by the person concerned, the right to transfer your data to another service provider and the right to know when your data has been hacked. the data protection package also includes a directive on data transfers for policing and judicial purposes which will help authorities transfer valuable personal data efficiently while respecting the fundamental right to privacy.

in writing. the proposed passenger name record (pnr) directive requires the systematic collection, use and retention of data such as contact details, flight dates and timetables or credit card details used for the payment of air tickets, for passengers on flights crossing eu borders. the use of such data should help the security services in the fight against terrorism and other criminal activities, as it would facilitate the identification of potential suspects. i supported this proposal because it is an important tool in the fight against terrorism and organised crime. i consider the report to be balanced with the right of eu citizens to privacy and i also believe that the passenger name record directive is in line with the european court of justice's decision on the data retention directive. i voted against the part concerning the mandatory transfer of data between states because i believe that this sharing should remain on a voluntary basis.

in writing. the unprecedented rise in terrorist attacks in europe has opened a long-running debate on so-called passenger name records. the new directive should ensure that data may only be processed for the purposes of the prevention, detection, investigation or prosecution of terrorism and other serious criminal offences. to prevent any misuse of personal data, all data will be stored for the first six months and then anonymised for a further four and a half years, with very strict rules for access. a clear system for exchanging data between member states and, in particular, strong safeguards for the protection of personal data will also be put in place. it is precisely the concerns about the lack of protection and misuse of passengers' personal data that have blocked this directive from being adopted by parliament in the last few years. the commission has now succeeded in making the vote on the data protection package a joint one. i believe that this directive is an important step towards better protecting all eu citizens and that, thanks to the strong security, sensitive data will not be leaked. the single system advocated by the european parliament should ensure that 28 different registers do not arise, which would not be able to communicate adequately with each other, would be incompatible and, consequently, would not be effective in ensuring security.

in writing. ‒ trade secrets and confidential business information are at the core of the competitiveness of any company. today, one company out of every five is a victim of theft of trade secrets every year. difficulties with getting redress against misappropriation of trade secrets need to be addressed. thanks to this directive, trade secrets will share a common definition and same level of protection across all 28 eu member states. this text will allow the creation of a safe, trustworthy and fair environment for european companies, by better securing their know-how while protecting whistle-blowers and journalists’ work. indeed, for the first time, the protection of whistle-blowers is explicitly mentioned in an eu piece of legislation. this is, i hope, a first step towards a european framework for the protection of whistle-blowers.
in writing. i abstained on the final draft because, in its final form, it provides companies with inadequate protection and allows them to sue anyone who uses or discloses information they consider to be trade secrets. this definition is so broad in the draft directive that it covers almost all inside information. the penalty for disclosing such a broadly understood trade secret is high. exceptions for certain groups of persons (employees, journalists, scientists, consumers and whistleblowers) do not ensure sufficient protection. in my view, this directive threatens, inter alia, the ability of journalists to publish information on unfair business practices and the ability of employees to use all their work experience to build their careers.
in writing. ‒ today we voted on a proposal for a directive harmonising trade secret legislation across the eu member states. however, the commission was not able to convince me of the need for such an adjustment, for several reasons at the outset. firstly, it was based on a public consultation, but only 386 respondents participated, which is not a particularly high number in the context of the eu as a whole. the experience of experts in this field, including those from the czech republic, has shown that member states can regulate civil law satisfactorily on their own without creating significant obstacles to the functioning of the internal market, and that compliance with the subsidiarity principle can therefore be contested to a minimum. moreover, no major problem with the existing legislation has been identified so far, including that differences in member states' legal systems would constitute a major obstacle to cross-border investment in this area. i also find a number of risks in the proposal such as insufficient protection of journalists' access to information, rather negligible protection of staff mobility, whereby employees may be prevented by their employer from finding work in the same field with another employer for up to 6 years after the end of their employment relationship, and in particular minimal or no protection for whistleblowers. i could not therefore vote for the current version of the draft directive and supported the rejected amendment.
in writing. i supported the proposal for a directive aimed at providing businesses with an adequate level of protection and effective remedies where their trade secrets have been stolen or misused. the protection of trade secrets is particularly important for small, less established businesses, which are much more dependent on trade secrets than larger companies, in part because of the cost of obtaining a patent and protection against misuse. the loss of trade secrets and the possibility of competitive access to key inventions thus represents a huge economic risk for smes. the available data confirm that a new higher level of legal protection is badly needed. a recent commission survey found that in the last ten years, one in five companies has been the victim of at least one attempted theft of a trade secret. according to another study, this number is even increasing: in 2013, 25% of companies reported information theft, compared to 18% in 2012.
‒ although europe is a leader in science and innovation, it lags behind other trading partners such as japan or the us in terms of business engagement in these sectors. as a member of the committee on industry, research and energy, i very much welcome and support the proposal for this directive, which is also part of the wider europe 2020 strategy in which the commission has committed itself to creating an innovation union. this directive is a further step towards creating a better environment for innovation by enterprises and a more favourable environment for new projects. the need to adopt this directive arises from differences in the protection of business secrets between member states. in particular, major shortcomings are found in the definition of a trade secret and the specification of when it is to be protected. many member states also lack rules seeking to protect trade secrets during legal proceedings, which discourages the injured party from seeking redress in court. i therefore see this proposal as a major contribution to addressing these shortcomings at eu level. i would like to emphasise that not only i but the whole s&d group have been strictly vigilant to ensure that whistleblowers and journalists are not violated, as they are clearly excluded from the scope of this law.
in writing. i consider the protection of undisclosed know-how and business information to be an unquestionable right of all kinds of businesses, non-profit research organisations and other communities that invest considerable funds in the acquisition, development and use of such knowledge, and thus the inviolability of business secrets should be guaranteed at the level of protection of private property. at the same time, it is worth noting the introduction of legislation addressing this issue. at a time when we are focusing on promoting sustainable development, poverty reduction, small and medium-sized enterprises, the private sector and its interaction with the public sector, it is necessary to highlight the importance of the protection of trade secrets, as this provides a clear competitive advantage to the holders of such information and breach of this protection would seriously undermine their economy. the protection of trade secrets should be actively addressed at member state level in order to create a high-quality and favourable environment for trade, business, science, research and investment in other sectors in all countries of the european union.
in writing. ‒ the establishment of european protection of trade secrets has worried many european union citizens since its adoption last week. the aim of this law is to shield innovative companies against corporate espionage, by protecting their know-how and business information. this is particularly important for smes and start-ups, especially in the digital sector, as they have been suffering most from these unlawful activities and do not necessarily have the financial resources to patent their work or use other intellectual rights. parliament also amended the text initially proposed by the commission to make sure that our fundamental freedoms, such as freedom of the press and of information, the media’s liberty and pluralism, as well as investigative journalism continue being guaranteed. moreover, this is the first time that the protection of whistle-blowers has been included in a legislative text at eu level.

in writing. i supported this report, which is much more critical of turkey than in previous years. it points to the continuing problems in respecting fundamental freedoms, freedom of expression, with journalists and academics still imprisoned for their opinions, freedom of assembly, the halting of the peace process with the kurdish minority and the increase in violence in the south-east of the country. i also welcome the fact that the report clearly separates turkey's position in the current refugee crisis settlement from the accession process, which has been underway since 2005. turkey must be made to understand that the eu will not compromise on its criteria, even though its negotiating position may seem more advantageous in the current context.
in writing. - i support the adoption of this annual report on turkey, which focuses on the current state of eu-turkey relations and the internal situation in the country. however, i find it very worrying that turkey, as a candidate country, is not making greater efforts to improve its respect for democracy and the rule of law, despite its declared efforts to open new chapters in the accession negotiations. i find turkey's approach to freedom of expression particularly unacceptable, given the still high number of imprisoned journalists, but also the gradual nationalization of the media and the censorship of the internet. the growing rate of corruption is also a matter of great concern to transparency international. in this context, it is necessary for turkey to adopt the necessary reforms in the areas of fundamental rights, justice, freedom and security. however, i also recognise that turkey is our strategic partner, particularly in the light of the refugee crisis, and that we need to cooperate with it in this area. however, i would like to stress that cooperation in tackling the migration crisis cannot have the effect of any relaxation or reduction of requirements in the negotiations on turkey's accession to the eu or on visa-free travel. other issues of common interest also include the fight against terrorism, the economy, trade and energy. it is therefore necessary to continue to strengthen good neighbourly relations and to intensify structured political dialogues.

in writing. i have today endorsed the 2015 report on turkey, as i believe it is overall balanced and criticizes what is criticizable and appreciates what is appreciated. the report condemns the discrimination and prosecution of journalists or academics who have publicly criticised the actions of the turkish president, highlights the possible use of terrorism to violate civil liberties and rights, and the need for further reforms in the justice sector. the report commends turkey's actions to help alleviate the migration crisis in greece and the assistance provided by turkey to refugees on its territory. as regards visa liberalisation, it is stated that the introduction of visa-free travel is possible only if the conditions previously laid down are fulfilled. that, i believe, is the appropriate attitude.

in writing. ‒ i have decided not to agree with the european parliament's report on turkey. i am aware of the fact that turkey is a strategic partner for the eu, but i am personally deeply concerned about the very slow pace of reforms and the decline in the level of respect for democracy and the rule of law. i see the problem as the questionable independence of the judiciary, the threatened freedom of assembly and expression, or the respect for human rights and the rule of law. turkey is thus steadily moving away from the copenhagen criteria. last but not least, i am also discouraged from supporting the report by the unresolved situation with cyprus. i therefore believe that we should change the debate on turkey's accession to the eu to a debate on a strategic partnership with turkey.
in writing. ‒ albania is a very controversial country in the balkans. high population growth combined with backward infrastructure, a very poor state of industry and agriculture, together with historical concepts of 'greater albania' and a literally tragic state of corruption, complete the image of one of the new nato member states. the report finds it difficult to find positive steps in government action and considers religious tolerance a success. the country has a lot of conditions for tourism development, from lake ohrid through magical mountains with wild, still preserved nature to an interesting coastline, there is also an interesting natural wealth (among other things, deposits of natural asphalt). the tragic state of the judiciary and the application of the new laws adopted is indicated in the report very carefully. i don't think that protecting the rights and freedoms of the lbti community should take precedence over national minority rights and improving relations with neighboring countries. nor can the development of renewable energy sources and environmental protection be given the same importance as the development of employment in industry and agriculture. other attributes of modern society (besides the widespread corruption) are also in the news. unfortunately, large grants to ngos only create another source of potential corruption. the whole picture is made up of a poor state of infrastructure. unfortunately, the report does not inspire historical optimism and rightly emphasises the need for further intensive all-round assistance in implementing the agreed measures. i therefore recommend that you take note of the report.

in writing. ‒ it is important to me as a social democrat that the poverty reduction target set out in strategy 2020 is met. as the eu continues to move away from this objective, i welcome this report, which seeks to raise awareness of this issue and at the same time to bridge the gap between social and energy policy in the european debate. the report on the achievement of the poverty reduction target in the light of increasing household costs focuses in particular on the significant shortcomings in the efforts to reduce high costs in poor households. to this end, it proposes targeting existing renewable energy and energy efficiency projects to poor households. reducing the costs for the poor and most vulnerable households and removing obstacles to the efficient use of resources is one of the eu's key pillars in the fight against poverty. i consider it particularly important to target european funds correctly on households in energy poverty. given the significant increase in the number of people at risk of poverty or social exclusion between 2008 and 2013, more energy needs to be invested in addressing this issue. it is therefore necessary to keep these people in need in mind and to continue to raise awareness and take action to combat poverty.
in writing. the problem of poverty and social exclusion must be actively addressed within the european union as a developed community, and every effort must be made to eliminate this risk and to promote at least minimum standards of living for as large a proportion of the population as possible in each member state. these problems cannot be solved with immediate effect, but maximum effort must be made continuously to create the optimal conditions for reducing the risk of poverty and social exclusion. the key role of individual member states, which should be expected to be willing to contribute to the common objective of the european union and to raise the standard of living of their citizens, is that they should also have their own national strategies to address this problem, which the european commission should fully assist them in developing. the european social and investment funds are undoubtedly an important instrument for poverty reduction, and they are a priori intended to be used precisely to finance investments that lead to social benefits.

in writing. the fight against poverty is certainly an important topic which deserves our attention, but i do not see the need to address this issue in an own-initiative report of the european parliament, which is not legally binding and whose discussion has resulted in a set of difficult to grasp, often contradictory and unrealistic recommendations which do not reflect the national specificities and social systems of the individual member states. poverty reduction measures, assistance to the needy and other social issues should be addressed by the member states, through their competent authorities at national, regional and local level, in such a way as to take the utmost account of the different conditions and needs of the groups of citizens concerned in each member state. i therefore did not support the report on the achievement of the poverty reduction target in the context of increasing household costs as a whole and regarded it as an unnecessary and counterproductive interference with the national social policies of the member states.

telecoms and automotive industries, chaired by commissioner oettinger. with a strong spirit of partnership, the commission is working towards a shared european strategy on connected and automated driving as part of the energy union, research, innovation and competitiveness strategy. research and innovation are thus also being addressed. vehicle automation technology has developed very quickly, from increasingly sophisticated driver assistance systems intended to improve road safety, and indeed driving comfort, already on the market, to fully automated vehicles that could participate in normal traffic in the short and medium term. however, safety must never be compromised. i want to be very clear that the process towards automation should ensure that it will provide clear road safety benefits by removing, not adding, risks. the first question referred to the challenges posed by automation. the existing legal framework defining the rules of behaviour for road users will need to be adapted to allow automated driving and to ensure safety for all road users. this includes a review not only of the international conventions on road traffic, in particular the vienna road traffic convention, but also the member states’ highway codes. work in the united nations economic commission for europe is already under way on the international framework. it is crucial to ensure the highest possible level of security of communications and the protection of data and privacy at all times. these are indeed key elements for raising public acceptance. several initiatives are taking place on security in the framework of the digital single market strategy in terms of privacy under the new general data protection regulation. there will be one data protection law applicable across the european union. data protection has been addressed also in the framework of the so-called c-its platform. concerning liability, the gear 2030 initiative on highly automated vehicles is now taking up the issue with the aim to understand if and what is changing with further levels of automation. then we have road construction. road construction will probably be affected if we want to maximise benefits from this new technology. these aspects are being assessed also in the c-its platform, and the results will be fed into the gear 2030 initiative. also, the upgrade of the relevant cellular communication networks is being discussed in the context of the relevant high-level round table on connected and automated driving. finally, a few remarks regarding testing and inspection procedures and vehicle-type approval. highly—automated vehicles can, to a large extent, already comply with conventional-type approval requirements, for instance general construction and emissions. discussions are also ongoing at unece level with a view to updating the relevant regulations in this are also.

the rapporteur. madam president, commissioner, mr president of the european court of auditors, ladies and gentlemen, today we are about to adopt one of the most important documents on the management of the common financial resources at european union level. we will express our views on the way the european commission used the means at its disposal to implement its policies in 2014. the discharge process is on the agenda of the european parliament every spring, and the rapporteurs regularly present and defend their reports, as i did this year. yet i tried to bring new perspectives and new themes into the routine process. this is because the new economic paradigm and the requirements for it present a good opportunity to make certain changes in the established standards of control of the european commission's management. these changes are not self-perpetuating. on the contrary, their sole purpose is to assess whether the eu budgetary resources are not only spent in accordance with the formal and legislative rules but also contribute to the real effects and impacts of the economic, social and environmental development of the european union. are we able to allocate resources to the areas where this effect is greatest? are we able to identify new european priorities or are we still living in the grip of the stereotypes of the past decades? and whether we can adequately measure and evaluate these effects and draw lessons from them to shape new policy strategies. i've been devoting the process of change towards performance culture for most of the past year. i believe that many of the questions above cannot be answered in the affirmative if we are to remain objective. although economic developments and investment activity in europe are now experiencing a modest recovery and the unemployment rate is declining, the effects of the crisis have not yet been fully overcome. and this is precisely what justifies us in thinking differently in the field of budgetary policy, in particular in order to be better able to face the next crises that will inevitably arise. the european union budget should be equipped with control tools and mechanisms so that european funds are not misused and that every euro spent can be effectively evaluated. we are not alone in the european parliament in this effort to boost efficiency and simplify the budget. the same approach is also stated by the european court of auditors in its annual report for 2014. it is also confirmed by the initiatives of the european commission and the role of the council, especially during the current dutch presidency. the absolution must be, in my view, a logical political document, a standard procedure, not a tool for the unsystematic prosecution of the guilty, only selected and exposed at random. let us focus on how to identify and describe the manifestations of possible mismanagement of 1% of the european union's gdp, and in particular let us seek together solutions to this situation. merely drawing attention to some of the suspects, without suggesting measures and solutions, is pointless. i am aware that political compromises are needed to promote new elements. i nevertheless maintain that discharge should be as objective and competent as possible and should not become a tool for political struggle or settling accounts between member states. i know it will take years to implement changes in the way we do things. but i am convinced that if the european parliament did not follow this trend, it would become isolated and out of the mainstream of the budgetary policy of the european union in its quest for a result-oriented and performance-oriented budget of the european union. and that's certainly not what any of us want. i thank you all for your professional approach, i thank my team, the secretariat of the committee on budgetary control, all my shadow rapporteurs, the court of auditors, the entire european commission headed by vice-president georgieva, and you, colleagues, for the utmost objectivity in your assessment of my report.

in writing. ‒ today we voted to accede croatia to the convention on mutual assistance and cooperation between customs administrations. the convention was adopted in 1997 and aims to enable judicial authorities to cooperate with each other in preventing and detecting infringements of national customs legislation. signatories to this convention may request assistance or cooperation in the customs field in various forms, such as personnel and organisational support. cross-border cooperation is most often carried out for the purpose of investigating and prosecuting offences in the form of illicit trafficking in narcotic drugs and psychotropic substances, hazardous and toxic waste, but also cultural goods or goods liable to taxation in order to avoid the fulfilment of the tax obligation. the european parliament hereby gives its consent to the accession of croatia to this convention, which i supported in my vote.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the recommendation for a council decision concerning the accession of the republic of croatia to the convention of 18 december 1997, drawn up on the basis of article k.3 of the treaty on european union, on mutual assistance and cooperation between customs administrations. the act of accession of the republic of croatia contains a simplified system for croatia’s accession to the conventions and protocols concluded by the member states on the basis of article 34 teu (previously article k.3 teu) or article 293 ec. the act of accession simply provides that croatia accedes to the conventions and protocols by virtue of the act.

in writing. ‒ i am strongly in favour of further integration of the european railway area. i believe that this step will have positive results for all parties, as it will bring more growth and create new jobs. three railway packages have been launched so far, bringing a lot of improvements in this area. however, further regulation is still needed as the european railway environment still faces many obstacles, especially in the area of entrepreneurship. for these reasons, i support the creation of a fourth package, based on the eu agency for railways and the proposal for a recast of directive 2004/49/ec. this new instrument will not only improve the technical compatibility of transport, rolling stock, signalling systems and other components of railway systems, but also increase transparency compared to many national regulations. it is equally important to take into account the situation in the individual member states with different track gauges. although this situation does not apply to the czech republic, this fact should be taken into account as countries with a track gauge greater than the eu standard are cut off from the main eu rail network.
in writing. i supported the second reading of the draft regulation, which, together with the draft directive on railway safety and the draft directive on the interoperability of railways in the eu, is part of the so-called eu's fourth railway package. those proposals aim to remove the remaining administrative and technical obstacles to the convergence of the different railway systems in the member states. the proposed regulation on the eu agency for railways is intended to replace the existing regulation no 881/2004 of the same name. the new legislation of the already functioning eu agency for railways responds to the changes under discussion at the same time in the framework of the railway package in the field of railway safety and interoperability of railway systems. the proposal would concentrate more powers in the eu agency for railways, which would allow the agency to issue all authorisations for vehicles to be used and all safety certificates to railway undertakings operating cross-border services. importantly, where previously undertakings had to apply for a licence in each member state separately, a single licence from the eu agency for railways is now sufficient. this is intended to reduce the administrative burden on railway undertakings. in addition, the agency will be able to establish a single contact point for the submission of all applications.
in writing. i voted in favour of the adoption of the european parliament's proposal for a regulation on the european union agency for railways (era). the european union agency for railways will have the power to issue safety certificates to railway undertakings operating in more than one member state. a railway undertaking operating in one member state may choose to be certified by era or by a national safety authority. the aim will be, in particular, to speed up administrative procedures and reduce administrative costs, while maintaining the existing high level of security and preventing hidden discrimination. it is expected to enable railway undertakings and manufacturers across the eu to increase economies of scale and also to increase their competitiveness.
in writing. ‒ i supported the revision of regulation (ec) 881/2004 establishing a european agency for railways (era). the revised text will give the era new competence in the area of safety certification, vehicle authorisation and monitoring the development of the european rail traffic management system. i believe a centralised agency will be more efficient that 28 national authorities and should have the capacity to settle conflicts, as is already the case in the air transport sector. this text is part of the technical pillar of the 4th railway package, which aims to advance toward a single european railway area, and the whole package should be evaluated globally. in a european union of free movement, the development of the transport sector cannot be confined to national level, and opening the national networks will attract the investment the sector is lacking.
in writing. the railway parcels, as they have been gradually adopted, have two pages. ensure the organisation of the interconnection of rail networks across the eu and the harmonisation of technical standards for both railway sets and infrastructure. this part of the package is undeniably a positive step. the forced division of railways into infrastructure, freight and passenger transport, often carried out recklessly, especially in smaller eu countries, or associated with privatisation (see uk), has clearly not worked. it is logical that a number of politicians have legitimate and critical comments on this aspect of railway developments. the interoperability directive is, in this respect, a technical standard and can therefore allow the recognition of the technical conditions for authorising the placing of a vehicle on the market and facilitate the obtaining of authorisation to place a vehicle in service. the railway agency shall authorise the safety and traffic management systems to ensure consistency between the corresponding on-board subsystems and the infrastructure. it is understandable that the member states will find in the directive an obligation to provide comparative tables when implementing it. they shall make it possible to identify easily the national provisions corresponding to the different parts of this directive. in view of the above, i am optimistic that the directive will make progress in addressing the problems associated with the recognition of the possibility of cross-eu operation of assemblies and will also improve the possibility of supplying the fitting in different eu countries. i therefore support the adoption of this directive.
in writing. i welcome the simplification of vehicle authorisation conditions which will remove a major barrier to the entry of new vehicles on the market. new companies wishing to enter the railway market have difficulty entering because they are unable to put their vehicles into service due to the complicated authorisation rules in the individual member states. in the czech republic, the example is regiojet or leo express. however, the same applies to established companies wishing to enter foreign markets or to introduce new vehicles, which must undergo a series of tests and obtain authorisation for placing in service. simplification of the conditions for the authorisation of vehicles will therefore help to create effective competition in rail transport.
in writing. i have agreed to the adoption of the recommendation for second reading in the council with a view to adopting a directive of the european parliament and of the council on the interoperability of the rail system within the european union, as i believe that this directive will lead to a better unification of the european railway area, reduce administrative costs and speed up procedures. i consider this directive to be important, in particular because of the persistent profound differences in rail transport between member states. at the same time, this directive will help to increase the competitiveness of eu businesses and reduce costs for railway companies and manufacturers. i also see a positive contribution in the effort to reduce the bureaucratic burden on companies focusing on the production of rolling stock. under the new rules, they will not have to submit an application to each member state in which the vehicle will be operated separately. a single point of contact will be established for this purpose, which will facilitate procedures and increase transparency.
in writing. i am pleased that after long negotiations a compromise has been reached which will move rail transport towards a single european railway area. the technical part of the fourth railway package simplifies the certification of vehicles intended for international operations to be newly approved by the european union agency for railways. the proposal also includes the unification of rail traffic management systems and the eu single safety certificate. the proposed agreement will help to speed up crossborder rail traffic by removing obstacles at border stations, such as the exchange of locomotives. that's why i decided to support this motion.
in writing. i supported the second reading of the draft directive which, together with the draft directive on railway safety and the draft regulation on the european union agency for railways, forms part of the so-called eu's fourth railway package. those proposals aim to remove the remaining administrative and technical obstacles to the convergence of the different railway systems (i.e. infrastructure networks and vehicles) in the member states. the new directive on the interoperability of the rail system within the european union is to replace directive 2008/57/ec on the interoperability of the rail system within the community. it has already been amended several times and a new regulation should be adopted for reasons of clarity. the interoperability, commonality and interconnectedness of rail systems are laid down in particular in the technical requirements for interoperability (tsi). the proposed directive clarifies some points of the existing adaptation, for example in the provisions on the scope of the directive, the adaptation of derogations from the tsi and the applicability of national rules. this directive aims to enhance interconnection in the design, manufacture, construction, operation and upgrading of railway systems.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the adoption of a european parliament and council directive on the interoperability of the rail system within the european union, as the system introduced by this new directive will bring europe closer to a single european railway area. it will significantly help to improve the technical compatibility of infrastructure, rolling stock, signalling systems and other components of the rail system and simplify the procedures for the approval of rolling stock for use on the entire european rail network. the interoperability of the european railway traffic management system (ertms) projects will also be ensured.
in writing. ‒ i supported the revised text on the interoperability of the rail system within the eu. the text is part of the 4th railway package which aims to achieve a single european rail area. i strongly believe that, while the eu is built upon free movement, the railway sector cannot compete with the other modes of transport as long as its development remains purely national. this new directive will provide for shortening the time it takes for companies to obtain certification of their rolling stock, and for unified procedures and clearer interoperability rules across the eu, under the surveillance of the european railways agency.
in writing. ‒ i have decided to support the report presented because i am convinced that the system introduced by this new directive will bring europe closer to a single european railway area. i am convinced that this directive will also reduce administrative costs and speed up procedures, while maintaining the existing high level of safety. i also welcome the fact that this directive will significantly reduce the number of national rules in the areas where harmonised regulation is being introduced at eu level. there is no doubt that this instrument will help to prevent any hidden discrimination, in particular against new undertakings seeking to enter the railway market. i therefore expect that the directive will enable railway undertakings and manufacturers across the eu to increase economies of scale and eu businesses to increase their competitiveness.
in writing. i voted in favour of the proposed text of the directive of the european parliament and of the council on railway safety, to support the efforts to create a common regulatory framework. this framework is to become the basis for the establishment of a single market for rail transport services. the railway safety directive, originally issued in 2004, brought about significant improvements in the harmonisation of the content of safety regulations, safety certificates for railway undertakings, the tasks and role of safety authorities and accident investigations. these advantages have led me to support the revision of this directive, which will lead to a transition from the current two-part system to a single safety certificate in the union. the revision will enhance the role of the eu agency for railways (era), which will play a key role in issuing safety certificates to railway undertakings operating in more than one member state. this will allow each company to decide whether it wants to be certified by era or by the national safety authority. in addition, railway safety and incident reporting will be improved.
in writing. i supported the second reading of the draft directive which, together with the draft directive on the interoperability of the rail system in the european union and the draft regulation on the european union agency for railways, is part of the so-called eu's fourth railway package. those proposals aim to remove the remaining administrative and technical obstacles to the convergence of the different railway systems in the member states. the new railway safety directive is to replace the existing directive 2004/49/ec of the same name. the proposed amendment provides in particular for a single safety certificate for railway undertakings to be issued by the eu agency for railways. the single certificate replaces the two-component system whereby undertakings have until now had to obtain a certificate at both union and member state level. the single safety certificate will be valid for undertakings in all member states where they operate. a railway undertaking operating in only one member state may choose to apply for certification to the eu railway agency or to a national authority. the proposal also gives the eu agency for railways the possibility to set up a system for the exchange of information on safety risks between safety authorities across member states. i consider it useful that all three legislative proposals under discussion are a meaningful development of the work begun with the first railway package adopted in 2001 and aimed at promoting the single internal market.
in writing. i supported the adoption of the directive of the european parliament and of the council on railway safety, in particular to create a framework for harmonising the content of safety rules and to create and implement a single eu safety certificate. it is essential to improve the safety and incident reporting culture of railway undertakings and infrastructure managers. this will motivate staff to report incidents in confidence and allow the railway industry to learn and improve working practices. the safety, interoperability and reliability of the european rail network will be enhanced. member states will be obliged to check, for example, whether drivers comply with the rules on working hours, driving hours and rest periods. an important element will be the improvement of the system for the timely exchange of information on security risks. this will further facilitate the cross-border exchange of information in cases where there is a safety risk, for example where the same type of rolling stock is used in more than one member state.
in writing. ‒ i supported the revision of directive 2004/49/ec on safety on the community’s railways, as negotiated. this proposal is part of the 4th railway package which aims at creating a single european railway area. specifically this text provides for a single eu safety certificate instead of the current two-part system. the competence to issue those certificates will be left to the european railways agency, thus enabling the use of a unified procedure across the eu and saving time. opening up the market to eu competition is the only way to overcome the current bottlenecks we are facing in the development of a european railway area, and this has to go hand in hand with ensuring the highest level of safety for cross-border train operations.

in writing. - an index is a measure of price or quantity, usually determined from time to time on the basis of a representative set of baseline data. if an index is used as a reference price for a financial instrument or contract, it becomes the reference value. currently, there is a wide variety of benchmarks, which are established by different entities, from public bodies to independent benchmark providers, using different methodologies. our group points out the importance of benchmarks, but above all their weaknesses. indeed, reference interest rates can be manipulated very easily, as has been demonstrated for example with reference interest rates libor and euribor. since the trialogue did not bring any significant improvement in this respect and no certainty of protection against possible manipulation, i voted against the proposal.
in writing. as my group's shadow rapporteur, i supported a compromise version of the regulation which would avoid scandals such as the manipulation of libor reference interest rates, reference exchange rates and the manipulation of other indices. the need to improve the quality of indices used in many financial contracts by both firms and individual investors was highlighted by the aforementioned scandals of the past years. the main challenge in the development of this legislation was to find rules that respected the existence of both indices describing markets with turnover in the hundreds of billions of euros and indices showing the development of small, often local, markets. we have, on behalf of the european parliament, pushed for clear proportionality in regulation, reflecting the differences between the different types of indices.

in writing. ‒ i supported this report because i believe that the principle stating that eu citizens should have an access to public administration documents is right. however, i see there are some limits to this principle and that is why i could not support some of the measures proposed in the report. the first one concerns holding trilogue negotiations in public. it has to be understood that the efficiency of the trilogue set-up is based on mutual trust between all parties present. in making these talks public we risk that there will be more political than technical exchange, which is not always useful when a deal should be reached. the same applies, in my view, to the second case mentioned in the report – negotiations of international agreements. by publishing the mandate or negotiating texts too early, we would undermine the position of the eu negotiators which could eventually end in reaching an agreement which is far less beneficial than previously expected.

in writing. ‒ today we voted on the draft report on public access to documents for 2014 and 2015. the report stresses the need for transparency, which can strengthen citizens' trust in the eu institutions. we recall that the eu institutions must operate and conduct their policies on the basis of representative democracy, as laid down in article 10 (1) teu, and must ensure that the principles of full transparency, sharing and proper and timely information of citizens are respected. we also underline the importance of article 10 (3) teu, which recognises participatory democracy as one of the eu's main principles. i agree that decisions must be taken as close as possible to the citizen. i also believe that citizens must have the right to know and control the activities of their representatives, the decision-making process as well as the use of public funds, including the structural funds. the report is, in my view, sufficiently critical of the application of the principle of transparency to date and sets ambitious targets for the future, which is why i voted in favour of its adoption.
in writing. ‒ i am a supporter of easy access by citizens to information held by the eu institutions and therefore believe that steps should be taken to facilitate this access based on the principle of transparency. to this end, digital and electronic means that are user-friendly and also meet the needs of people with disabilities should be used to the maximum extent. only official documents for which there is a genuine justification for classifying them should be subject to a certain degree of classification. these are mainly informal or diplomatic meetings involving eu institutions, the full disclosure of which would be detrimental rather than beneficial.
in writing. public access to eu documents is one of the fundamental rights of eu citizens, as laid down in the charter of fundamental rights. i personally think it is very important that all citizens have an overview of what is happening in the eu and are aware not only of the specific decisions that affect them, but also of their rights within the eu. i therefore welcomed the report on public access to documents in 2014/2015, which highlighted in particular the imperfections that need to be addressed as soon as possible in the public interest. the key problem here remains the lack of transparency on the part of all institutions and bodies. i therefore strongly advocate the appointment of a transparency officer, who would be responsible for compliance with the legislation and improving procedures. every citizen has the right to access information about their representatives, the decision-making process and, in particular, the way public funds are allocated and spent. to this end, i agree to the publication of an electronic register to facilitate access to this data. however, all eu institutions and bodies need to develop appropriate action in this area and contribute to greater openness and access to information, as this approach is a fundamental democratic element and should not be relegated to the background. i'm a long-time advocate of the introduction of a mandatory register of lobbyists.
in writing. in today's vote on the draft report on public access to documents in 2014/2015, i supported the position of the european people's party's parliamentary club, as i believe that some of the proposals contained in the original version of the report overemphasise the principles of 'direct democracy' and i do not believe that this approach would be the solution to all problems. there is no doubt that there is still room for improving transparency and hence the comprehensibility of the eu institutions and the processes they use. the public's right to know must be respected. however, i do not believe that this right can be exercised by measures such as the preservation of all e-mail correspondence, the making available of all supporting material in all circumstances or the keeping of a record of all meetings held. for example, a member of the european parliament is a public figure who is responsible for the integrity of the performance of his mandate, but this does not mean that he has to publish a list of all his meetings, including meetings with friends and family members.
