in writing. i supported the resolution on domestic workers and carers in the eu, as i believe that this group of people has been neglected for a long time. in 2010, the domestic work sector employed more than 52 million people worldwide, according to the international labour organization. according to the international labour organisation, 29.9% of domestic workers are completely excluded from national labour laws and, in the eu, the work of domestic workers and carers is still very rarely and unevenly regulated in the member states, with the result that domestic workers are often not considered typical or properly employed workers and their employment rights and social protection are therefore severely restricted. i therefore welcome the fact that we have asked the commission to present a set of policy instruments for domestic and care work, setting out qualitative guidelines for both areas. it considers that these proposals should focus, firstly, on the introduction of a general framework for the professionalisation of domestic and care work, leading to the recognition and standardisation of the relevant professions, skills and career progression, and secondly, on the urgent proposal for a directive on carers' leave and a framework for the recognition of the status of non-professional carers, which ensures them a remuneration and minimum social security standards for the period they are caring.
in writing. ‒ i am in favour of the dignity of workers and carers, but this area has its own specificities in each country and it is not the eu's role to impose regulations on the member states. i voted against it.
in writing. ‒ today we voted on a report highlighting the obstacles faced by domestic workers and carers in the eu. according to statistics, this is an industry that employed over 52 million people worldwide in 2010. the majority of these are women, who accounted for 83% of global domestic workers in 2010. i believe that these workers should be given greater legal protection, employment and social protection rights, equal to those of employees with an employment contract. equally important are decent wages, regular working hours, paid holidays, health and safety at work and health insurance. i am also aware that this is an area where workers, mainly women, are at increased risk of exploitation. the report calls for greater protection for such persons as well as for greater enforcement of their rights. i supported the report.
in writing. i supported the report on domestic workers and carers in the eu, which touches on the long-standing problem of the use of mostly illegal workers, especially women. these women are often subject to multiple discrimination on the basis of lack of education and language skills, and are most at risk of gender-based violence and discrimination. due to the growing demand for domestic workers and carers and the lack of formal structures to provide work, this issue has become part of the grey economy. illegal workers are thus excluded from labour law and cannot enjoy, for example, the right to wage fixing, the organisation of working hours, the right to weekly, annual or maternity leave and the related benefits. paradoxically, however, this problem also affects the regular carers and workers who live in these households at the same time. it is therefore necessary to establish a specific legal framework to allow for the legal and organised employment of domestic workers and carers and to lay down the rights and obligations of the persons concerned in order to guarantee legal certainty for workers in this sector and their potential employers. i believe it is essential to recognise the work of these people as a full-fledged profession and to guarantee the rights of these workers. equally urgent is the need to tackle undeclared work, which affects mainly migrant women and domestic workers.
in writing. the report addresses the issue of domestic workers, of whom 2.5 million were employed in the eu in 2010, according to ilo data, 88% of whom were women. in most eu countries, domestic work is unreported and a significant proportion of domestic workers are migrants. in the light of the single labour market and the mobility of citizens, the question of ensuring the quality and professionalism of domestic work arises, while ensuring the decent treatment of these workers. the draft report was from the outset one-sidedly concerned with the protection of workers, expressing concern about exploitation and lack of transparency in the employment of domestic workers. quality assurance of their work is mentioned only in relation to their professionalisation. the report calls on the commission to adopt legislative and non-legislative measures, such as a proposal for a directive on carers' leave and a framework for the recognition of the status of non-professional carers. it also calls on the member states to provide for professional qualifications for certain types of domestic work, requiring specific skills and competences. i consider these and other measures to be merely an increase in the administrative burden and formal requirements without improving the quality of work performed in households. since the amendments themselves did not bring about a substantial improvement in the report, i was ultimately among those who spoke against the draft report.
in writing. ‒ i voted against this report as it calls for an eu legislative framework on domestic workers and carers. i believe that this should be up to member states’ competences.
in writing. ‒ the digital era provide a series of opportunities for women to perform a professional activity, either being employed or self-employed. that is a phenomenon to be supported and promoted as it gives more chances for women to have both a successful professional career and a balanced family life. this report, however, addresses a rather unrelated issue of women on boards of companies which i am opposed to and for that reason i could not support it as a whole.
in writing. ‒ i support the elimination of inequalities between men and women, including in employment. i believe that increasing digital literacy and the use of information and communication technologies is one of the main drivers of employment for women today. i have decided to vote against this report, however, because it calls, among other things, for the unblocking of the directive on women in public administration. while i support the overturning of long-held stereotypes and welcome initiatives aimed at gender equality, the directive on women in public administration and similar proposals containing gender quotas go, in my view, far beyond these efforts in their legislative reach.
in writing. i endorsed the european parliament resolution of 28 april 2016 on gender equality and the empowerment of women in the digital age, as i believe that digitalisation has revolutionized and fundamentally changed the way people obtain and provide information, communicate, interact, study and work, creating new opportunities for participation in public and political debates, education and employment, new opportunities for self-determination and huge economic potential for the european union and beyond, and therefore the digital age has the potential to influence the status of women in society. the problem is that only 9% of developers in europe are women, only 19% of leaders in ict and communications are women (compared to 45% in other services) and only 19% of entrepreneurs are women (compared to 54% in other services). i therefore believe that it was appropriate to call on the commission and the council to fully exploit the potential of the information society, ict and the internet in terms of women's empowerment, their rights and freedoms and gender equality irrespective of age and other factors.

in writing. ‒ today we voted on a report on gender equality and the empowerment of women in the digital age. the report points out that digitalisation has revolutionized and transformed the way people obtain and provide information, interact, study and work, and that this process also brings huge economic potential for the eu and beyond. however, it also points out that there are significant gender gaps in access to vocational and educational opportunities in the field of information and communication technologies and computer skills. i believe that digitalisation also has a significant impact on the labour market, as it changes value chains and creates new job opportunities, but also brings with it negative impacts that can affect women in particular, such as the infringement of workers' rights and the delimitation of working hours and work and non-work obligations, leading to an increase in low-paid and less secure jobs. the report also remembers that. that's why i voted for her.
in writing. ‒ digitalisation has enormous potential to be exploited in a number of areas, including improving gender equality. i am a supporter of equal opportunities for both sexes and would be happy to support initiatives that help to increase the representation of women in the information technology (ict) sectors. the ict sector is growing very fast and is constantly creating new jobs. this creates approximately 120 000 new jobs each year that are not being filled. at the same time, this shortage represents an opportunity for more qualified women to be involved in the sector. however, to empower women in the digital age, it is first necessary to ensure better education and training, which so far appears to be severely lacking given that 60% of school pupils in the eu do not even use digital equipment in the classroom. i am convinced that increasing the active participation of women in the information society will lead to increased competitiveness and improved social and economic conditions in society. i am convinced that the commission's estimate that more women in the digital labour market can increase eu gdp by eur 9 billion a year is correct. at the same time, digitalisation needs to be promoted in politics, allowing for more active participation and self-realisation not only for women but also for other under-represented groups.
in writing. i endorsed the report on gender equality and the empowerment of women in the digital age, despite many reservations. while the digital age brings advanced communication capabilities and creates space for faster and better access to information, including information supporting greater empowerment of women in the labour market and public life, its negative consequences cannot be underestimated either. there is systematic intimidation and harassment of women in cyberspace on a daily basis, not to mention cases of sexual exploitation. consider the tragic case of amanda todd. cybercrime is difficult to track and prove to offenders, and its regulation in national criminal codes is often inadequate. i therefore welcome the report's call for policymakers and the european commission to act effectively in the development of legislation in this area and to better prosecute cyber violence and bullying. there is also a need to raise awareness through education and promote safe use of the internet, especially by women. i also welcome the calls to member states and the commission to provide financial support to women entrepreneurs to use digital technologies and start businesses and to highlight the added value of online training courses for women, people with disabilities and those living in rural areas. these instruments will give these groups a chance to gain a foothold in the labour market, enable them to fight possible unemployment and strengthen their financial independence and the desire to set up their own business.
in writing. ‒ while i share the observation that the digital revolution is benefiting men more than women – currently, just 30% of all people working in the ict sector are women – i decided to vote against this report because some of the provision in the report will not help solve this situation. indeed, i do not believe that the women-on-boards directive imposing quotas will help to improve the situation.

mr president, the nord stream 2 gas pipeline is a practical example of how the european union often acts in contradiction to its more long-standing intentions. when the gas crisis erupted a few years ago, eu politicians agreed that ensuring the security of gas supply was one of the union's common priorities. today, everything seems different. nord stream 2 can be viewed from three perspectives. the first is to ensure that there is enough gas for the eu countries. the second is the political decision whether only one member state can be so strongly represented on the entry of natural gas into the european union. the third point of view is the economic point of view. the transit of gas is an interesting source of financing for some countries, i understand that, they are ukraine, poland, slovakia, the czech republic. personally, i prefer to safely secure sufficient gas, and therefore i see no reason to question that intention in any way. in conclusion, i would like to add that it is only because of some strange behind-the-scenes machinations that a pipeline has not yet been built to bring natural gas directly to the balkans. it is in this context that it would be appropriate to discuss strengthening the security of gas supply to the eu countries.
mr president, exactly 66 years ago, robert schuman set out his vision for a secure europe. it was five years after the end of world war ii, and europe was recovering from the trauma of war. politicians asked themselves how to avoid repeating the same horrors. schuman formulated his vision as follows: 'by the common setting up of the productions of the base and the institution of a new high authority whose decisions will be taken by france, germany and the countries which will join them, this proposal will achieve the first concrete assises of a european federation indispensable to the preservation of peace.' it was therefore clear already 66 years ago that the path to a secure europe would not be a one-off and simple one. it's good to remember this long-term effort. once, in communist czechoslovakia, i dreamed of the free life we enjoy today. the founding fathers had courage, and we must have courage, today, to not be afraid to thank them and to continue in this effort.

in writing. i supported the recommendation to approve at second reading the council's position on the draft europol regulation. the regulation further strengthens and streamlines this already existing organisation for police cooperation to combat terrorism and serious cross-border crime. it helps to better counter the threats that eu member states face together today. europol is already making the eu safer by operating in cooperation with national police authorities and by collecting, exchanging (including with partners outside the eu) and processing data on suspects. it will be able to do so even better after the adoption of this regulation. the adopted regulation also substantially strengthens the role of the european parliament and national parliaments, the directly elected representatives of the eu citizens, in monitoring europol's activities, which i very much welcome. in addition, the regulation provides a robust framework for the protection of personal data with which europol works in its databases, which also requires our support. at the same time, the regulation does not give europol 'agents' enforcement powers which are reserved to member states' police forces, and thus does not restrict member states' sovereignty in sensitive areas of internal security.
in writing. i supported the revision of the regulation strengthening the powers of the european agency europol. the agency is one of the largest analysis centres for serious crime and terrorism in the eu. it is involved in more than 18 000 cross-border investigations every year. europol has recently been focusing, among other things, on combating relatively new and serious threats such as online propaganda and human trafficking. the internet environment associated with terrorist propaganda, in particular by the islamic state, is the focus of europol's specialised centre, the internet referral unit, which has been operational since july 2015. this unit systematically combats hateful content on the internet and removes harmful content in cooperation with the internet service provider. this activity is preventing the radicalisation and recruitment of young people into terrorist organisations. since the launch of the unit, more than 1 700 decisions have been issued, and in 90% of cases, harmful content has been removed in cooperation with specific internet providers. the new european counter-terrorism centre was launched in january 2016. the revision aims to improve and extend the exchange of information between member states, to make the agency work more easily and efficiently, and, above all, to simplify the creation of specialised units to deal with specific threats. the review shall also take into account sufficient safeguards for the protection of personal data and provide for democratic oversight.
in writing. i supported the proposal to reform the eu agency for law enforcement cooperation (europol) because i believe it will contribute to an effective fight against terrorism or cybercrime of all kinds. organized crime in particular is now a transnational issue and it is therefore natural that the fight against it requires coordinated international cooperation, capable of deploying rapid response resources in crisis situations. in order to promote the sharing of information between individual member states, europol is obliged to inform the ep, the ec and the council of the status and quality of the sharing of information between member states. it is clear that the protection of personal data is sufficiently guaranteed. as at national levels, access to such data is restricted to authorised persons and the information is transmitted in encrypted form. all eu standard rules apply to the handling of personal data by europol, including the possibility for individuals to lodge a complaint.

in writing. this directive resonates with the eu's objective of attracting to its member states qualified and capable workers, researchers or students from third countries who can benefit the european economy and fill labour market gaps. the text provides clearer and simpler conditions for both the entry and subsequent residence of third-country nationals in the eu, and constitutes a harmonised european system that will apply in all member states. i believe that talented students or workers from outside the eu can help member states to improve their competitiveness on the global stage, which is why i voted in favour of this report.
in writing. this directive summarises the conditions for the admission of third-country nationals to the eu for periods of more than three months for the purposes of research, studies, pupil exchange, paid and unpaid training, voluntary service and au pairs. for the first time, the directive establishes the general principle that an applicant who fulfils both the general and the specific conditions for admission must be admitted by the member state where the application for a residence or long-stay visa was lodged. the directive also defines compulsory and optional grounds for refusal, denial or non-renewal of a residence permit or long-stay visa. the directive guarantees the right to work, to study or to receive other forms of education. after the end of the stay for the purpose for which the residence permit was issued, the applicant also has the possibility to find a job for a specified period. it also provides for access to the labour market for family members of certain categories of third-country nationals and addresses mobility between eu member states. i believe that the directive can make a significant contribution to the desirable migration to eu countries and i cannot fail to mention the successful programmes of the countries of central and eastern europe which, more than 50 years ago, addressed the issues of training, studies and vocational training. if the directive will result in an improvement in the situation of those who want to migrate from eu countries to at least the level of the 1970s in the then socialist countries, then we can only welcome the proposal.

in writing. - in the context of accelerating the implementation of cohesion policy, i consider it important that the commission, in cooperation with the member states and their local and regional authorities, find ways to effectively combine funding from the structural funds and the european fund for strategic investments. although these are two instruments of different nature, they can complement each other and increase the leverage of investments. the commission should also issue comprehensive guidance on public procurement and the preventive measures necessary to avoid unnecessary errors and irregularities in the procurement process and, consequently, financial corrections and possible cancellation of eu financial contributions.
in writing. cohesion policy is the european union's strongest investment and development tool, with more than €350 billion earmarked for it until 2020. however, as the policy was launched with considerable delays in many member states in the new programming period and the pace of implementation is still sluggish, the threat of not being able to use all its instruments by the end of the period is more than real. it is for this reason that i supported the european parliament's resolution calling on the european commission to analyse and assess the current situation. i think it is extremely important that the analysis also includes a study of the obstacles faced by individual member states in drawing on their resources. i also voted for strengthening administrative capacity at national, regional and local levels to help implement cohesion policy in the future. i also supported new communication initiatives, as it is the lack of information among the public that is one of the blocks that negatively affects not only the implementation of policy itself, but also the scepticism that is often the product of misinformation.
in writing. cohesion policy plays a crucial role in bridging the socioeconomic gaps between eu member states. a successful cohesion policy will lead to an increase in the competitiveness of all european regions. however, the eu and the member states have shown significant delays in implementation and lack of flexibility, which severely limits the effectiveness of this policy. the report as a whole proposes a number of recommendations for accelerating progress in this area and for better implementation of the existing programmes for the period 2014-2020. the eu lacks administrative and absorption capacities at all levels, but these are crucial for faster and more effective implementation of european policies. therefore, both these areas need to be significantly strengthened. the potential of local and regional authorities, whose role in mobilising esi funds is crucial, is also far from being exploited.
in writing. ‒ the cohesion policy is the eus main tool to invest in and develop eu regions and cities, in order to promote job creation, business competitiveness, economic growth, sustainable development, and improve citizens’ quality of life. looking back at the period 2007-2013, the main obstacle to the better implementation of this policy has been the insufficient information available for potential beneficiaries. smes, start-ups and non-governmental organisations, which have the least administrative capacity, have particularly suffered much from this. this is why i welcome this resolution to accelerate the implementation of the cohesion policy, to find ways to speed up and improve the efficient implementation of the policy without losing the quality of the spending. simplifying the policy, decreasing the administrative burdens it implies, and increasing its good governance, among other measures, could be helpful in that regard.

in writing. reform of the asylum system is, in my view, inevitable. the eu cannot operate by the old rules and be able to face new challenges, including the migration crisis. i am strongly in favour of harmonising asylum procedures across the eu, and of putting in place and accessing reliable registration systems. but it is not possible to include quota redistribution in the reform of the asylum system. that's not the solution in my opinion. far more important is the establishment of an effective mechanism for the registration and screening of all asylum seekers in the eu.

in writing. the 2030 agenda for sustainable development and the sustainable development goals were adopted by the un general assembly in september 2015. it is a renewed international commitment to eradicate poverty, redefine and modernise our development strategies over the next 15 years. the document contains 17 new sustainable development goals and 169 targets, which strike a balance between the three dimensions of sustainable development - environmental, social and economic - in areas such as poverty, inequality, food security, health, sustainable consumption and production, growth, employment, infrastructure, sustainable management of natural resources and climate change, as well as gender equality. a full range of resources, both domestic and international, public and private, are needed to successfully deliver this programme. all countries must contribute a fair share, taking into account their level of development, specific conditions and capacity. the own and mutual responsibilities of states will be central to the agenda. i voted yes.
in writing. ‒ i am pleased that the resolution also contains what i consider to be a very important call for the eu and the member states to confirm their intention to allocate 0.7% of gni to official development assistance and to present a timetable for gradually increasing official development assistance to achieve this 0.7% target. unfortunately, funding for development programmes such as the un world food programme and the eu trust fund for syria and africa has so far fallen short of expectations and significantly below the level of commitments made. this is why eu member states must make a significant contribution in this area if the fight against poverty and conflict in the world and the related causes of the protracted migration crisis is to be successful.
in writing. given the importance of european and global development policy, i supported the resolution on the monitoring and the current status of the 2030 agenda and the sustainable development goals. it is necessary that the foreign affairs council of the european union develops a common position in this regard, which would serve as a starting point for the next high level political forum. it is probably not necessary to point out that, although there has been a general decline in poverty over the past decade, there are still some 900 million people in the world today who have to survive on less than $1.90 a day. the provision of basic conditions for a dignified life and the satisfaction of the most basic human needs is therefore often out of the question. i therefore called on the european commission to come forward with a proposal for an overarching strategy for internal and external policies, the development of which should be consulted by all relevant parties. this includes civil society, whose role in providing development assistance is indispensable. i also supported the renewal of the historic commitment of member states to contribute 0.7% of their gross national income to official development assistance. only five member states have now made this commitment. as in other areas, i believe that if the member states had been more conscientious and fulfilled their commitments, europe would not be facing a crisis of this magnitude today.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the resolution on the follow-up and state of play of the agenda 2030 and sustainable development goals, as i believe that it is crucial that the eu adopts a coherent and common position to ensure its leadership on this ambitious agenda. the 2030 agenda and the sustainable development goals embody a courageous international commitment to eradicate poverty and develop new development strategies for the next 15 years, and we should work hard to formulate an eu sustainable development strategy to play our part in delivering on its objectives. democratic scrutiny over the process will be key to the strategy’s success, which is why i would like to see the european parliament being more involved in the formulation, implementation and monitoring of the process.
in writing. ‒ i fully support measures introducing clear and transparent labelling of products sold directly to consumers, especially when it comes to food production. having said that, before introducing such measures, we have to assess fully their potential impacts on all the parts of a supply chain. it is perfectly reasonable to come up with compulsory labelling of fresh or frozen meat products, however the resolution added also products containing milk or meat and that could be, in my view, rather complicated for our producers. i am not convinced about the added value for the consumers. i would prefer to leave them liberty to decide whether labelling of origins of those ingredients should be or not present. that is why i voted against the resolution.
‒ i support the requirements for transparent labelling of products with regard to the country of origin. however, i consider that such measures must not impose a disproportionate administrative burden on food business operators. such measures are primarily aimed at providing consumers with information about products, so labels should primarily remain legible and understandable, not misleading. i would therefore prefer to have the indication of the country of origin for drinking milk or meat and milk as ingredients of a product on a voluntary basis. that is why i did not support the motion for a resolution calling for mandatory labelling.
in writing. ‒ i do not agree with the tightening of mandatory labelling on foodstuffs, such as the obligation to always indicate the country of origin of milk and milk-containing products. if that's the information that consumers want, it's an opportunity for companies to voluntarily provide it. the scope of mandatory data is already so wide that it is rather confusing and counterproductive for consumers.
in writing. today we voted on a report on the compulsory indication of the country of origin or place of provenance of certain foods. i think consumer awareness is of great importance. the consumer must be sufficiently informed about where a product is manufactured to make a genuinely informed choice. human health comes first. knowledge of the origin of a product can give consumers an idea of the quality of the product, especially milk and meat, which are products that consumers buy almost daily. according to the 2013 eurobarometr survey, 84% of consumers consider it necessary to indicate the origin of milk, including in milk products. i voted in favor of the bill.
in writing. the indication of the country of origin can be useful information for consumers who indicate in surveys that they would welcome this information for a wider range of foods than for beef, pork, poultry and sheepmeat, where this indication is already provided. on the other hand, the increased costs for producers and the question of feasibility in general must be considered, particularly in the case of multi-ingredient foods, where the indication of the origin of each individual ingredient could lead to a rather long list. i therefore favour an approach which does not subject all food to a single system of designation of origin but which distinguishes between single-component food, where designation of origin could be compulsory, and multi-component food, where it could remain voluntary.
in writing. i supported the resolution on the mandatory indication of the country of origin for certain categories of food, by which we repeatedly call on the commission to submit a legislative proposal for the mandatory indication of the origin of meat in processed products, but also, for example, the indication of the country of origin or place of provenance for all types of milk for drinking or milk products. not only is this information required by more than 80% of consumers, but by providing transparent and understandable information to consumers, we can contribute to the fight against fraud in the food sector and to achieving a level playing field in the internal market. it is important to remember that consumers do not want to be labelled 'made in the eu', but want to know the specific country of origin.
in writing. i did not support a resolution calling for mandatory country of origin labelling for certain foods. the rules currently in force make it compulsory to indicate the origin of certain types of meat, fish, fresh fruit and vegetables and others. in my view, this adjustment is sufficient. the consumer has sufficient information and undertakings wishing to indicate the origin of other foods can do so on a voluntary basis. some actually do, and they use that as a competitive advantage. but to make it mandatory in such complex cases as processed meat products would place a disproportionate burden on them. and for most consumers, the complex and lengthy listing of the origin of all types of meat (indicating both the country of rearing and slaughter) on the packaging of a meat product would have no meaning. there are, of course, cases where the introduction of mandatory origin labelling would be reasonable for consumers on the one hand and feasible without imposing an undue financial burden on producers on the other, for example extending the list of meat types to include game or farm animals. but the motion for a resolution combines a few acceptable proposals with a large number of unacceptable ones, and that is why i could not support it as a whole.
in writing. ‒ i voted against the resolution on the mandatory indication of the country of origin or place of provenance for certain foods. considering that labelling products is already a common practice and that the eu already has the highest standards of food quality and security worldwide, i consider that mandatory labelling will result in increased protectionist behaviours. in addition, it will lead to significant additional administrative costs, particularly for smes, and an increase in the price of products which will outweigh the benefits of such a measure.
in writing. ‒ any further regulation will need to strike a reasonable balance between consumer awareness and unnecessary financial and administrative burden on food producers. i do not think the text is balanced, and that is why i abstained.
in writing. ‒ i could not support the report as presented because it proposes some measures contradictory to our national legislation in this area. i believe there should be more emphasis put on national decision-making processes when it comes to modalities and provisions on parental leave.
in writing. i appreciate the attention that the european parliament and the rapporteur have paid to the issue of parental leave and reconciliation of work and private life. i consider initiatives to promote reconciliation of work and family life and to promote return to work to be very important. i prefer non-legislative initiatives, positive motivation and the removal of obstacles. the european union should uphold the principle of subsidiarity in this matter. i see no reason for european legislation to deal with issues such as men's use of parental leave or their share of housework. i am also not entirely convinced that the extension of the minimum length of parental leave follows current trends and is consistent with the objective of facilitating return to the work process. for these reasons, i could not support this motion and abstained.
in writing. ‒ while i fully agree that maternity or parental leave is a fundamental right and a benefit for both parents and children, and that reconciling motherhood and working life is a topic worthy of our attention, i do not think that there is a need to legislate on these issues at the level of the european union. i think that given the different historical experiences, the different approaches to the family and the different traditions in the countries of europe, it is important to think about the principle of subsidiarity and to leave the decision to the individual member states. the union may, by means of other non-legislative initiatives, call for the harmonisation of the conditions for parental leave and facilitate the reconciliation of work and maternity. however, in my view, such incentives should be based on the principle of voluntariness. for the reasons stated above, i could not support the motion and therefore abstained.
in writing. today we voted on a report on the right to parental leave at eu level, at least for a minimum duration. the aim is to introduce a system that would also motivate fathers to stay with their children for a period of time on parental leave without harming them in their jobs and when they return to work. i personally support this proposal, but only in the form of minimum harmonization. i believe that we have very high standards in the czech republic. i support a system that guarantees parents at least a minimum of rights and that is most beneficial to the children. i am also in favour of a system which allows flexibility in which parent stays on leave and i am also in favour of the possibility of choosing from a number of alternatives. i voted in favour of the report.
in writing. ‒ whatever the best length and amount of maternity or paternity leave, the report is an unacceptable interference with the social policies of the member states. i also don't agree with calls for compensation for same-sex parents to achieve work-life balance. we respect that a child has a father and a mother, but talking about same-sex parents is playing god. parents can only be a man and a woman.
in writing. i supported the resolution on the application of the parental leave directive, which also indicates in some points the possible directions for changes to this legislation. i agree with the recommendation to consider extending the minimum length of parental leave from 4 to 6 months by ensuring better coordination and accessibility of leave systems in the member states (maternity, paternity and parental leave) and with the call for a proposal for an eu directive on a minimum of two weeks of paternity leave. improvements to existing legislation should be sought that emphasise the importance of childcare while facilitating the reconciliation of family and working life for both parents.
in writing. ‒ i decided to abstain from voting on the report on the framework agreement on parental leave, which calls on the member states to better implement the common rules on minimum parental. this is because i believe that decisions in this area should be left to member states individually. while i fully agree that parental leave is a fundamental right and essential for mothers, fathers, children and society as a whole, the eu has no competence on the matter and conditions of parental leave should therefore be decided upon accordingly, at a national level.
in writing. - i did not support the resolution. i believe that this area should be left to the competence of the individual member states, which have different cultural traditions and social conditions for parental leave.
in writing. ‒ i support the report presented. i am convinced that social security is a matter for the member states. the political debate should also focus on non-legislative initiatives aimed at joint action with member states and civil society to highlight the role of parents and promote work-life balance. i believe that in order to achieve a work-life balance that is gender balanced, it is necessary to promote the individualisation of the right to leave and compensatory measures aimed at promoting the role of fathers. member states should aim to remove obstacles to returning to work after long parental leave in order to avoid exclusion from the labour market.

in writing. the results of the statistics tell us a number of interesting things. historically, slightly more boys have been born, but the mortality rate for boys is higher than for girls, and so the numbers are matched at a relatively early age. women in societies that do not live in extreme poverty, virtually everywhere in the world, have significantly longer life expectancies. in developed societies, in the so-called rich countries, we find that women are more educated than men. yet inequality in family care and related inequality in employment advancement still exists. this phenomenon also results in a higher risk of poverty for women than for men, across all age groups. in recent years, a new phenomenon of working poverty has been observed in a number of countries. the fact that even in some eu countries the minimum wage is below the social emergency threshold is a clear indictment of the current economic system. capitalism, which calls for free competition, is not able to solve the problem of poverty. despite all the measures, whether it be investments in social areas or legislative action to bring equality between men and women to the labour market, the increased vulnerability of women remains a fact. the resolution seeks to make a positive correction to this malfunctioning system. although it does not address the substance of the problem, the gue supports the motion for a resolution.

virtual currencies are certainly a very interesting innovation that allows citizens to be less dependent on banks and their often extortionate fees. however, we cannot turn a blind eye to the fact that this opens up the space for black market transactions: the laundering of the proceeds of crime, the financing of terrorism, tax fraud and tax evasion and other criminal activities. i believe that we need to call for appropriate regulation at eu level, which will not stifle innovation or unnecessarily increase costs at this early stage, but will seriously address the regulatory challenges that could arise from the expansion of the use of virtual currencies. i hope that the commission will also realise that it is on very thin ice and will not use the situation to increase its surveillance of citizens who very often want to escape the oppressive grip of the greedy banks.
i will not talk about the problem of destroying the european union, but i will talk about the problem of controlling the european projects. i have often pointed out in the ep, as a member of the cont committee, that many european projects are not treated transparently and that there is corruption and fraud in connection with european projects in my own country. however, the other extreme that i see when i go around the czech republic is that for one project that is checked, there are three or four other checks that look for whether there was a mistake in that project. i personally consider this situation to be unprecedented and i call on the commission to really think about whether each project needs to be checked four or five times.
we often deal with critical situations in the area of democracy, security and human rights in the european parliament. we should also see positive changes. for example, in taiwan a new president and government were democratically elected by the democratic progressive party, which is now succeeding the ruling kuomintang party. i attended the inauguration with the ep delegation, where the new president, tsai jing-wen, called for the unity of the taiwanese people and for a joint work on reform. taiwan has such a great opportunity for further democratic and economic growth and is interested in working with the eu and individual member states, and we should take advantage of this offer. the second good news is that we've seen the release of nadia savchenko. the ep has repeatedly called for her release, and we are very happy to see her back in the ep. ukraine and europe need brave people.

in the strategy for the internal market in goods and services, the commission made an open commitment to combating discrimination against consumers in the internal market. it is not only consumer centres that often receive complaints from consumers about unjustified differences in treatment based on nationality or residence. any form of discrimination against consumers on the basis of their nationality or country of residence is absolutely unacceptable to me and contrary to the very idea of the internal market. i therefore welcome the resolution's strong rejection of the current form of discrimination, both in and out of the electronic environment. the increasing importance of the digital agenda cannot lead us to lose focus on compliance and effective enforcement in the offline world. nor, unlike the commission, does the resolution limit the forms of discrimination to differences in prices, sales conditions or delivery options. i therefore call on the commission, if it is really serious about its commitment to combating discrimination, to respect the demand of this house and to carry out a thorough investigation of possible differences in the quality of products of the same brand and the same packaging distributed within the single market, which is another concrete example of consumer discrimination.
i supported this report, however unlike several of my predecessors i want to warn against virtual currencies being fully allowed into the financial system without any initial regulation. i think that the regulation of every human activity is, of course, unacceptable to me. on the other hand, the stability of the financial system and the ability to react to the negative effects that virtual currencies bring to the system, is the responsibility of the legislator, that is, our responsibility. the negatives that are described by all of us in the same way about virtual currencies are actually the legalization of the proceeds of crime and the high volatility that is associated with these virtual currencies and the speculative bubbles that can result in the collapse of the financial system. i therefore call for regulation to be made in advance.

in writing. ‒ digital cash has been part of the financial technologies we use today for a few years now, by significantly reducing the cost of transferring funds and increasing their availability. however, as this type of currency is still associated with considerable risks, i supported the report which deals specifically with the management of risks such as their high volatility, the formation of speculative bubbles or the absence of control structures. i believe that the technological documentation on the functioning of virtual currencies must become more transparent and that a proper legal framework should be developed, which is currently lacking. i therefore supported the recommendation that the european commission carry out a comprehensive analysis of digital cash and the new opportunities it offers in this context. at the same time, i would like to stress that consumer protection plays a very important role in this area. i therefore voted in favour of establishing cooperation between the commission, the member states and the representatives of this innovative financial sector, which must guarantee the provision of correct information. it is necessary to enable any consumer in the european internal market to make optimal decisions based on clear and unbiased information. i also supported the clause asking the european commission to amend the legislation to prevent these new technologies from being misused for money laundering or other black economy activities, including terrorist financing.
in writing. consumer confidence in a financial service provider, together with a high level of consumer protection in the event that that trust is not respected, are essential factors for a well-functioning and stable financial system. virtual currencies are a fast-developing technology that, like other novelties of the digital environment, is currently not subject to fixed and enforceable rules and is not subject to oversight. this, of course, entails a number of risks that need to be addressed appropriately. i therefore welcome the fact that this resolution not only highlights the potential benefits of virtual currencies, but in particular clearly identifies the areas that need to be addressed to ensure that virtual currencies are not used as a tool for fraud, theft, cybercrime or consumer deception. i am pleased that the resolution emphasises the importance of consumer awareness, transparency and trust in the use of virtual currencies and calls on the commission to develop concrete guidelines aimed at ensuring that users of virtual currencies are provided with correct, clear and complete information.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on virtual currencies, as i believe that this is a much needed step to address the emergence and growth of virtual currencies (vc) and their underlying technologies. virtual currencies offer both great opportunities by contributing positively to citizens’ welfare and economic development, including in the financial sector, but can also entail non-negligible risks such as their use for criminal purposes. i believe that this report has managed to present a responsible and balanced way of addressing virtual currencies, by avoiding over-regulation, allowing this new and still developing technology to reach its full potential, while at the same time taking precautionary measures to be able to regulate when necessary and deal with potential risks before they become systemic.
in writing. ‒ the european globalisation adjustment fund provides assistance to workers made redundant as a result of major structural changes in world trade linked to globalisation. in this case, the funds were released to the french company moryglobal, which operates in the fields of courier services, freight transport and the delivery of goods. the appropriations made available should provide dismissed workers with career counselling, training seminars and other support leading to a better position on the labour market. since the french authorities have given the necessary assurances regarding the use of the funds, i voted in favour of the report.
in writing. ‒ today we voted on a report on the mobilisation of the european globalisation adjustment fund, one of the instruments the eu has set up to provide additional support to workers who are affected by the consequences of major changes in the structure of world trade or the consequences of the global financial and economic crisis and to help them reintegrate into the labour market. france applied for assistance from this fund for the employees of moryglobal, which had to lay off over 2 500 workers as a result of globalisation, many of whom were already of retirement or pre-retirement age. i agree with the need for financial assistance, which is why i voted to release the corresponding funds from the european globalisation adjustment fund.
in writing. i voted in favour of the report on the mobilisation of the european globalisation adjustment fund in the event of mass redundancies at moryglobal in france. as europe faces a decline in physical production, which is being shifted to other continents due to globalisation, the need for truck transport is logically decreasing. this is precisely what happened to more than two thousand workers who should rightly have been granted aid of eur 5 million. these, in combination with appropriate national measures, can then help them to reintegrate into the labour market. i have supported the provision of assistance to workers in the form of counselling in the search for a new job, in the setting up of new businesses or in the creation of new training courses. it is important to note that this mass redundancy case has affected workers in the problematic 55-64 age group to a large extent. it is therefore necessary to start individual assistance as soon as possible in order to prevent the social exclusion of these citizens. i am pleased that the european parliament was able to agree to grant aid in a relatively short time. in conclusion, i would like to add that i believe that support for mass redundancies should be available to all europeans, regardless of their member state, as the positive and negative effects of globalisation are felt throughout the european union.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report as the rapporteur has made clear what the eu and the single market is all about, which is removing barriers to trade and growth in europe. europe must not be about over—regulation, but instead removing the outdated protectionism measures of the past. goods and services must be free to move across europe without running into unjustified national regulations. a statement saying that ‘this is how it has always been done’ is not a valid justification. we are a single market and we must act like it.
‒ more than 20 years after the creation of the single market, unjustified non-tariff barriers (ntbs) still affect trade and the free movement of goods and services between member states. ntbs are often motivated by protectionism, are associated with a disproportionate administrative burden and are a hindrance to a competitive market economy. the report asks the commission to present in 2016 a comprehensive overview of ntbs in the single market and an analysis of how to address them. the removal of non-tariff barriers would allow the untapped potential of the single market to be exploited, benefiting consumers, producers and traders alike. for these reasons, i voted in favour of the motion.
in writing. i voted against the motion. i agree, for example, with the first point, which i voted for separately, that 'the free movement of goods and services continues to be restricted by non-tariff barriers such as unjustified national technical regulations and regulatory and non-regulatory requirements imposed on products, service providers and conditions of service provision or bureaucracy'. but i couldn't agree with the bill as a whole because of the proposals calling for further regulation of banking, the digital market, or the establishment of retail stores.
in writing. ‒ today we voted on a report on non-tariff barriers to the single market. the report criticises the persistence of such obstacles in the single market, but it no longer addresses the other side of the coin, namely the fact that the single market does not only bring benefits but also imposes greater demands on smaller countries with weaker economies and has rather negative effects. in the report, the rapporteur also criticises the complexity of the current vat system. i am afraid that this will not lead to the unification of vat systems in the next stage. because i do not consider the report balanced, i abstained in the final vote.
in writing. i supported the report on non-tariff barriers in the single market, which among other things points to the complexity of vat rules as one of the biggest non-tariff barriers. i believe that this obstacle could be removed by introducing a single vat office, which would also support smes in their cross-border activities. it should be stressed that many national administrative procedures also lead to unjustified non-tariff barriers. i see the solution in the wider use of e-governance and in the prioritisation of interoperability and digital signatures and in general in the provision of wider and more accessible digital services to citizens and businesses and in facilitating cross-border cooperation and interoperability of public administrations. at the same time, however, the use of e-government should not exclude alternative ways of accessing information or put at a disadvantage citizens who do not have access to digital services.
‒ the purpose of this resolution is to identify non-tariff barriers which prevent the full development of the internal market. in the context of the ongoing debate on so-called better regulation, however, i consider it very important to distinguish consistently between the attempt to eliminate unjustified or discriminatory regulatory measures for society and the attempt to dilute existing rules to reduce the level of consumer or employee rights. i therefore welcome the fact that, thanks to the contribution of the social democrats, the resolution does not in any way affect the right of the member states to regulate and pursue legitimate public policy objectives aimed specifically at protecting consumers, workers or the environment. i am also very pleased to have succeeded in getting the resolution to include the provision that although the widespread use of egovernment is seen as an important tool, especially for businesses, egovernment cannot exclude alternative ways of accessing information or put citizens who do not have access to digital services at a disadvantage.
in writing. ‒ more than 20 years after first launching the single market, trade and free movement of goods and services between states in europe, there are still numerous non-tariff barriers (ntbs) that hamper both consumers and business, particularly smes and start-ups. ntbs include heavy compliance costs between member states, unjustified national technical rules or unnecessary administrative requirements. i voted in favour of the resolution, which will look into ways to identify and remove the ntbs that are not justified, and make sure that, in cases where ntbs are justified, information on differing requirements is clear, accessible and user-friendly. i am confident that by ensuring a more uniform regulatory environment, making full use of digitisation, and guaranteeing mutual recognition where harmonisation is not possible, we can unleash the full potential of the single market and boost europe’s competitiveness.
in writing. ‒ i support the european parliament's report because the creation of the single market is a major achievement, achieved only by working together to remove trade barriers across the european union. i believe that just as customs barriers have been removed, non-customs barriers should also be removed. the removal of non-tariff barriers will help businesses in the eu, but the main beneficiaries of the removal of these barriers will be consumers. i believe there are two main steps that need to be taken. better and more consistent enforcement of existing rules and a change in member states' mindsets that would lead to a shift away from increasingly used protectionist measures and towards a more full opening of domestic markets.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report as whole because the single market is the heart of the european union. the commission’s strategy is another step towards its completion and should be welcomed. but during the voting, i voted against the references to the ‘made in’ article of the consumer products safety regulation. this important piece of legislation has been blocked for too long over this one point, especially when the inclusion of such a requirement would have no benefits for product safety. it is time we as a parliament accept that it needs to be removed, at least from this regulation, so that we can move forward and finally enter trilogues with the council.
in writing. in an own-initiative report, the european parliament presented a strategy to improve the single market. although the single market has seen positive developments in recent years, there is still room for improvement. for example, the eu should aim to reduce administrative burdens, get rid of unnecessary legislation, while ensuring a high level of standards for consumers, workers, health and the environment. the report also supported the commission's commitment to tackle the lack of tax coordination within the eu, in particular with regard to vat reform or cross-border crowdfunding. a functioning single market is, i believe, one of the eu's greatest assets, and i was happy to support the report calling for many improvements.

in writing. i supported the single market strategy report, which sets out new directions for the development of the internal market in the light of the identified gaps and shortcomings in its functioning. for example, the possibility of introducing a simplified vat approach for the same category of goods in the area of e-commerce should be considered. in practice, this would be new rules on the place of supply as regards vat on digital services. i support the commission's intention to use cosme funds to finance information campaigns targeting young innovative smes. smes in particular would also certainly welcome the commission's initiative to harmonise insolvency proceedings across the eu, from which they could expect to benefit from shorter proceedings and lower costs.
in writing. i supported today's european parliament resolution on the single market strategy. this document responds to the european commission's plan for the single market and gives the european parliament the opportunity to highlight some specific issues that it considers important. i believe that such a theme is above all one of support for smes, whose specificities must be taken into account in the individual future steps, starting with not burdening them with unnecessary administrative work and ending with actively supporting them through tailor-made provisions in the individual areas of the single market. however, i consider it equally important to reflect in further considerations the position of consumers, who should only be prevented from using services in the single market by genuinely well-founded obstacles based on the principle of the public interest. with the increased mobility of european citizens, there is also a growing legitimate demand for the possibility of using services across borders or of benefiting from uniform consumer protection rules.
in writing. ‒ despite positive developments, the single market is still underperforming in most areas, and europe’s competitiveness is suffering from it. this resolution proposes a new strategic approach to achieve a better integration of the single market, which is why i voted in favour of it. europe should exploit the full potential of digitalisation and innovation, create a more start-up and risk friendly environment, but also ensure that legislation, namely in the area of taxation, is harmonised across member states. lowering administrative burdens and compliance costs on businesses, especially smes, and repealing unnecessary legislation, while continuing to ensure high standards of consumer, employee, health and environmental protection, is key to delivering the objectives of the strategy.

in writing. ‒ today we voted on a report on the world health organisation (who) protocol on the elimination of illicit trade in tobacco products, in which parliament gives its consent to the conclusion of this protocol. the who protocol aims to eliminate all forms of illicit trade in tobacco products. illicit trade is defined as any practice or conduct prohibited by law relating to the manufacture, distribution, purchase or sale of tobacco products. the protocol should also apply to supply chains. it focuses on combating counterfeit tobacco products or money laundering derived from the illicit trade in those products. i voted yes.
in writing. i supported the council's decision to conclude this protocol. the protocol to eliminate illicit trade in tobacco products was signed in december 2013 as part of the world health organisation framework convention on tobacco control. the protocol aims to eliminate all forms of illicit trade, specifically targeting supply chains through a series of measures at governmental levels. it establishes a global regime for monitoring the movement of tobacco supplies and a central hub for sharing this information, which should prevent the smuggling of goods. the protocol contains a series of specific measures (definition of offences, liability, payments, treatment of confiscated goods, etc.). the protocol also emphasises the incompatibility of the interests of the tobacco industry with public health interests.
in writing. ‒ illicit trade in tobacco products, in particular cigarette smuggling is a criminal activity seriously threatening public health and causing huge losses of revenue to the eu in terms of unpaid taxes and customs duties. estimates indicate more than eur 10 billion losses of revenue annually to the eu and member states, in other words this means that roughly one cigarette out of 10 is sold illegally. i voted in favour of ratifying the protocol to eliminate illicit trade in tobacco products (fctc protocol) of the who framework convention on tobacco control (fctc) as it is both a necessary step to improve public health, as well as to help fight illicit tobacco trade, tax evasion and organised crime. the protocol’s main suggestion is to make the supply chain of tobacco, tobacco products and manufacturing equipment secure by establishing a global tracking and tracing system, and increasing international cooperation in customs matters.

in writing. ‒ 17 member states decided to introduce a system of so-called enhanced cooperation (including the czech republic) with the aim of bringing clear rules to govern the property relations of international married couples and registered partnerships. the aim is to provide such couples, whose number is constantly increasing, with greater legal certainty. it is clear that in the event of divorce or death of a partner, a person living in an international union, of which there are some 16 million in the eu, may find himself in a difficult situation, faced with an uncertain legal situation. the purpose of the motions is, for example, to clarify the jurisdiction of the national court, the applicable law, to facilitate the enforcement and recognition of judgments, etc. i believe this will make life easier for couples and save additional costs of up to eur 400 million per year. i therefore voted in favour of the proposal.
in writing. i supported the european parliament's recommendation to approve enhanced cooperation between member states on the property rights of international couples. i am also pleased that the czech republic has acted actively when it applied to the commission to participate in this enhanced cooperation. the increase in the number of marriages and registered partnerships with an international element is an undeniable reality of the union today, to which the increasing mobility of students and workers across the union contributes. in 2007 alone, there were 300 000 international marriages in the eu and some 41 000 registered partnerships had an international element in terms of assets. although the settlement of assets presents daily practical challenges, there are no union rules in this area yet. for example, international couples cannot determine with certainty which court has jurisdiction to settle their property or which law will govern a particular property situation. the enhanced cooperation is intended to create a clear legal framework for almost 16 million international couples in the participating member states. the property relations of international couples will be dealt with in a comprehensive manner, under one applicable law and by one authority. this avoids parallel proceedings, conflicting court decisions or high costs of proceedings. at the same time, enhanced cooperation does not restrict the sovereignty of the state to establish or not to establish the institution of registered partnership. he only counts on it where it already exists.
in writing. i have supported today the european parliament's endorsement of enhanced cooperation on the property rights of international couples, since this is an endorsement of enhanced cooperation between member states which have concluded such cooperation on the council's territory, and such enhanced cooperation does not in any way bind non-participating states to the procedure to be followed by member states participating in such enhanced cooperation.
in writing. ‒ in times of intense cooperation and exchange between all member states of the eu, it seems only natural to adjust the legal rights on property regimes for international couples. since it was impossible to reach an agreement between all member states within a reasonable period, an agreement was now reached between 18 member states of the union wishing to establish enhanced cooperation: belgium, bulgaria, the czech republic, germany, greece, spain, france, croatia, italy, cyprus, luxembourg, malta, the netherlands, austria, portugal, slovenia, finland and sweden. this agreement will authorise enhanced cooperation between these member states in the area of jurisdiction, applicable law and the recognition and enforcement of decisions on the property regimes of international couples, covering both matters of matrimonial property regimes and the property consequences of registered partnerships.

in writing. ‒ illicit trade in tobacco products, in particular cigarette smuggling is a criminal activity seriously threatening public health and causing huge losses of revenue to the eu in terms of unpaid taxes and customs duties. estimates indicate more than eur 10 billion in lost revenue annually to the eu and member states. this is why i voted in favour of the provisions on obligations related to judicial cooperation in criminal matters and the definition of criminal offences of the protocol to eliminate illicit trade in tobacco products to the world health organisation’s framework convention on tobacco control. through this provision, special efforts will be made to encourage and enhance international cooperation, valid information sharing, technical and law enforcement cooperation, mutual legal and administrative assistance. it will establish offences, address liability and seizure payments as well and the disposal of confiscated products.
mr president, i want to emphasize that i voted for both reports on financial instruments in the trading market. it is essential to me that the european union continues to move towards an effective internal market, that the internal market functions regardless of whether member states put additional obstacles in its way. i firmly believe that the european union will push for a review of financial instruments in the trading market.
in writing. - i voted yes. this amendment to the directive postpones the effective date of financial market regulation to 3 january 2018. the commission is asking for time to be able to prepare the infrastructure to process all the data it wants from financial institutions. i am generally against the new regulations that the financial markets directive 2014/65 introduces. i see the deferral as a chance to reject the directive altogether.
in writing. i supported the extension of the applicability of the entire mifid ii rulebook until 3 january 2018, which should be sufficient time for esma, ncas and operators to put in place the infrastructure for data collection, reporting and calculation of transparency thresholds. i am convinced that this will avoid the risk of confusion and unnecessary costs for the parties concerned due to the phased implementation. building different infrastructures simultaneously rather than in stages makes the whole process cost-effective. this will, for example, avoid situations where investment firms executing orders would have to introduce organisational requirements or rules governing the conduct of business in stages, which would be complicated, costly and expensive.
in writing. ‒ in april 2014, in the wake of the financial crisis, we believed to have adopted a cornerstone of european financial market regulation to better shield the union from another crisis. mifid and mifir, collectively referred to as mifid, were supposed to increase the transparency of markets and improve their oversight for businesses and consumers. while i find it regrettable that, two years later, we need to delay the implementation date of this important package after an already unusually long period of work by one year, i am aware of the complexities and technical challenges this package represents, which is why i voted in favour of the delay. it is more important to lay out good, workable rules than to rush things too quickly and to disturb the good functioning of the market.
