in writing. - i voted yes. this amendment to the directive postpones the effective date of financial market regulation to 3 january 2018. the commission is asking for time to be able to prepare the infrastructure to process all the data it wants from financial institutions. i am generally against the new regulations that the financial markets directive 2014/65 introduces. i see the deferral as a chance to reject the directive altogether.
in writing. ‒ package transactions enable investment firms and their clients to better manage their risks, with the price of each component of the package transaction reflecting the overall risk profile of the package rather than the prevailing market price of each component. i voted in favour of deferring the implementation of the specific circumstances in which pre-trade transparency should not apply to package transactions, nor to any individual component of such transactions. while i am fully supportive of transparency measures in the financial sector, package transactions can take various forms, and it is important to consider those specificities when applying the transparency regime.
in writing. ‒ having verified the credibility and suitability of rimantas šadžius by the committee on budgets and having recommended him to the members as a credible candidate in view of the requirements laid down in the tfeu, i voted in favour of his membership of the court of auditors.
in writing. ‒ the european court of auditors operates as a college of 28 members, with one nominee for each eu member state. initial nominations are followed by a hearing in the european parliament (in the committee on budgetary control, of which i am a member). i have unambiguously supported the candidacy of mr shadijus, both on the basis of the hearing and on the basis of the written replies to the supplementary questions of the members of the committee on budgetary control. i am convinced that he is an excellent expert and i am pleased to be able to work more closely with him as a member of the committee on budgetary control in the coming term.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of nominating of rimantas šadžius as a member of the court of auditors as suggested by the committee on budgetary control. i trust that mr šadžius’s professional experience as a minister of finance in lithuania from 2007 to 2008, and his second term as minister of finance in the cabinet of algirdas butkevičius since 2012 will qualify him to deliver on the requirements of this position.
in writing. ‒ i abstained from a vote on this report as it included some of provision not directly linked, in my view, to development policy itself and its coherence with other union’s policies. it mainly called for greater harmonisation of migration and asylum policies with international partners and single common asylum and immigration policies within the eu. also, i could not agree with the statement that trade liberalisation is not positive for a poverty eradication and has negative effects on sustainable development. i believe exactly the opposite, and although i am convinced that there is a constant need for policy coherence in development area, i could not support this report.
in writing. i was very pleased to support the european parliament resolution on the eu report on policy coherence for development for 2015. i'm glad we're focusing on sustainable development these days. it tells me that maybe we'll finally be able to solve the problems that we're all facing in a holistic way, without the rose-colored glasses. for example, the final text includes a point stating that: 'trade liberalisation is not in itself positive in terms of reducing poverty and inequality, as it could have negative consequences for sustainable development'. translated into colloquial english, this means that if developing countries open their markets to multinational corporations, they run a significant risk of being robbed, and poverty and inequality in society will increase as slums are built away from luxury housing. i also appreciated the fact that the resolution calls on the eu and its member states to continue to actively engage with the un human rights council to hold transnational corporations accountable for human rights violations. but we have a lot of work to do to rectify the fact that 1.5 billion people still live in poverty, without proper health care, education and living standards. this is a step in the right direction.
in writing. the report criticises developing countries for using tax incentives and tax breaks to attract or retain investors, leading to harmful tax competition and a race to the bottom, while celebrating subsidies and cohesion policies. i think we need to give developing countries the freedom to cut taxes and attract investors instead of teaching them to draw on subsidies. on the other hand, i consider tax competition to be healthy. the report also calls for new taxes: 'it is necessary to consider innovative and diversified sources of funding such as a financial transaction tax, a carbon tax, a surcharge on air tickets, rents from natural resources'. i'm against the introduction of these new taxes.
in writing. ‒ today we voted on the report on policy coherence for development for 2015. the report makes a number of key points with which i fully agree, such as the fact that impact assessments are an important tool for achieving policy coherence for development, but that there are not too many development and developing country impact assessments. with reference to the 2030 agenda, the ambitious goals set out are recalled, such as food security for the whole world, the total eradication of hunger and the elimination of all forms of malnutrition. the impact of eu policies on developing countries, for example in agriculture, trade or energy, also needs to be considered. i also welcome the commitment to promote sustainable and agroecological practices. i voted to accept the report.
in writing. ‒ i supported a report which takes a comprehensive approach to development policy issues. developing countries should be assisted in strengthening their capacity in tax and financial administration and public financial management and in combating illicit financial flows. we should ensure that multinational companies pay taxes in the countries where value is obtained or created. in this regard, the establishment of a new intergovernmental body under the auspices of the un to deal with international tax cooperation could be useful. it is the eu's task and responsibility to seek to deepen international cooperation in tax matters.
in writing. ‒ the scale of the current migration crisis has shown us just how far a situation can go, which is primarily caused by the lack of development in the surrounding world and its ignorance by developed countries. i therefore voted in favour of the 2015 report on policy coherence for development. it is necessary that the european union pursue its policies in a manner consistent with its commitments in the past with regard to development aid and assistance. it is now clear that the commitments made so far have not been sufficient and that it would be appropriate to develop new development concepts and objectives that do not exclusively follow the original paradigm of cooperation. it is necessary to involve local and regional authorities, expert groups and civil society organisations even more in the process of providing assistance. furthermore, to ensure deeper coordination between the european union institutions and the member states. it is crucial that european countries remember their commitment to provide 0.7% of their gnp in official development assistance and ensure the exchange of good cooperation practices. i also supported the systematic assessment of the impact of other european union policies on the food and other security of developing countries. it is not possible, for example, that poorly designed biofuel policies in modern countries endanger the livelihoods of the poorest on other continents, who are also more vulnerable to global climate change.
in writing. as a social democrat, i decided to support the european commission's fifth biennial report on policy cohesion for development (pcd), which was published in august 2015. it is a very important instrument that ensures a harmonious development in all parts of the european union at a similar level. it is a very important concept that takes advantage of the solidarity between the rich eu countries and the poorer eu countries so that there are no big differences in economic development. the ep resolution on the 2016 mff analyses and formulates concrete recommendations on five priority areas (trade and finance, food security, climate change, migration and security). the rapporteur nevertheless suggests that attention should be paid to the eu's external policy, which i agree with in principle, but any new policy orientation for the coming period should be seen in a comprehensive way so that solving a problem in one area does not create a problem in another. all eu policies depend on the budget the eu has at its disposal. i am convinced that in the current circumstances and with the growing demands for european solutions to a number of parallel crises, it will be necessary to proceed with an overall increase in the eu budget.
in writing. i supported the european parliament's report on the eu's 2015 report on policy coherence for development, as it addresses the important topic of policy coherence in general to promote sustainable development, and also because it mentions the importance of development aid in the context of the current migration crisis. development assistance is now a tool to tackle the migration crisis in the long term, as it is clear that only the comprehensive development of the countries that are now the source countries of migration will ensure that the numbers of migrants gradually decrease and that these people find a safe and meaningful life in their own countries. achieving this objective requires, in particular, that development aid is not only humanitarian aid but also, and increasingly, investment that leads to further development in the countries receiving development aid.
in writing. ‒ the 2030 sustainable development agenda represents a unique opportunity to review the coherence of our development strategies to ensure that they actually improve people’s lives. while i appreciate and agree with many of the proposals made in this report, i however decided to abstain because there are some elements that i cannot compromise on. while it is crucial that we agree on a holistic and efficient migration and asylum system, i do not believe that developing a single common system is at the moment feasible. furthermore, i don’t believe in using instruments such as a financial transaction tax, a carbon tax, an air ticket levy, rents from natural resources as sustainable sources of financing. finally, if the market rules are fully respected, i do believe that trade liberalisation is a very efficient tool to combat poverty and encourage development, unlike what the report states.
in writing. i abstained because i have a number of important points to make about the report. the proposal concerns, for example, the harmonisation of migration policy, the gender dimension, the financial transaction tax or the involvement of the un in tax controls - all of which are to be addressed primarily in the individual member states concerned.
in writing. ‒ i have decided to support the report presented because i believe that trade and direct finance are one of the main priorities for policy coherence and a pathway to sustainable development. however, it must be stressed that trade liberalisation is not in itself positive in terms of reducing poverty and inequality. i am of the opinion that private funding for individual climate action cannot replace public funding.
in writing. ‒ the new alliance for food security and nutrition aims to improve food security and nutrition by helping 50 million people in sub-saharan africa to lift themselves out of poverty by 2020, and that is why i voted in favour of it. this is of course also important for the future of europe in many ways. africa should be as self-sufficient as possible. the situation is complicated, however, by the prospect of further waves of migration in the future, due to global warming. africa is becoming increasingly dry, limiting the ability to survive in certain areas. in addition, the continent, like the world, should meet the un sustainable development goals by 2030, in particular the goals related to the elimination of hunger and poverty. as a member of the committee on the environment, public health and food safety, i appreciate that the report 'urgently calls on g8 member states not to promote genetically modified crops in africa'. i wonder how some g8 countries, especially the us, are going to handle this, when the eu is trying to impose gmos at all costs, and fortunately, the eu has the power to oppose. but what chance do states facing economic instability and significant social problems have against such a powerful lobby?
in writing. on the one hand, the report calls for the eu to remove tariffs on african products, which i agree with. on the other hand, the report criticizes the tax incentives that african countries provide. i think we should leave it to the african countries to decide what taxes they're going to have. the report also calls on member states to ensure that eu-based companies doing business in africa apply a 'social responsibility policy' in africa, and ensure that 'environmental, social, land, labour and human rights and the highest standards of transparency' are respected, and that 'local african businesses' are supported. this is something that our government cannot provide, and the enforcement of african law must be provided by african governments. for these very serious reasons, i voted against.
in writing. ‒ today we voted on a report on the objectives of the new alliance for food and nutrition security. the question of nutrition is and will be of the utmost importance. it is estimated that by 2050, 70% of the world's population will live in cities and that the issue of nutrition will still require a response at both global and regional levels. the new alliance aims to improve this by helping 50 million people in sub-saharan africa to lift themselves out of poverty by 2020. investment in smallholder farming has been severely neglected in africa in recent years and this needs to be corrected. i also agree that food security in developing countries depends to a large extent on the sustainable use of natural resources. improving access to water and intensifying nutrition education and sharing best practice strategies are needed. the report contains a number of ideas with which i cannot but identify, which is why i voted in favour of the report.
in writing. ‒ i share the view of the report's authors that every effort must be made to improve nutrition, food security and the fight against hunger in developing countries. the data show that stability is higher and emigration rates are lower in areas where food security is based on healthy and vibrant soils and productive agricultural ecosystems that are resilient to climate change. ways must be found to move from over-reliance on food imports to ensuring reliable domestic food production, with preference given to local crops that meet nutritional requirements. i believe that whatever the eu and individual member states' attitude to the cultivation of gm crops in the eu, we should not prevent the cultivation of gm crops in developing countries facing food shortages.
in writing. ‒ i am pleased to see such positive efforts being made by the european union in restructuring nafsn to further promote human rights, reduce poverty, and cooperate effectively with local farmers and families in sub-saharan africa to mitigate the inadequacies which currently exist. this motion encapsulates the spirit of ‘true’ external affairs and highlights honest international cooperation between states. the pivot from a modern, business-oriented approach to wiser investments in family farming and agro—ecology clearly underlines this. as a result of such focus, we are able to move in line with previous agreements on climate change and sustainable agriculture as well as diversify crop production, increase living standards and develop rural areas – effectively reducing poverty. i will echo the acknowledgement of gender equality in the agricultural sector as integral to development – socially, economically, and politically. i would go even further and state gender equality as one of the most important issues in the fight against poverty as it utilises the full potential of women. that is why i support this motion and welcome even more progress in supporting our developing partners in sub-saharan africa.
in writing. ‒ the european parliament voted on the new alliance for food and nutrition security. this initiative was launched in 2012 under the auspices of the g8 as a public-private partnership to improve food security and nutrition in sub-saharan africa. the eu is involved in the project as coordinator for malawi and côte d'ivoire. food and nutrition security is certainly a laudable goal, but the project itself has a number of shortcomings that this resolution is addressing. the european parliament, for example, warns against a repeat of the so-called green revolution, i.e. increasing productivity through the use of chemical fertilizers, mechanization and monocultures, as this approach can have serious environmental impacts. it also calls for more support for small farmers to prevent the interests of big business and land grabs from being overridden. however, in paragraph 72 the resolution 'urgently requests that g8 member states do not support genetically modified crops in africa'. i consider this export of ideologisation of a professional problem beyond the eu's borders to be unacceptable. nor does the eu have a strict ban on the cultivation of genetically modified crops. that's why i didn't support the resolution as a whole.
in writing. ‒ when it was launched in 2012, the aim of the new alliance for food security and nutrition in africa (nafsn) was to improve food security and nutrition in sub-saharan africa by leveraging private investment in agriculture. however, monoculture, mechanisation, biotechnology, dependence on fertilisers, long distribution channels and the production of export crops have proven to be harmful to the poorest communities and pose a risk to the environment. i voted in favour of this report, as i agree that, if we want to make it a genuine instrument of support for family farming and local economies in sub-saharan africa, we need to invest in a model of agriculture which is sustainable, pro-smallholder farming and pro-women, and which unlocks the potential of domestic and regional markets. only if we manage to do that will we realistically be able help 50 million people in sub-saharan africa out of poverty by 2020.
in writing. ‒ i support this report and appreciate the fact that the new alliance is committed to promoting growth based on agriculture. it also focuses on supporting smallholder farmers and helping to alleviate poverty, hunger and malnutrition. the new alliance should limit the use of chemical fertilizers and pesticides as much as possible, given their health and environmental impacts on local communities. all funding should be as transparent as possible. i am personally in favour of donors focusing their efforts on supporting education, training and technical advice for farmers. in addition to encouraging private investment, public investment in african agriculture needs to be revived. i prefer innovation in agroecology to increase food security and reduce poverty and hunger. however, these measures must go hand in hand with the protection of biodiversity and respect for indigenous knowledge and innovation.
in writing. the report calls for mandatory country-by-country accounting as part of the 'fight against tax avoidance and tax evasion'. i see in this a continuing effort by western eu states to prevent companies from taxing in the czech republic. the uniform accounting standards and mandatory reporting are a step towards uniform corporate taxation and tax shifting to countries with high corporate tax rates at the expense of the czech republic.
in writing. ‒ i am of the opinion that only simple accounting rules can be effectively implemented by users and controlled by supervisors. in this context, the g20 call for simplification of accounting standards for financial instruments and for a uniform approach to the international application of valuation standards in cooperation with supervisors can be recalled. given that most companies are small and medium-sized enterprises (smes), the commission should assess the possibility of developing common, high-quality and simplified accounting standards for smes.
in writing. ‒ international standards in accounting and auditing are essential for the efficient functioning of the internal market and of the capital markets. they strengthen accountability by reducing the information gap between investors and companies, protect investment, bring transparency and allow stakeholders to make informed economic decisions. this is why i voted in favour of the report, which assesses the application of these standards in the eu 10 years after their endorsement. i am particularly supportive of the commission’s intention to possibly develop common high-quality and simplified accounting standards for smes. i also believe that an impact assessment for every new accounting standard or change of a current accounting standard would be very useful. finally, i agree that parliament should have an active role in setting and implementing these standards.
in writing. i decided to abstain in the vote on the european parliament resolution on eu cooperation with the un and the african union in peacekeeping operations. i believe that it is of course true that peacekeeping operations are a form of crisis response and are intended to prevent armed conflict, restore, maintain or build peace, promote peace agreements and address complex emergencies and problems caused by failing or weak states, and that the aim of peacekeeping operations is to help create a stable, secure and more prosperous environment in the long term, but the resolutions ignore the fact that in the past, great peacekeeping missions have not been successful at all in terms of long-term stability and peace. i agree in principle with many of the demands in the minority report, such as that the responsibility for protection mechanism should not be used as a pretext for military intervention, that multinational companies and foreign powers should immediately end the plundering of natural resources and that reparations should be paid, that nato should withdraw from the african continent, that the merging of civilian and military capabilities should be stopped and that eu cooperation with nato and its interventions should be terminated, and that there should be a clear separation of the eu from the nato alliance. this does not change the fact that many countries on the african continent are on the brink of civil war and the eu must not stand by or abandon instruments that help to resolve conflicts peacefully.
in writing. i do not agree with the call in this report for member states to help train african armies. if france, for example, is interested in training or financing african armies, let it do so within its competence, but there is no reason to challenge the czech republic to do so. i agree with the report that open borders are one of the main factors in the spread of terrorism in africa. it is a pity that the governing meps do not understand the same thing in the case of europe. i disagree with the challenge to 'including women among mission staff as well as gender advisers'. it's unfortunate if some africans don't treat women nicely, but the inclusion of gender advisors in military missions doesn't seem to be making things better.
in writing. ‒ i am glad to see that this motion reiterates the importance of cooperation between the european union, african union, and the united nations – an essential tri—partnership for tackling the many trends which have emerged in the past decade. one very concerning trend is the rise of terrorist and insurgent groups in somalia, nigeria, and the sahel—sahara region, which has come to threaten the stability and sovereignty of surrounding states. they have taken advantage of porous borders and ungoverned areas to expand their control, making the importance of investment in conflict prevention and peace support operations (psos) vital to building african capabilities and accomplishing the 2030 agenda for sustainable development. along these lines, i believe we must continue to stress the importance of efficient and coordinated responses between the three international organisations, utilising the full potential of all resources – rather than increased funding as a solution – to effectively carry out any and all operations. i support this motion and look forward to seeing more strides made in this direction.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the european parliament's own-initiative report on eu cooperation with the un and the african union (au) on peacekeeping missions, as i believe that we need to reflect also at european level on the quality of the current cooperation between the eu, the un and the au. cooperation with the au in particular deserves a great deal of attention today, because without cooperation with african countries, the major problems of our time, such as migration or terrorism, cannot be satisfactorily solved. these complex problems need to be addressed in a comprehensive manner using all instruments of international cooperation. the report makes it clear that the focus should be on compliance with funding rules and on avoiding duplication of effort between the institutions involved, but this does not mean that the eu cannot use, for example, its representation in african countries or offer cooperation to individual states or the au directly from the eu's position in order to achieve common objectives.
in writing. ‒ the security landscape in africa has changed dramatically in the last decade, with the emergence of terrorist and insurgent groups in somalia, nigeria, and the sahel—sahara region, which is why it was essential to review our peace support operations strategies. i voted in favour of this report, which evaluates the eu’s engagement with the un and the african union in peace support operations, as useful step allowing us to focus this review. for one, i am convinced that we should support african countries to build their own capacities, instead of them relying on external ones. i also agree with the report’s suggestion to increase the coordination between all actors, in order to tackle the challenges more efficiently and avoid unnecessary duplication. more investment in conflict prevention is also necessary. furthermore, while the lack of funds is not a problem, it is essential that we achieve better targeted funding. finally, sexual abuse by un personnel is highly unacceptable and must absolutely be halted if we want to restore confidence in our peace operations.
in writing. ‒ i supported the report in the final, even though i don't agree with all the points. but in general, i think it is very important that initiatives to promote the peace process in african countries are as vocal as possible.
in writing. i have abstained on the report. the text includes a proposal which envisages a legislative solution to the problem, i.e. new eu regulations, which i do not consider to be a happy decision at the moment. i'm all for minimal or necessary interference in business in general. in this respect, i was satisfied with the text adopted by the committee. i do not want to underestimate the problems of smaller suppliers and primary producers, they should certainly be addressed. i see their joint activities at a pan-european level, such as the supply chain initiative, as an appropriate way to do this. they are better able to establish equivalence between suppliers than eu directives or regulations.
in writing. the issue of preventing unfair commercial practices is extremely important and serious. the strategic importance of the food supply chain is reflected in the fact that it employs more than 47 million people in the eu and accounts for around 7% of gross value added. in my view, the main obstacle to finding a common concept of a union solution is the wide current coverage of the problem in national legislation, which differs significantly in scope and in the way it is dealt with. i therefore consider it necessary that coordination should allow for freedom of choice of means of redress in the light of the existing legal arrangements of the member states. i am against the adoption of further eu legislation and i think it is effective to address this issue at national level. that's why i abstained.
in writing. unfair trading practices between enterprises in the food chain are often reduced to supplier-customer relationships of transnational trading chains. the fact remains that the public does indeed consider these relationships to be unfair, but unfair practices certainly include misleading country of origin labelling and other tricks. in many eu countries, retail chains are important players, often representing over 50% of the food market, and it is therefore important to identify unfair practices and, in line with the proposed procedures, to take steps to contribute to predictability and compliance with agreements, including risk liability and the elimination of unjustified requirements. it is known that some large companies are reluctant to provide written contracts to suppliers, seek to delay invoice payments or require long maturities. the effort is often to force the return of unsold goods, payments for so-called cataloging, or other unfair practices. typically, the supplier's forced share of the seller's discount shares. the abovementioned and other practices have been going on for many years and it is good that the ep is addressing these issues. only increased attention by the eu institutions and national states can make progress in eliminating this negative phenomenon, which has brought with it the predatory rise of large retail chains. the report suggests possible ways of improving the current situation, and i therefore fully support it.
in writing. when voting on the report on unfair trading practices with the proposed amendments by czesław siekierski, i voted in favour of the motion. i believe that unfair trading practices between large retail chains and small and medium-sized suppliers and farmers are a big problem in the eu in general. this behaviour not only results in unfair conditions for suppliers, who are often forced to sell their products below price and face further infringements of their rights. but the other consequences of these practices are poor working conditions for farmers, a lower quality food supply for consumers and food waste. the proposal therefore aims to ensure fair and transparent trade relations between manufacturers, suppliers and retail chains. this should ensure fair returns for farmers, a wide choice of food for consumers and at the same time reduce food waste. at present, the only legislation in the eu that exists is one that protects consumers against unfair commercial practices. however, there is no legislation at union level to ensure protection for the individual parts of the supply chain. it is therefore essential that the eu adopts legislation uniformly and effectively to combat unfair trading practices in all member states.
in writing. ‒ if traders pressure suppliers to lower prices, have long payment periods, withdraw from supplier contracts without giving reasons, they are usually entitled to do so, just as suppliers are entitled to find other customers. if anyone thinks that traders are abusing their power, it's a matter of trade law and enforcement in individual member states, and the eu has nothing to say about it.
in writing. ‒ today we voted on a report that addresses an issue that perhaps all of us have encountered in our daily lives, namely unfair trading practices in the food chain. these unfair practices cost suppliers between eur 30 and 40 trillion a year. these undesirable practices are known across the eu, which is why 20 member states have adopted legislation to combat these undesirable phenomena. i share the view that the fight against these undesirable practices, which have a negative impact on the most important thing, namely the health of consumers, should be regulated at european level, provided that the protection standards in the member states are not reduced in any way. that is why i supported the report.
in writing. i did not support the report on unfair trading practices because, in my view, it goes too far in regulating the contractual relationships in the food supply chain. i am of the opinion that intervention in market relations should only take place where there is evidence that those market relations are distorted and where it is really necessary. that's not the case in my opinion. i do not want an eu legal framework that dictates to food business operators the conditions under which they can enter into contracts. in effect, this means favouring one party to the contract over the other, and i consider this conceptually unhealthy.
in writing. unfair trading practices in the food or other supply chain can generally be considered to be unfair practices unilaterally used by one trading partner towards another. although it is not easy to assess this phenomenon in all contexts, statistics and market analyses show that these practices are also quite common in the eu and take many forms, which have often been felt by companies in the czech republic. these may include unilateral or retroactive changes to contractual terms, flat-rate fees that companies charge suppliers for being placed on a supplier list (pay to stay) or late payments, even for months. we must now take action. given that the effectiveness of self-regulatory mechanisms can be rightly doubted in this case, the report supports regulation at union level, which should lead to the proper functioning of markets and fair and transparent relationships between all actors in the supply chain.
in writing. ‒ the as the social democrats' shadow rapporteur, i supported this report because it gives a comprehensive picture of the situation in the food chain and at the same time calls on the commission to take concrete measures to redress the current market situation. unfair trading practices are a long-standing and serious problem affecting all parts of the supply chain. i also supported the amendments of the committee on agriculture and rural development because i agree with the provision that unfair trading practices can only be curbed if there is a framework legislation at eu level, which is in line with the wording of the whole report. the report also mentions the specific reasons for the need for a common european approach to this issue.
in writing. i supported the european parliament resolution on unfair trading practices in the food supply chain. i consider this a very important problem for farmers and consumers. we are seeing it in individual countries, including the czech republic, but the problem is so closely linked to the eu's internal market that it deserves a european approach and a solution at eu level. the european parliament calls for the most appropriate means of protecting food producers and suppliers against unfair trading practices by retailers, most often retail chains. the debate and vote on this text took two different approaches. the imco approach was one of self-regulation and non-intervention through legislation. the agri committee took a different view, urging in its opinion 'the timely submission of a draft eu framework legislation' and thus favouring a legislative solution at eu level. in our group, the agri committee's position was ultimately the prevailing one, and i agree with it. i am of the opinion that voluntary self-regulatory solutions can help to cultivate trade relations, but cannot in themselves bring about a solution to the problem of unfair trade practices. my position is in line with the czech ministry of agriculture. i therefore supported the resolution as such and the amendments of the agri committee.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report, in line with the position of the czech republic. this is a complicated issue because unfair trading practices cannot be addressed by existing legislative instruments. the amendment to the law on significant market power has brought about some improvement in this situation in the czech republic, but it does not resolve the whole situation. given the international nature of some retail chains, a solution at international level would also be needed, namely the prohibition of unfair trading practices, which would protect smes, micro-enterprises and, of course, consumers, and provide a level playing field for retail chains across the eu.

in writing. when voting on the report on the ratification of the 2010 protocol to the international convention on liability and compensation for damage in connection with the carriage of dangerous and noxious substances, i voted in favour of the motion. the objective of the report is to express the consent of the council to the adoption by the european parliament of the 2010 protocol to the convention. the convention itself aims to ensure prompt and effective compensation for damage caused by the escape of dangerous and harmful substances during their transport by sea. the protocol brings change, in particular, in the area of stricter pollution liability regimes. in the event of ratification of the convention as amended by the protocol by member states, the resulting legislation may partially overlap with the adaptation under directive 2004/35/ec aimed at preventing and remedying environmental damage. the report therefore recommends that the council address this issue in the adoption process. the report also recommends, inter alia, that the integrity and effectiveness of the eu's common rules should not be adversely affected by the international obligations arising from the convention, and warns against the possibility of the continued existence of two regimes, one eu and the other international, of legal liability for marine pollution. i agree with the report's proposals as they stand.

in writing. on 17 december 2015, parliament received a letter requesting its consent to the draft council decision on the ratification by member states and their accession on behalf of the union to the 2010 protocol to the hns convention. the international convention on liability and compensation for damage in connection with the carriage of hazardous and noxious substances by sea, 1996, is the last international maritime organisation (imo) convention dealing with liability and compensation for damage arising from the carriage of hazardous and noxious substances by sea, including liquefied natural gas (lng) and liquefied petroleum gas (lpg), which has not yet been ratified. the imo has gained experience with similar international regimes governing liability for damage caused by other maritime activities, such as the transport of oil by tankers, and has adopted this international agreement, as amended by the 2010 protocol to the hns convention, to complement the maritime liability convention system with a dedicated instrument. the 1996 hns convention and the 2010 protocol to the hns convention have not yet entered into force. since i consider the protocol to be important, i have spoken in favour of its ratification.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the ratification and accession of eu members to the 2010 protocol to the hazardous and noxious substances (hns) convention. this convention ensures uniform application of rules on liability and compensation in connection with accidents caused by ships carrying hns at sea across the eu, and ensures availability of sufficient funds for compensation of victims of such accidents. considering the nature of shipping as a global business with a cross-boundary impact, i do believe that an international regime rather than regional solutions is better suited to tackle this type of challenge. this protocol would also be an opportunity to frame a coherent policy at eu level.
in writing. when voting on the report on the aspects of judicial cooperation in civil matters in the context of the ratification of the 2010 protocol to the international convention on liability and compensation for damage in connection with the carriage of dangerous and noxious substances, i voted in favour of the motion. the objective of the report is to express the consent of the council to the adoption by the european parliament of the 2010 protocol to the convention. the report takes account of the related aspects of judicial cooperation in civil matters. the main objective of the protocol is to strengthen the liability regime for marine pollution by dangerous substances in connection with their transport. in the event of ratification of the convention as amended by the protocol, the resulting legislation of chapter iv of the protocol dealing with civil matters may partially overlap with certain rules under the brussels i regulation. the protocol creates a restrictive system of jurisdiction, whereas the brussels i regulation leaves the choice of jurisdiction to the parties. the report therefore aims, inter alia, to alert the council to the possibility of such an irregularity in the event of the accession of member states to the convention as amended by the 2010 protocol. it is essential that the convention guarantee the uniform application of the rules on liability and compensation for damage resulting from accidents caused by vessels carrying dangerous goods. the report also calls for the convention to be ratified by the member states within two years at the latest. i agree with the report's requirements, which are set out above, and that is why i voted in favour of the proposal.

in writing. on 8 june 2016, we voted on the draft resolution on endocrine disruptors: the state of play following the judgment of the court of justice (cjeu) of 16 december 2015 at the european parliament's plenary session in strasbourg. at the last additional plenary session of the european parliament in brussels, i criticised the commission's flagrant disregard for the eusc decision in the commission v sweden case. the european parliament, together with the council, has unambiguously committed the commission in directive 528/2012 to adopt criteria for the assessment of endocrine disruptors by 13 december 2013. the commission has not done so until now, and it has not done so even after the eusr explicitly told it that it should. due to the absence of criteria for the evaluation of endocrine disruptors, the prohibition of endocrine disruptors laid down in directive 528/2012 cannot be active and therefore these substances continue to cause significant harm to the health of european citizens. i am therefore very pleased to have been able to support the joint resolution which criticises the commission's approach to the whole case and at the same time calls on it to act.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this joint resolution urging the commission to publish scientific criteria for identifying endocrine disruptors. indeed endocrine disruptors are chemicals which interfere with the hormonal system, potentially causing damage to health and the environment. under the regulations in force on the marketing of biocidal products (regulation 528/2012) and of plant health products (regulation 1107/2009), the commission ought to have specified scientific criteria for the determination of endocrine-disrupting properties of active substances and biocidal products no later than 13 december 2013. the commission has, however, postponed that deadline arguing the need for a socio-economic study to be conducted. at the end of 2015, the general court of the eu found that the commission had breached eu law. finally, this resolution condemns the commission not only for failing to deliver upon its obligation to adopt delegated acts under the terms of regulation 528/2012 but also for not complying with the court ruling (article 266 tfeu).

in writing. on 8 june 2016, at the european parliament's plenary session in strasbourg, i voted in favour of my group colleague lynn boylan's objection to the authorisation of genetically modified maize. as you know, i have long protested against any authorisation of the cultivation of genetically modified crops on european soil. i personally believe that this is a dangerous gamble with our biodiversity and our health, because all the risks to both human health and the environment as a whole are still unpredictable. we already have a number of scientific studies that explicitly point out, for example, that the foetuses of animals fed genetically modified crops show numerous mutations, malformations and other damage to the immune system. there is a real risk that these animal health problems will then spread to humans through the consumption of milk or meat. the current gmo authorisation process is dysfunctional and does not provide adequate safeguards. i am of the opinion that until it is reformed in a very substantial way, all authorisation processes for such crops should be suspended. rather than allowing more and more gmos, the commission and the member states should take on their responsibilities for the health of the european population and rework the system.

author. – madam president, parliament has repeatedly called for the adoption of a regulation on the administrative procedure of the union, which would enable european citizens to better exercise their right to good administration. for the first time, in 2001, parliament called on the commission to submit a proposal for a regulation containing a code of good administrative behaviour. at that time we had no clear legal basis for an eu administrative procedure law but, with the lisbon treaty, article 298 was introduced as an appropriate legal base. in 2010, the committee on legal affairs (juri) set up a working group on eu administrative law. we concluded that eu administrative law was very fragmented and only a very few areas of the union’s administrative activities were subject to a systematic approach. that is why parliament, in january 2013, adopted the berlinguer report, in which it clearly requested the commission to submit a proposal for an administrative regulation applicable to the administration of the union’s institutions, bodies, offices and agencies. in the current parliamentary term we have again followed up, with a working group chaired by my esteemed colleague heidi hautala, which has done tremendous work that has now come to an end. as the commission has, unfortunately, still not come up with a concrete proposal for a regulation, or clearly stated that we are to expect such an initiative, the oral question and resolution we are talking about tonight shall serve as a gentle reminder from parliament to the commission. in order to help the commission to make up its mind, the main aim of the juri committee working group was to draft a model regulation, with the advice of law professors, containing a basic set of the rules we would like to see. we have annexed this regulation to the oral question and resolution presented tonight. the objective of such a proposal is to provide citizens and the union’s administration with a comprehensive and cross-cutting administrative procedure. especially in the current times, with euroscepticism on the rise, citizens would enormously benefit from uniform procedural guarantees enforceable in the eu courts. increased in writing. one of the greatest achievements of european integration, the single internal market, is based on four principles. it is the free movement of goods, persons, services and capital. it is precisely for its optimal functioning that i have supported simplifying the requirements for the presentation of certain authentic instruments in other countries. although we have made considerable progress in the degree of integration since the adoption of the single european act of 1986 relevant to the internal market, the reality remains that the submission and approval of documents abroad is often a very demanding process. i therefore approve the application of the exemption exempting citizens from the need to legalise documents and to apply for an apostille in the case of public documents on personal status and certain other documents that are often required when exercising the right to mobility. although this process is outdated, it is still used and is time-consuming and logistically demanding for citizens. in addition, it involves unnecessary financial costs. the european parliament has proposed from the outset that the range of documents covered by this exception be broader. i do not understand the council's negative attitude. i therefore find the outcome of the negotiations limited and have supported it reluctantly, and only because even such a limited stance is better than being stuck in the ground and accepting the unnecessary bureaucratic burden that citizens are exposed to.
in writing. ‒ today, people who want to move from one eu country to another face unnecessary obstacles. one of these is the cross-border recognition of public documents on personal status, nationality or criminal records. i am therefore pleased that this regulation will finally make it easier to recognise them. however, i think that the list of such documents should be extended. for example, i see no reason why the disabled person's card should not be recognised in this way. i therefore supported the report, but i hope that the other instruments will soon be recognised across borders.
in writing. i supported the ep's report, which adopts the council's position at second reading on the proposal for a regulation simplifying the requirements for the submission of certain public documents in the eu. documents certifying, for example, birth, marriage, permanent residence or criminal integrity will no longer need to be legalised or apostilled before being presented to the authorities in another eu country. for most of the documents covered by the new regulation, translation will even be eliminated as uniform multilingual forms will be introduced. the european parliament originally proposed going further and extending the regulation to include educational documents. it is a pity that the member states were not willing to go that far, but the proposal is a great step forward and a good compromise. the new rules will make life much easier for millions of citizens living, studying and working in another eu country. the unpleasant additional administration, time delays and, in some cases, the financial burden of formalities such as apostilles or official translation will be eliminated. it is worth noting that the regulation respects the sovereignty of the member states and does not require them to recognise the content of the documents submitted it is only a matter of making life easier for the citizens who submit the documents. any verification of documents by member states will be carried out electronically between the authorities, so that this burden is not passed on to the citizen. i think that approach is the right one and that is why i supported the text.
in writing. i was very pleased to support the regulation on the facilitation of the mutual recognition of official documents in plenary. more than 14 million people in the eu live, study or work outside their home country. these citizens are exposed to unnecessary administrative burdens in various life situations in the form of obtaining court translations, notarial and other time-consuming and costly forms of authentication and obtaining translations of personal documents. the purpose of the adopted regulation is to simplify the recognition of certain public documents in the eu. the regulation covers documents relating to personal status as well as certain other documents frequently requested by citizens relating to residence, nationality or criminal records. the regulation provides for exemptions from legalisation and apostille, and simplified measures for certified copies and certified translations. the institutions will be able to request the authenticity of the document from the issuing authority themselves, if necessary. the regulation also includes multilingual forms, which are completed by the official in the citizen's home country and attached to the document. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the regulation to cover a wider range of documents, such as diplomas or disability certificates, but i regard this compromise between the ep and the member states as a success. the text also contains a revision clause which allows for the future expansion of the range of documents covered.

in writing. i supported the commission's initiative to present a proposal for a regulation harmonising the official procedures of the union institutions, with the exception of judicial and legislative procedures. clear and clearly defined rules of administrative procedure would provide greater legal certainty for individuals who come into contact with the eu institutions, in particular where these institutions decide on their rights and obligations. specific examples of harmonised legislation could be the right of access to the file, the right to effective legal protection, the obligation for institutions to take decisions within a reasonable time and the obligation to state reasons for administrative acts.
in writing. the administrative and legislative procedures of the european union are difficult for the public to read. citizens do not understand the rights that european institutions and agencies guarantee them, and this is partly why the current wave of euroscepticism is taking place. that is why i supported the resolution on an open, efficient and independent administration of the european union. i believe that such legislation, although not entirely supported by the european commission, can help to reduce the distance that citizens feel towards the institutions of the european union. it is in the public interest that european administration should function efficiently and that there should be no unnecessary production and no lack of rules. both of these can be very dangerous. more specifically, this proposal is designed to ensure that any decision to initiate a new administrative procedure is accompanied by the provision of sufficient information to the relevant parties. it also includes emphasising the need to adopt administrative decisions within a reasonable timeframe and to avoid unnecessary delays. what i also find very positive is the provision on the right of citizens to be sure that they can turn to the institutions and receive an answer to their questions in their own language at the optimum time. the institutions, agencies and offices of the european union are there for their citizens, who should be made aware that there is no other way.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this resolution calling on the commission to present a draft regulation for an open, efficient and independent administration for the european union. over the years, the eu has introduced a large number of sector-specific administrative procedures in the form of binding and non-binding measures without necessarily taking account of the overall coherence of the system. there are gaps and inconsistencies in these procedures, due to their complex diversity, and a set of common administrative-procedure rules now urgently needs to be established at the level of eu institutions, bodies and organs in order to boost legal security, close gaps in the eu legal system and contribute to respect for the rule of law.
in writing. ‒ i support the report presented and am convinced that this regulation will contribute to a more open and efficient administration of the european union. as the european union's powers have gradually expanded, citizens have increasingly come into contact with the union's institutions, bodies and agencies. in my view, citizens have a right to expect a high level of transparency, efficiency and speed of action from the union's institutions, bodies, offices and agencies. the duly structured and uniform administrative procedures guaranteed by this regulation promote both effective administration and the proper enforcement of the right to good administration guaranteed as a general principle of union law and under article 41 of the charter. this regulation is therefore the right step towards greater efficiency and transparency of the institutions of the european union.
in writing. i disagree with the call for the commission to invest money in the rail sector: the european parliament asks the commission to make full use of the various eu funding instruments, to explore and use additional sources of funding for the s2r joint undertaking and to seek synergies between the different eu funds. in my view, the commission should not interfere in railway business and the czech experience with private carriers shows that a free market without subsidies is perfectly applicable to railways.
in writing. in the context of the report approved, i consider it important to implement rapidly the technical pillar of the fourth railway package, which is crucial for the creation of a genuine single market for rail products. it can be noted that greater interoperability and a strengthened role for the european railway agency (era) will facilitate the harmonisation of the network and thus reduce the costs of developing and approving rolling stock. the importance of the political pillar of the fourth railway package, which should ensure a fair competitive environment for carriers and suppliers in general, should also be stressed.
in writing. ‒ i supported the modernisation of the european rail supply industry which is integral to increasing the technological standards of the european union. this is most important as the railway sector accounts for 1 million direct and 1.2 million indirect jobs in the eu. likewise, this is another step towards achieving the commission’s 20% industrialisation target. with the passing of this resolution, we can continue these strides towards a competitive europe whose standards of modernisation match our role in the global market.
in writing. ‒ the european railway supply industry has long faced unfair competition from third country suppliers. this lack of a level playing field is threatening jobs in the railway sector in europe. that's why i voted for the motion.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this resolution calling on the commission to unveil a coherent strategy as soon as possible on an industrial policy to re-industrialise the european continent. in this resolution we are asking that the eu re-industrialisation strategy should be based on sustainability and energy and resource efficiency and be organised by sector, incorporating strong, vertical industrial production measures within the eu. the rail sector deserves special attention and we call on the commission to set up a structure to facilitate exchanges between established companies and start-ups in the sector. finally this text points the finger at unfair practices from international competitors, particularly china.

represent the people of europe, and if we want to serve our citizens well we must be fully informed. commissioner, the treaties are very clear in this regard. the european parliament shall be immediately and fully informed at all stages of international agreements. there are no conditional clauses in that sentence. as the guardian of the treaties, the commission must fulfil this requirement. moreover, the framework agreement sets out clearly how this is to be done: parliament must be informed by the commission at the same time as the council, before a mandate is given, during in writing. the energy efficiency directive is built on an interesting theory. on the one hand, it assumes that, regardless of the costs involved and the local climate, it is worthwhile for everyone across the eu to implement the maximum possible energy efficiency measures in all circumstances. unknown why the whole report is based on the thesis that the free market is the best solution to all problems. in several places, this claim is 'tendered' by social considerations. a significant part of the proposal deals with improving reporting and promoting technical progress. however, at some points there are very few realistic claims for a near future of virtually zero energy demand for all buildings. a very weak point in the text is the assumption that co2 emissions can be eliminated even for a substantial part of industrial production. which, while theoretically possible, is practically impossible with today's best technology. despite these reservations, the report contains a number of interesting suggestions which can make a significant contribution to energy savings. this combination of unrealistic goals in the relatively short term, market fundamentalism and social elements, together with unrealistic expectations of rapid technical progress, is the reason why i cannot unequivocally support or reject the proposals submitted under consideration.

in writing. i abstained in the vote on the approval of the protocol to the euro-mediterranean agreement between the eu and lebanon. lebanon is a member of the euro-mediterranean partnership, which aims primarily at deeper economic cooperation with the 16 countries bordering the eu in north africa and the middle east. the purpose of the vote was to express parliament's agreement or disagreement with the protocol to the eu-lebanon agreement and to make some formal changes to the agreement in connection with the accession of new states to the eu after its conclusion. as the agreement is generally aimed at the gradual establishment of a free market between lebanon and the eu, which could have some adverse economic consequences for lebanon, i could not support the proposal. in my view, in general, when concluding economic cooperation agreements, it is necessary to take into account the negative effects that the agreements may have, for example, on the country's agriculture or industry and to try to limit them as much as possible. it is also necessary to establish in the treaties rules for respecting human rights and to regulate the sanctions for their violation. we won't find any such clause in the agreement. on the other hand, i recognise that the will to conclude an agreement and gradually deepen economic cooperation between the eu and lebanon came directly from the lebanese state authorities, who want to deepen cooperation.
in writing. - i voted against it. i'm all for free trade and cooperation agreements. i do not, however, agree with the inclusion of the lebanese republic in the programmes of the european union. the best way to let poorer countries get rich is to remove trade barriers, not to send subsidies out of the pockets of european taxpayers.
in writing. - lebanon is a strategic partner of the eu in the middle east. the country faces security threats especially in relation to its neighbourhood with war-torn syria. lebanon has now given asylum to around 1 million refugees, whom the eu is trying to help through newly created trust funds. it is therefore in the eu's best interest to strengthen stability in the country and develop the capacity to cope with the current difficult situation. i am pleased that there is a broad consensus on the report on the need to strengthen cooperation and support for lebanon.

in writing. ‒ monaco is considered one of the few tax havens in the world. the tax system in monaco is virtually devoid of income tax, property tax, real estate tax, land tax or capital gains tax. the only direct tax is the income tax on po, which is 33,33% of the profit, but even this is quite benevolent to the taxpayers. the fight against tax havens and tax fraud is necessary, which is why i supported the eu-monaco agreement on the automatic exchange of financial account information. the agreement will help prevent taxpayers from hiding their capital abroad, but will also improve international tax cooperation and compliance. under the new agreement, eu countries and monaco will be able to automatically exchange information on financial accounts held by each other's nationals on their territory. the exchange of information on financial accounts between eu countries and monaco will also be intensified and financial support will be easier to identify.
in writing. ‒ cross-border tax fraud and tax evasion are harmful for our economy, as well as for our financial credibility and long-term sustainability. this is why i voted in favour of amending the protocol to the agreement concluded between the eu and monaco, which aims at improving international tax cooperation and compliance through the automatic exchange of financial account information. this agreement will increase tax transparency in europe by ensuring that monaco applies the same measures on the taxation of savings income as those currently applied in the eu. it will also incorporate a new set of provisions to reflect the global standard for automatic exchange of financial account information developed by the oecd in 2014.
in writing. ‒ i have decided to support this report as it deepens international cooperation in the field of taxation and commits to complying with the relevant regulations. i believe that this agreement is an important step in the ongoing efforts to combat tax fraud and tax evasion. the aim of the agreement is to ensure that monaco applies stricter measures equivalent to the eu legal framework. in particular, i appreciate the possibility in this measure to establish correctly and unequivocally the identity of the taxpayers concerned and to assess the likelihood of tax evasion.
