in writing. i voted in favour of the report on the multiannual plan for the recovery of the bluefin tuna stock. the plan represents a number of steps necessary to achieve the objective. the tacs should be reduced. it is also necessary to introduce stricter rules for catches in certain areas and during certain periods. the strengthening of international control is an equally important step. it is important to apply the agreed rules uniformly and to ensure a level playing field for all fishermen, including foreigners, in order to successfully restore the tuna stock. without the same rules for non-eu fishermen, we cannot achieve the desired result.
in writing. - i got held up. i regularly miss these reports because the czech republic has no sea.
in writing. ‒ bluefin tuna is one of the top predators in the mediterranean sea, a crucial species for its ecosystem, and has a very high economic value, both in the european and japanese market. in the late 90s however, the mediterranean stock dramatically decreased to levels compromising the future of the species and the viability of the fishing sector. the multi-annual bluefin tuna recovery plan in the eastern atlantic and the mediterranean established in 2006 by the international commission for the conservation of atlantic tunas (iccat) was very efficient in contributing to the recovery of the stock. this is why i voted in favour of transposing this plan into eu law, as i hope that it will contribute to ensuring the exploitation of living aquatic resources under sustainable economic, environmental and social conditions. i particularly agree with the decision to ensure equitable distribution between the various fleets and support small scale and artisanal fisheries, which usually practice sustainable fishing practices and ensure the livelihood of many local communities.
in writing. this report brings with it a long-awaited blueprint for fisheries policy, which no longer focuses on one species but takes account of the evolution of different species and their interaction. the plan should help to ensure a balanced and sustainable fishing of these species and the stability of opportunities and thus the livelihoods of fishermen. an important part of the proposal is to guarantee the use of current scientific knowledge concerning both the stocks of the species concerned, the interactions between them and other aspects of sustainable fishing. i believe that this baltic sea plan is a big step in the right direction towards reforming the common fisheries policy and sustainable fishing and i was therefore pleased to vote in favour of the proposal.
in writing. - i got held up. i regularly miss these reports because the czech republic has no sea.
in writing. ‒ i supported the adoption of this first multiannual plan under the reformed common fisheries policy. it is precisely because this is the first multiannual plan, which will logically be a model for similar plans for other seas, that setting the conditions is of particular importance. this is also why it has been so difficult to reach agreements and concessions between parliament and the council. the plan aims to ensure sustainable fishing for cod, herring and sprat in the baltic sea. last year, parliament decided to postpone the vote on this issue, mainly because of the impossibility of reaching a compromise on the fish mortality rate. parliament pushed for far more stringent measures. while it has only succeeded in enforcing the partial limitations on flexibility proposed by the member states in the trialogue, i welcome the fact that it has also succeeded in enforcing stronger safeguards with regard to sustainable fishing. the social democrats have done an excellent job in this respect within the committee on fisheries. i welcome the fact that the committee's position was confirmed today by the plenary.
in writing. ‒ cod, herring and sprat represent 94% of catches in the baltic sea and are important components of the very sensitive baltic ecosystem. this is why i voted in favour of establishing a multiannual plan, whose aim is to establish a framework for the multispecies management of these stocks and the fisheries exploiting them, in order to reverse the effects of their overfishing in the eu. based on sound scientific advice and an innovative long-term perspective, it strives to become a pioneer tool in fisheries management policies. the plan will thus provide for a balanced, sustainable exploitation of cod, herring and sprat stocks promote the stability of fishing opportunities and thereby guarantee the livelihoods of fishers. beyond the content of this plan, i also welcome the increased participation of the european parliament in european fisheries policies.
in writing. i voted in favour of the proposal on the property relations of international couples, which affects some 16 million such couples in the eu. this report dealt with the case of international marriages or registered partnerships and the settlement of property in the event of divorce, legal separation or death. the new legal framework gives couples from 18 eu countries the choice of which jurisdiction to deal with their case, to avoid parallel proceedings in two states and possible conflicting court decisions. this will provide legal certainty, harmonisation of rules and better access to fair proceedings for international couples. the same rights will be guaranteed to both married couples and registered partners.
in writing. - i got held up. i'm in favor of states voluntarily agreeing to recognize decisions on marital property. i think this is a classic example of how to use intergovernmental cooperation without the involvement of the european parliament and the eu.
in writing. i voted in favour of the property relations act. the main contribution of this proposal is to clarify the status of international married couples. as this type of union is becoming more frequent thanks to the free movement of persons, it is important that it be properly treated legally in all matters, including property matters. the compromise form of the proposal, which does not interfere with the autonomy of the member states in matters of family law and thus prevents it from being rejected by the member states, as has already happened, is also a significant reason for supporting it.
in writing. i supported the legislative resolution on the proposal for a council regulation on jurisdiction, applicable law and the recognition and enforcement of decisions in matrimonial property regime. although the increasing number of marriages with an international element has become an unquestionable daily reality in the union, international couples are still faced with practical problems in the settlement of their property, such as which law will govern the specific property situation or which court will have jurisdiction to settle their property. the result is legal uncertainty, delays in the case and the associated disproportionate costs. enhanced cooperation will create a clear legal framework for the settlement of thousands of international marriages in the participating member states. the property relations of international marriages will thus be dealt with in a comprehensive manner, under a single applicable law and by a single judicial body. in particular, i appreciate the flexible jurisdictional regulation for the settlement of property and the principle of the unity of the applicable law, where the applicable law will apply to the property as a whole. this avoids fragmentation of the arrangement, with different legal systems applying to different parts of the spouses' property. i am also pleased that, while the draft regulation brings forward progressive practical elements, it preserves the autonomy of the member states in the area of family law. the regulation does not in any way affect or change the substantive law of the czech republic governing the institution of marriage and its legal consequences.
in writing. ‒ due to the increased mobility, cooperation and exchange inside the eu, the eu now counts 16 million international couples, most commonly bound by the ties of marriage. this is why i voted in favour of a new legal framework that will clarify and simplify property rules in cases of divorce, legal separation or death for international married couples, by determining the jurisdiction and the law applicable to their property regimes. this is an indispensable measure to put an end to the practical and legal difficulties and costs these couples have to face, in line with the principle that every european citizen has the right to equal treatment in front of our national institutions.
in writing. ‒ i support this report because the regulation will be a very useful tool for international marriage within the european union, while preserving the autonomy of the member states in family law. i appreciate that parliament's demands have been heeded. i am convinced that this proposal for a regulation on matrimonial property regime is in the best interests of the union and its international married couples and that it will resolve a number of uncertainties and legal problems.
in writing. i voted in favour of the proposal on the property relations of international couples, which affects some 16 million such couples in the eu. this report dealt with the case of international marriages as well as registered partnerships and their property settlement in the event of divorce, separation or death. the new legal framework gives couples from 18 eu countries the choice of which jurisdiction to deal with their case, to avoid parallel proceedings in two states and possible conflicting court decisions. this will provide legal certainty, harmonisation of rules and better access to fair proceedings for international couples. the same rights will be guaranteed to both married couples and registered partners.
in writing. when voting on the council regulation on jurisdiction, applicable law and the recognition and enforcement of decisions in matrimonial property regimes and registered partnerships, i voted in favour of the proposal. within the eu, the number of partnerships with an international element is increasing. the regulation therefore aims, in particular, to simplify the regime of joint property of spouses and registered partners, both in everyday life and in the event of divorce or death of one of the partners. the regulation provides for greater legal certainty within those bundles, inter alia, by facilitating the designation of a common court and the mutual recognition of judgments in related cases by the member states. all property relationships of international couples originating in eu member states will thus be administered by the courts of one member state, irrespective of the nature of the property, both in the context of their daily relationships and in the event of divorce or death of one of the partners. as there is no agreement between all member states in this respect, the regulation will only be applied between 17 member states through so-called closer cooperation. in view of the increasing number of marriages and registered partnerships with an international element, it is important in my view to simplify the resulting processes, including the property relations of these persons. i therefore supported the draft regulation.
in writing. - i got held up. i am in favour of states voluntarily agreeing to recognise decisions on matters of property relations in registered partnerships. i think this is a classic example of how to use intergovernmental cooperation without the involvement of the european parliament and the eu.
in writing. i supported the draft regulation, which i believe will be a very useful tool for international couples in the european union. in matters of property consequences of registered partnerships, it concerns jurisdiction, the applicable law and the recognition and enforcement of decisions. however, it does not cover, in particular, questions of the legal capacity of the partners, the existence, validity and recognition of a partnership, maintenance obligations and the inheritance of the property of a deceased partner. the autonomy of the member states in the area of family law is thus preserved. nor does it concern the legislation of the member states on registered partnerships or its legal consequences. the ep was an active participant in the negotiations and succeeded in achieving a substantial improvement in the content of the regulation.
in writing. ‒ as a result of increased integration between european countries, the eu now counts 16 million international couples, namely 32 million citizens. while marriage remains the most common type of union, new forms of partnerships have emerged, including the registered partnership, by which two people in a stable relationship formally register their union with a public authority. these couples often encounter great difficulties when it comes to the property rights of their union, because of the significant difference regarding the rules governing registered partnerships between the different eu countries. this is why i voted in favour of the proposal that will enable international couples in the eu to benefit from legal security, a better access to justice and harmonised rules regarding property rights. concretely, it will allow citizens in international couples to have the various procedures related to property rights, namely divorce, legal separation and death procedures, handled by the courts of the same eu country.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the european parliament's report on the continuation of the strategic framework for european cooperation in education and training (et 2020). i was the shadow rapporteur for this report for the epp and i agree with the way it came out. i'm glad it was passed by such a large majority. the final vote managed to drop some of the controversial points against mobility and the bologna process, which i consider to be important and beneficial aspects of eu education policy. the report fully respects the fact that education is primarily in the hands of the member states. however, the eu is expected to provide a framework for skills, training to promote inclusion and reduce radicalisation, and recommendations for bringing education and the labour market closer together to reduce youth unemployment. on the other hand, the report rightly emphasises that education is a value in itself and not just a means of meeting the needs of the labour market. in this context, i have succeeded in inserting into the report an emphasis on ethical and personal education, as well as an emphasis on the irreplaceable role of parents in the educational process and in communication with schools. it is good that the report gives a positive assessment of the eu's actions to support teachers, including the use of the erasmus+ programme. overall, the report emphasises the quality of education over quantity, and also the need to integrate refugee and migrant children into the education system.
in writing. ‒ faced with high youth unemployment and the new challenges of migration, it is essential to rethink our take on european cooperation in education and training. that is why i voted in favour of improving the strategic framework for european cooperation in education and training 2020 (et2020), which is an umbrella for all eu-level policy exchanges on education and training between eu countries. it is important that we enhance the quality of education and training by extending cooperation with more stakeholders from civil society, by ensuring coherent, transparent and inclusive education for a diverse group of learners, and by promoting a new agenda for adult learning. this is also an opportunity to reiterate the importance of creating access for migrants to language courses, basic skills training and higher education, in order to facilitate their integration into society and the labour market. finally, better cooperation between eu member states would certainly be very helpful in establishing new, innovative and interactive methods of teaching, training and learning.

in writing. ‒ while the eu is well on track to meet its 2020 renewable energy targets, it is clear that many member states need to strengthen their policies and instruments to ensure that the targets are met. the report focuses on the importance of sharing best practices or the need to assess the impact of renewables on prices, in particular for households. it stresses the need for european legislation on energy market rules, stable and efficient renewable energy support regimes for long-term investments, which are also adapted to national needs and circumstances. environmental care is truly a global problem. i was happy to support the report calling for more effective cooperation and coordination within and between member states.
in writing. renewable resources are a rewarding topic of philosophical discussion. the radical demands for 100% coverage of energy needs in the next few years are technically justified by philosophical considerations and the real technician is amazed at how simple everything is. if we take seriously the objective of ensuring strict environmental protection on the one hand and 100% renewable energy on the other, we are faced with a contradiction which is difficult to resolve. wind farms are fundamentally changing the landscape wherever they are located. the several hectares of photovoltaic plants have a significant impact on local air flows, as do the large valley water reservoir projects. the daily and annual distribution of electricity consumption does not correspond to the sunlight, wind or rainfall ratios. so we're left with biomass and geothermal energy. when comparing the possibilities of individual renewable sources, we find that on the one hand there are a large number of administrative obstacles (in particular for the connection of small photovoltaic and the installation of small hydropower plants) and on the other hand there are legitimate concerns of the operators of large electricity networks about ensuring the stability of the whole system. electricity is very difficult to store. these problems are not addressed in the report. as well as the overly optimistic outlook, the report contains a number of positive suggestions and i assume that the most fantastic proposals will not be accepted, so i support the adoption of the report.
in writing. on 23 june 2016, we voted on the progress report on renewable energy at the european parliament's extraordinary plenary session in brussels. this was a report by the committee on industry, research and energy. but this is also a long-standing concern of my committee on the environment, public health and food safety. that is why i was very critical of the text presented from the outset. first of all, i have to say that i abstained from the vote. although the documentary ended up with some good things, like mentioning the issue of energy poverty or pushing for new generations of biofuels at the expense of the old and flawed, i could not support it in good conscience. in my view, the report is unbalanced, for example, by its strong endorsement of the use of biomass, which we all know today is totally unsustainable in terms of emissions and its negative impact on food self-sufficiency. the whole text says that the only right source for the future of energy is renewable energy, which is unacceptable. the report omits any mention of nuclear energy, which it no longer envisages in the future. they also ignore any potential breakthroughs in the industry, such as cold fusion.

in writing. i supported the progress report on renewable energy because i consider political support for the transformation of the energy grid towards renewable energy to be absolutely crucial. the reason is not just to combat climate change, but also to promote energy security and the development of new economic sectors. i also appreciate the report's critical approach to some aspects of promoting renewable sources, such as promoting biofuels in transport.
in writing. ‒ i am pleased that the european parliament, thanks in part to my vote, has adopted this report today. the report assesses the progress the eu has made towards its target of 20% renewables in the eu energy mix by 2020. the report also looks at the outlook beyond 2020. as in the energy efficiency report, i am not satisfied with the low ambition of the targets originally proposed by the commission the commission has abolished the binding targets at national level and has only set a europe-wide target of 27% by 2030, which is really low. i am therefore very pleased that the commission has been able to send a clear message that it is through binding national targets that the current 2020 targets are being achieved and that the abolition of national targets is a big mistake. the social democrats have also long held the view that the european-wide target for 2030 should be at least 45% renewable energy, and this requirement has also been successfully implemented in the report.
in writing. i finally voted in favour of the resolution on the progress report on renewable energy. the non-binding resolution responds to the commission's evaluation report of last year and sets out the commission's ideas for the upcoming revision of the relevant legislation. the commission report notes that the target of at least 20% of energy from renewable sources by 2020 is likely to be met, which is welcomed by the european parliament. i am pleased that the czech republic is recognised in the resolution as a country that is well ahead of its target. the resolution addresses some of the problems that the introduction of renewable sources has brought and calls for effective solutions. for example, it points out that some member states have neglected their transmission networks and these are now unable to accommodate the surges of energy from renewable sources. the czech republic is also facing the consequences of the shortcomings of the german transmission network. i also think it is important to mention the impact of renewable energy support on agriculture. the cultivation of crops for the production of biofuels shall not be contrary to food production or food safety.
in writing. ‒ this own-initiative report on the implementation of the renewables directive (2009/28/ec) concentrates on the results achieved, their added value and the opportunities provided for european citizens and businesses, as well as reasons why certain member states are struggling to meet ambitious targets set in the directive. while most of the member states are well on track to achieving 20% renewables targets by 2020, and some are even ahead, a few will probably fail to deliver. the european policies on renewable energy and sustainability are very important, especially for our future development. the rapporteur made a number of good points and, even though i do not agree on all the points in the report, i believe it is important to recognise the role of renewables in the eu’s energy market and to support their further integration into the market. therefore, i supported the report.
in writing. ‒ i support this report. i believe that our primary responsibility is to fight climate change, which is a historic duty that we must take on. at the same time, we need to reduce our dependence on energy resources from the rest of the world if we are to not only be at the forefront of developing strategic technologies for the energy transition, but also to support our manufacturing model and create quality jobs. i believe that the transition to a sustainable energy production model is a societal priority that cannot be addressed from a market perspective alone. it must be understood that regulation and democratic participation are necessary to avoid serious social and environmental side effects.
in writing. ‒ although the energy efficiency directive has started positive developments in the member states, the lack of implementation is undermining its potential. member states were invited to promote smart metering and transparent billing as a way of encouraging more responsible consumer behaviour with regard to consumption and investment in energy efficiency. there is still a lot of common effort to be made to achieve the objectives set, and i therefore voted in favour of the report, which points out the shortcomings and urges the member states and the commission to take effective and timely action in implementing the directive.
in writing. on 23 june, at the european parliament's extraordinary plenary session in brussels, we voted on the itre report on the implementation of the energy efficiency directive. although the main committee responsible for this report was the itre committee, the envi committee, of which i am a member, also issued its report on the subject of the proposed energy efficiency directive. i was a shadow reporter for this report. from the very beginning, we in the envi committee have been faced with great pressure to set binding, new and very ambitious targets for the new energy efficiency era. personally, i agree that energy efficiency is itself an energy source, but given what we are currently learning from the whole emissions cheating scandal in the automotive industry dieselgate , i strongly insist that any further determination of emission ceilings or energy targets should always be based on real and solid data, predictions and, above all, be practicable and achievable by the member states. and that is exactly what i was lacking in the negotiations on the text of this report. the text of the report sets out a very ambitious target, but very little attention is paid to the problem of how to achieve it successfully and, above all, in time. so i could not support him in good conscience.
in writing. - i voted against it. i don't agree that the decline in fossil fuel prices is a negative phenomenon. instead, it means more money saved for citizens and businesses and growth for the economy. i strongly disagree with the argument that lower fuel prices and the outlook for economic growth could further jeopardise the achievement of the 20% target. only rich economies can afford to invest in innovation, so i'm not opposed to lowering prices. it is clear that the european commission wants to pursue its policy even at the cost of impoverishing the population and with absolutely uncertain or no result.
in writing. ‒ i supported the report which highlights the importance of energy efficiency for the eu's sustainable economic development and calls for the adoption of an ambitious binding energy efficiency target of 40% by 2030. i am convinced that this set target represents cost-effective energy efficiency that will benefit both companies and consumers. the report also rightly points out that seven member states have not introduced energy audits. i'm glad the czech republic isn't one of those countries.
in writing. as the shadow rapporteur for this report, i very much welcome the final form, as it has managed to strengthen a number of elements that were omitted from the original proposal. the current energy efficiency directive is a good basis for achieving europe's climate and energy goals, including the ambitious cop 21 commitments. however, this will only be achieved if some of its shortcomings, in particular excessive flexibility, are removed. as a result, we are lagging behind our targets and, if nothing changes, we will not achieve a 20% increase in energy efficiency by 2020. the report calls for a binding 40% energy efficiency target, because if we do not meet this target, we will be closing the way to greater savings, to fostering innovation and to strengthening our dependence on imports. the report also pays great attention to the fight against energy poverty. lastly, it draws the commission's attention to the need to address competing legislation, in particular legislation on energy efficiency, the promotion of renewable sources and the emissions trading system. in this respect, i consider it absolutely essential that there be an analysis of the mutual effects and that the commission come up with a proposal that effectively addresses this situation.
in writing. i did not support the resolution on the report on the implementation of the energy efficiency directive. the resolution responds to a commission report assessing the progress of member states in implementing measures to achieve the energy efficiency target by 2020. the european union has set a non-binding target of 20% energy savings, and the energy efficiency directive contains the instruments to achieve this target. the resolution welcomes the flexibility of the directive member states can choose the best energy efficiency tool for them. however, the commission itself and the ep (ep in resolution) regret that this target will not be met by 2020. the resolution also points out that the instruments for achieving individual energy and climate targets by 2020 are often competing with each other and are therefore ineffective. it also correctly points out the problems of member states adding additional requirements, particularly bureaucratic ones, to businesses and consumers that are not required by european legislation. but the main problem with the resolution is that the left-wing factions have pushed the mention of the 2030 climate goals into it. in october 2014, member states agreed on a non-binding target of 27% energy efficiency improvements by 2030 (with a possible increase to 30%). but the resolution calls for a 40% binding target. this formulation was unacceptable to the ppe group of meps, and that is why my colleagues and i did not support the motion for a resolution.
in writing. ‒ the main objective of this implementation report is to assess implementation of the energy efficiency directive (2012/27/eu). the issue of energy efficiency is also closely related to development in the field of renewables. while the energy efficiency directive entered into force relatively recently, some conclusions can be drawn. while many member states are on track to achieving 20% efficiency target for 2020, full implementation is highly unlikely. the report further highlights the need to focus on improvements in the building sector, which accounts for 40% of total energy consumption and 36% of co2 emissions in the eu, the need to protect vulnerable consumers, improve conditions and provide technical support to those who wish to become prosumers. the rapporteur has pointed out that energy efficiency should be treated as an energy resource, thus decreasing eu dependency on energy imports from third countries, especially gas imports. i voted in favour of this report.
in writing. ‒ i did not support the report because i have long disagreed with the setting of binding energy efficiency targets. the report also calls for a further increase to 40%.

in writing. ‒ in today's vote on the european parliament's resolution on the decision to withdraw from the eu, which is the result of the referendum in the united kingdom, i abstained because i believe that the resulting text is not adequate to the situation, which in my opinion requires balance above all. the result of the referendum is the clear will of the majority of the uk voters to leave the eu, and i do not question that will. however, from a legal point of view, the process of withdrawal from the eu can only be initiated after the member state has confirmed and notified its intention to do so. this has not happened at the moment and i do not think it is necessary at this point to require the notification to be made within a number of days. the uk government is responsible for announcing its intention to leave the eu, and we should respect that responsibility. so, whether from this legal point of view or in the interest of future friendly cooperation between the eu and the uk, i believe that it is not appropriate now to publish hastily prepared political resolutions announcing, among other things, changes in the internal organisation of the european parliament (i.e. staff changes) a few days after the referendum, while the uk is still an eu member state.
in writing. ‒ the result of the british referendum is a massive shock for the eu which will lose one of its important members. it is a unique case in eu history and we must not underestimate the impact of such a decision for the future of the union. eu leaders and institutions need to provide a clear answer and agenda to this extraordinary situation. i nevertheless decided to abstain on this resolution, not because of the content which i share to a large extent, but because of the excessive pressure put on the british government. if i wish the european parliament to be fully involved in all stages of the procedures regarding both the agreement for the united kingdom’s exit and any future relationship between it and the future union of 27 member states, and the negotiation to start as soon as possible, i do not believe that calling for the immediate triggering of article 50 of the treaty is the best way to proceed.

rapporteur for the opinion of the committee on development. – mr president, with all due respect to our colleagues in the different political groups and with different opinions, i cannot give the green light to the attitude which i feel is contrary to our eu trade strategies, by politicising the trade agenda too much. i believe that human rights and trade are not contradictory, but complementary. i believe that trade is a key development instrument that brings growth and wealth, and therefore in the long term contributes to the development of human, labour and social rights. i stand for the strategy of engagement, instead of the policy of conditionality. i believe that we should treat our counterparts as trading partners on an equal footing, and that this kind of treatment will bring a solid basis for ongoing dialogue and cooperation. one free trade agreement in particular, that has only recently been concluded, the free trade agreement between the eu and vietnam, could serve as a very good example of that approach. i think that developing countries need social, labour and environmental standards that correspond in the first place with their level of economic and social development, and any effort to bring binding requirements, to impose binding requirements, which unfortunately is an attitude becoming more and more popular in this chamber, means that it will be harmful to them. it will be counterproductive and also de facto this means a certain exporting of protectionism from our side, and this is something that i cannot support.
rapporteur for the opinion of the committee on the internal market and consumer protection. – mr president, so what do we expect from the new trade strategy? well, first of all, it must not be business as usual. on the one hand, we are seeing more and more eu citizens interested in trade issues. however, on the other hand, there are increasing numbers of those concerned and fearful of the potential impact of the trade issues. we have to be able to come up with new ways to communicate these issues more effectively and to address citizens’ concerns. this would mean saying a clear ‘no’ to all forms of protectionism while aiming for trade that is both fair and responsible. i am convinced that a proper implementation of the strategy should start with an inventory of all current trade negotiations. for this to occur you would need to reallocate sufficient human resources within the commission services. the eu does not show itself to be very serious about this, when we see negotiations taking more than 12 or 15 years. we need to have clear priorities and deliver. personally, i see three key areas for our future trade policy. they should consist of: first, promoting a digital dimension of international trade; secondly, facilitating exchange in the services sector; and lastly, providing our companies, especially smes, with real new business opportunities. the success of our trade policy will ultimately be measured by how well eu companies can access foreign markets and how effectively we can respond to their daily problems.
mr president, commissioner, the thread running through this debate is the question of whether fairer trade is possible. i think, together with my colleagues, that it is, but it is important to remember that parliament also has a role to play in approving trade clauses. we should also remember that if a european company leaves a market, for example because of a failure to respect human rights or certain standards, it is usually prevented from doing so by another entrepreneur who has no regard for them. we should remember that, too. i would also like to point out that human rights can be seen from several angles. the first is that they are fundamental, they are truly universally inviolable. then there's the next generation of human rights. i do not wish to question their scope and listing, but some other geographical areas may find the scope of certain social rights rather problematic. i would therefore urge caution, but i also believe that fairer trade is possible.
mr president, i would like to raise an important point. although we have been talking about it for a long time, commissioner, it has not been sufficiently addressed. few people realise that mileage is one of the biggest problems facing consumers in the european union. experts estimate that this problem affects more than 30% of used cars in the european union. consumers lose more than 9 billion euros a year because of these unfair practices. fraudsters profit at the expense of society as a whole. and the european parliament, which represents this whole, should do everything in its power to protect citizens. after all, customers have a right to know the actual mileage they choose to purchase. i therefore ask you, commissioner, to advocate systemic legislative changes in this area.

in writing. - i voted in favour of the eu-peru agreement, which will allow visa-free travel for citizens of both parties for short stays of up to 90 days. this agreement is a milestone in the deepening of relations between the union and the peruvians. peru has one of the fastest growing economies in latin america and eu countries are among the largest investors. i believe that granting visa-free access will boost tourism and lead to even more intensive trade relations and more investment. visa-free travel will also make life easier for students, tourists and diplomats. it is also a further way to intensify cultural relations and strengthen political dialogue with peru, including on human rights and fundamental freedoms, good governance and the rule of law.

in writing. i voted to reduce emissions from off-road vehicles such as construction machinery, locomotives and small inland vessels, which are major contributors to air pollution. this adjustment will ensure that only machinery with engines complying with the new emission limits will be placed on the common market. we have to realize that non-road machines are responsible for up to 15% of all nitrogen emissions into the atmosphere, which is not a small amount. i believe that an agreement has been reached which balances well the need to protect the environment and the health of europeans and the competitiveness of european companies. i also welcome the aim of simplifying the current legal framework and simplifying administrative procedures leading to the removal of administrative burdens, which is in line with our long-term objective of better regulation in the eu.
in writing. on 5 july 2016, we voted at the european parliament plenary session in strasbourg on the proposal for a regulation on the requirements relating to emission limit values and type-approval of combustion engines in non-road mobile machinery. european legislation has always been more focused on emissions from transport and cars in general. personally, i'm not a big fan of the fact that when it comes to emissions, for example, agriculture, unlike other sectors, is getting a lot of substantial exemptions from the caps all the time. but they do contribute greatly to the quality of the air we breathe. so i was glad that this time there were finally vehicles and vehicles that were not designed for road transport, such as lawn mowers, bulldozers, diesel locomotives, or combine harvesters, etc. on the other hand, it must be admitted that these types of vehicles/machinery require a very different approach than normal passenger cars. this is only because their actual life span is much longer, even extending over decades. the proposed regulation is a reasonable compromise between protecting the environment and safeguarding the competitiveness of the sectors concerned. so i'm glad i could support this text.
in writing. - i voted against it. i don't agree with the eu regulating the emission limits of tractors or lawn mowers. national legislation is sufficient.
in writing. i supported the approval of emission limits for internal combustion engines, which affect a wide range of machines from chainsaws, lawn mowers, ship bulldozers and locomotives. the limits approved apply to newly manufactured machines and a transitional period of sufficient duration has been agreed to allow all manufacturers to prepare for the new situation. the new legislation will not directly affect the users of these machines, and gardeners will of course not have to carry their lawn mowers to any emissions checks. the justification for its adoption is both the unification of the hitherto fragmented national regulations, which will improve the functioning of the common market, and the improvement of air quality, since analyses show that off-road machinery is responsible for up to 15% of all nitrogen emissions into the atmosphere and 5% of particulate matter emissions. i believe that at the present state of technological development there is no excuse for tolerating excessive release of toxins into the air.
in writing. ‒ i have decided to support the proposal to introduce emission limits for combustion engines not intended for road transport. these include motorboats, lawn mowers, bulldozers, diesel locomotives, and diesel generators. the waste from these machines accounts for around 15% of total nox emissions and 5% of particulate matter emissions, and is estimated to increase to 19% by 2020, so it was necessary to address this issue. i believe that the new emission requirements should be in line with technological progress, but also stimulate it. another important element of this proposal was market harmonisation, which will contribute to the increased competitiveness of european products on international markets.
in writing. i supported the legislative resolution on the draft regulation on the requirements relating to emission limit values and type-approval of combustion engines in non-road mobile machinery. the resolution adopted by parliament contains amendments to the commission's original proposal which were informally negotiated with the member states. the council is yet to formally approve this regulation, which will then enter into force. the regulation replaces the 1997 directive. on the one hand, it will unify the 28 existing legal regimes into one, which is particularly welcomed by engine manufacturers. on the other hand, it modernizes an already somewhat outdated arrangement. the new regulation sets out the same rules in principle for all combustion engines, from those in locomotives to those in large construction machinery to those in chainsaws and lawnmowers. the emission limits limit the discharge of health-damaging nitrogen oxides (nox) and hazardous particulate matter from these engines in the future. the envi and imco colleagues have succeeded in refining the commission's original proposal and in bringing it into a form acceptable to both member states and industry representatives. i must emphasise in particular that the new limits will only apply to newly produced engines placed on the market. for consumers, nothing changes except that in the future their garden machines will emit less unhealthy exhaust gases.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of limiting emissions for non-road mobile machinery, such as small equipment, construction machinery, locomotives and inland waterway vessels, which contribute significantly to air pollution. this regulation will ensure that only engines in compliance with the new emission-limits requirements will be allowed to be placed on the internal market. in addition to protecting human health and the environment better, it will ensure the proper functioning of the internal market for engines in non-road mobile machinery by improving the general conditions for enforcement, in particular through stronger rules on market surveillance. i am particularly supportive of the aim to simplify the current legal framework and simplify administrative procedures, which is in line with my commitment to bring better regulation to the eu.

in writing. ‒ i welcome mr benifeia's efforts to contribute to the effective integration of refugees into the eu labour market. the report contains many important recommendations and suggestions. these include support for language and vocational education and literacy, equal rights for refugees to a wage in the country, involvement of civil society and voluntary organisations, etc. i could not support this resolution, however, because it contains fundamental points of concern with which i do not agree. this is mainly the adoption of a system of permanent redistribution of quotas. i believe that neither the permanent relocation mechanism nor the proposed asylum system are appropriate instruments to provide a lasting and acceptable solution to the migration crisis, nor will they contribute to the labour and social integration of the arriving refugees.
in writing. ‒ while i fully agree that labour market integration and social inclusion are the best ways to contribute to the good integration of migrants in the long term, i voted against the report. it contains certain elements which, in my view, are contrary to the objective of achieving a coherent migration policy. at this stage, it seems to me pointless to talk about a permanent relocation scheme binding on all member states and a common asylum system, as long as agreements on a broader framework for migration and asylum policy and an effective external border management are not yet finalised. i also do not share the view that the european parliament should order states to grant asylum seekers faster access to the labour market than the current directive allows. because that's something that states can do today, but they shouldn't be told to do.
in writing. the commission notes that the commission has not yet adopted a decision on the application of the principle of proportionality, as set out in article 108 (3) tfeu, to the principle of equal treatment for men and women. stresses that most member states do not meet the quotas for the reception of refugees; calls on the commission and the member states to start applying the relevant agreements as soon as possible and to speed up the process of accepting and resettling refugees; i remain convinced that quotas are a step in the wrong direction and do not contribute to creating an atmosphere of calm across european society. the resolution acknowledges that the refugee crisis is primarily a humanitarian crisis, caused inter alia by the destabilisation of the eu's neighbouring countries, but fails to identify the main culprits (nato, and in particular the us). i believe that the search for a solution to this situation is impossible without subjecting the actions that led to it to a critical analysis.
in writing. - i voted against it. i do not agree with the unification of eu asylum policy (there is an urgent need to establish a common asylum system) or with the call to adopt a permanent mechanism for the redistribution of migrants (there is a need to establish as soon as possible a permanent mechanism for their relocation within all member states).
in writing. ‒ i abstained because i and my group disagree with some of the points that were not taken up in the separate vote. for example, the requirement to allocate 25% of cohesion policy resources to the european social fund is an issue related to the establishment of the eu budget and should not be addressed in such a report. i also find some of the proposals concerning access to the labour market for asylum seekers controversial. the major problem that has affected my approach to the report is the willingness of some political groups to include in similar reports areas that are not directly related to their focus, which i consider to be a very bad practice.
‒ managing the refugee crisis is one of the main challenges facing the european union and its society today. the situation can only be addressed by a comprehensive approach, and i therefore regard the report adopted by the european parliament today as another important element in the mosaic of an integrated solution. it is essential that the challenges posed by migratory pressures in the fields of employment, education, social and health care become a source of economic and cultural development for our society. as a social democrat, i decided to support a new european agenda on migration to address the challenges of managing the unprecedented influx of people coming to the eu. this can only be achieved if the external and internal policies of the union and its member states are synergistic and complementary. i also strongly support the strengthening of the european social fund, which could help with the integration of refugees into society and their employment. in my view, this is the right way forward, and it should help to manage the situation in all eu member states. on the contrary, the cuts in the funds mentioned above or the punishment of malus and similar nonsense would only damage pan-european growth and significantly limit the management of the situation.
in writing. i could not support the resolution on the social integration and labour market of refugees. i agree that refugees need to be integrated into our societies. in this integration, we must learn from the mistakes of the past and avoid the creation of new ghettos and social exclusion leading to radicalisation. the resolution is based on the correct assumption that integration is most effective through the labour market. however, as often happens with non-binding parliamentary resolutions, paragraphs creep into the meaningful text that disqualify the text as a whole. the resolution calls for a shortening of the period after which asylum seekers whose applications have not been decided on are to have access to the labour market. our ppe group voted unsuccessfully against this point and we succeeded in closely enforcing at least the omission of the explicit call after the six-month period. i do not consider such challenges to be fortunate, we should leave the possible reductions to the member states, as the current legislation allows. i also cannot support calls for a targeted increase in the budgetary allocation for the european social fund. budgetary changes require a thorough expert assessment by the european commission, not politically motivated calls. the biggest problem with the text is that it expresses support for a proposal for a permanent system of relocation of asylum seekers. this question clearly has no place in the debate about refugee access to the labour market. unfortunately, we were unable to remove it from the text.
in writing. in today's vote on the report entitled 'refugees: social inclusion and employment', i abstained as i do not think it is effective to discuss the nature of the eu asylum system in a report on the integration and employment of refugees. i am aware that the debate on the common asylum system in particular touches on the problem of the social integration of refugees, but i believe that there are important parameters for a future common asylum system. but we're not talking about those here. as for the idea of a common asylum system, i do not reject it a priori. it should be noted, first of all, that the common asylum system in no way deprives the member states of their competence to assess applications for asylum. no one's proposing that change. the debate is only about the rules under which asylum applications will be assessed, but these will still be assessed by the member states' authorities, not by any of the eu institutions or agencies. i therefore believe that this debate is legitimate, it is supported by article 78 of the tfeu, which states that 'the union shall develop a common policy on asylum' and as a result it can contribute to reducing some of the so-called 'pull factors' that we are now seeing within the eu. however, the exact parameters of this envisaged system need to be discussed further.
in writing. ‒ while i fully agree that participation in the labour market and social inclusion are the best ways to ensure long-term integration for migrants, i voted against the report on the social inclusion and integration into the labour market of refugees. this is because it contains certain elements that are counterproductive to our efforts to achieving a coherent migration strategy for europe. in fact, agreeing on a permanent relocation mechanism and a common asylum system makes little sense so long as we have not yet agreed on the larger common approach to migration and organised our external borders effectively, and it might even jeopardise our efforts to find compromises on controversial issues.
in writing. i could not support the own-initiative report on the integration of refugees in the eu, even though it puts pressure on member states to introduce and enforce redistribution systems. but in my opinion, they will not solve the refugee crisis. these proposals are outdated and do not reflect the current evolution of the migration situation in the eu.
in writing. ‒ trade is clearly an important eu tool for ensuring cooperation with third countries and promoting democratic values in them, whether on environmental issues, human rights or corporate responsibility. trade has great potential for the eu, but unfortunately it is still not being fully exploited. i therefore supported the report which analyses the progress made by the commission in implementing such standards and makes new recommendations. the aim is to strike a balance between economic diplomacy and the removal of trade barriers, to ensure greater cooperation between development aid and trade policy, to promote binding measures that ensure that firms pay taxes in the country where they do business. at the same time, the report points out that trade policy deserves to be an eu priority.
in writing. i was very happy to support the report on the implementation of parliament's 2010 recommendations on social and environmental standards, human rights and corporate social responsibility. i think it is important that the european parliament really controls the commission's activities (especially the current ones) and ensures that the commission is still acting as it should. in particular, i appreciated that the report recognised that universal access to public goods such as water, health and education are essential elements that demonstrate a member state's capacity to respect human rights and to ensure social justice. the commission should realise that this is the way to make eu citizens' lives better, not its directives and quotas.
in writing. i supported the report which rightly emphasises the importance of trade and foreign investment as important tools for achieving economic growth, sustainable development and the protection of human rights. i am convinced that well-designed trade and direct investment regimes increase prosperity in poorer countries and that increased prosperity is a prerequisite for better protection of human and social rights and workers' rights and better protection of the environment.
in writing. ‒ the european union is the biggest player in world trade. that is why i consider it very important that in the conclusion of trade agreements, a strong emphasis is placed on social and environmental standards, human rights and also corporate social responsibility. i voted in favour of this report because i consider it very important that the commission ensures that development policy is consistent with its trade strategy, which includes fair taxation. i therefore supported the provision that taxes should be paid where economic activity takes place. while foreign investment and trade generally lead to economic growth and increased prosperity, this does not mean that the same thing happens to improvements in human rights protection and the overall environment. deforestation and forest degradation also show a negative relationship between these two factors. there is therefore a need for multinational enterprises and groups to play a much greater role and provide positive incentives in the field of protection. in particular, they should ensure, for example, responsible logging, felling and commodity sourcing, as well as social justice. i voted to put far greater responsibility on the shoulders of the companies in this respect. the commission must become more stringent and ensure that the principles laid down in the un framework are applied consistently.
in writing. as a social democrat, i consider this report to be very important, as some of the basic principles of the functioning of european society are often forgotten nowadays, namely human rights, corporate social responsibility and, last but not least, social and environmental standards. it is essential that our high european standards are taken into account today, when the european union is negotiating several important international agreements. it is necessary that rules for the protection of european workers are also firmly anchored in international treaties. last but not least, i consider it essential that the report adopted by the european parliament calls for greater transparency in the negotiation of international agreements, such as the ttip agreement.
in writing. as tragedy such as the rana plaza factory collapse in bangladesh has shown, european consumers are also closely concerned by the working and social conditions of workers in third countries. compliance with basic social, labour and environmental standards should therefore be guaranteed in all trade agreements concluded by the european union. this applies not only to companies in third countries but also, and in particular, to companies established in the european union but operating outside its borders. such actions can contribute to achieving sustainable development or to combating forced and child labour, which is why i was happy to support this report.
in writing. ‒ trade is an important tool for the european union to promote democratic values in third countries, such as environmental and social standards, human rights and corporate responsibility. this is why i voted in favour of this report, which analyses the progress achieved by the commission in implementing these standards and provides new recommendations. the recommendations aim to reflect the right balance between economic diplomacy and diminishing trade barriers, by ensuring greater coordination between development aid and trade policy, promoting binding measures to ensure that companies pay taxes where their economic activity takes place, and advocating that this issue is given priority on the agenda.
in writing. ‒ i very much welcome the new strategy proposed by the commission entitled ‘trade for all – towards a more responsible trade and investment policy’. therefore, i also support this resolution. one of our biggest future challenges will be to keep the eu’s position as a global trade player; for that, it is necessary to have solid trade agreements with third countries, which would bring more jobs and growth. we have to waive protectionist practices and support free trade outside of the european union just as we have done within it.
in writing. ‒ if the european union is to maintain its economic importance in the face of competition from the rest of the world, it needs a truly effective, comprehensive and progressive trade strategy. that is why i voted in favour of a resolution calling for greater participation and accountability of all stakeholders involved in trade and greater transparency, in particular to win the trust of citizens. the requirement of regular annual reports on implementation is certainly important, as it will enable the eu to achieve the best possible strategy in the light of current requirements.
in writing. ‒ i could not support the european parliament's resolution on a new and innovative future strategy for trade and investment. the business is not self-sufficient. it is intended to contribute to social, economic, political prosperity and stability, to sustainable economic development, to social progress, to cultural diversity and to the creation of quality jobs. it's supposed to raise living standards, and the resolution didn't mention that. moreover, it did not indicate that more and more citizens were openly criticizing and even rejecting free trade agreements. they do not address all these issues and have a profound and long-term impact on the national and regional development of trading partners, on their ability to develop their own production capacities in order to guarantee long-term sustainable economic performance contributing to economic growth and the prosperity of citizens. this includes the current negative impacts on macroeconomic and microeconomic relationships and conditions that very often cause disruption of smes, job losses, the relocation of entire sectors to third countries, environmental and social dumping, the disappearance of family farms and medium-sized enterprises, the limitation of access to basic public services, the limitation of cultural diversity, as well as the exacerbation of negative trends such as climate change and persistent poverty, both in developing and in developed countries.

in writing. i supported the report, which, among other things, welcomed the commission's reference to the efforts of the new investment court system to replace the criticised and unpredictable private arbitration, while stressing that this investment court system must be in line with the eu legal order, in particular the jurisdiction of courts in the eu, and in particular with eu competition law. in this context, i support the commission's approach to ttip so far, including the fact that it has increased transparency and openness at all stages of trade negotiations.
in writing. ‒ an innovative approach has played and will continue to play a key role in the eu economy in the future. we must realise that the importance of the eu economy in the world as a whole will decline in the future, even though it is currently the richest economic area in the world. the center of wealth creation is shifting eastward to the asia-pacific region, which is a trend that i don't think we can stop, but we have to respond to it in the right way. this is why debates on future innovative strategies are so important for trade and investment. as a socially-democratically minded politician, i believe that the system for protecting the union's trade needs to be modernised, also in view of the fact that china will continue to seek to be granted market economy status. we must not allow jobs to be threatened and unemployment to rise, leading to a fall in european exports or a disproportionate increase in imports, especially in certain sectors. on the contrary, it is necessary to go a step further and define trade and investment agreements in such a way as to promote sustainable development and not to allow a decline in labour and social standards, including environmental sustainability.
in writing. the european parliament adopted a resolution, to which i also contributed, on the european union's trade strategy. in it, the european parliament recalls the role of the european union in the world and stresses that trading in a sustainable and responsible way is the most powerful tool for promoting european interests and values abroad. eu citizens are often concerned about the potential impact of trade agreements that europe negotiates with its trading partners. in this resolution, for example, the european parliament stresses the need for greater transparency in negotiations or for a comprehensive analysis of the impact of the european union's trade initiatives and asks the european commission to provide data on the impact of trade agreements already concluded, in particular on small and medium-sized enterprises, the environment, etc. the european parliament also touches on non-eu countries in this resolution, mentioning the importance of new markets for european agricultural production, but also calling for development aid. funds such as the european development fund (edf) are intended to support, for example, the fight against poverty or to tackle the causes behind migration. the resolution also talks about cooperation with specific countries, and in the resolution i supported the call for the european commission to start negotiations on an investment agreement with taiwan immediately.
in writing. ‒ while the eu is the wealthiest economy worldwide, an effective, comprehensive and forward-looking trade and investment strategy is of vital importance if we want to keep our economic importance in the face of the growing competition from other continents. this is why i voted in favour of this resolution, which calls for more transparency, engagement and accountability towards all stakeholders involved in the trade, namely to regain the confidence of citizens regarding the benefits of international trade. i particularly agree with the need for regular updates and annual implementation reports that will allow us to achieve the best possible strategy.
in writing. ‒ i have decided to support this report because i am aware that an effective, comprehensive and forward-looking trade and investment strategy is of crucial importance for the european union. at the same time, i am aware of the concerns that the citizens have. many european citizens associate globalisation with job losses. i therefore believe that trade policy in the 21st century must respond to citizens' concerns. we therefore need more transparency, involvement and accountability with all stakeholders. in my view, given the rapidly changing global business environment, the trade strategy should be regularly updated and the commission should report in detail on its implementation on an annual basis, in order to allow european citizens to have a look.

in writing. i supported the european parliament's report on global trends in human trafficking. trafficking in human beings is a modern form of slavery and a serious crime that constitutes one of the worst violations of human rights. it is tragic that in the 21st century, human trafficking is still a lucrative business worldwide, linked to other crimes, such as money laundering. unfortunately, this is facilitated by the absence or lack of legislation in many countries of the world. the revenues from human trafficking are thus returned to the financial systems. the report offers an overview of the different forms of trafficking in human beings, but also suggests concrete forms of cooperation to combat it at regional and international level. eu policy in building relations with third countries, e.g. exchange of best practices, training of police and humanitarian workers on how to communicate with victims, etc. at eu level, a position of coordinator for the fight against trafficking in human beings has been created to improve coordination between eu institutions, agencies and member states with third countries and international actors. the report focuses separately on trafficking in migrants, who are among the least vulnerable groups, especially women and children. europol has warned that more than 10,000 unaccompanied refugees and migrant children have disappeared in europe.

in writing. azerbaijan is one of the caspian countries with significant oil and natural gas deposits. these deposits have been exploited since the end of the 19th century. at present, the export of oil and natural gas provides a substantial part of the income of this caucasian state. in the recent past, the eu has attempted to prepare a project for a gas pipeline from the caspian sea region through turkey and the balkans. unfortunately, this platonic effort to prepare a project called nabucco ended in failure. the basic prerequisite for the construction of the pipeline is to ensure sufficient natural gas, which the eu politicians of that time failed to do. on the one hand, the sanctions against iran, on the other hand, the lack of resource capacity in azerbaijan (about 1/3 of the total planned capacity). the economic crisis of the late 1990s and the subsequent recession did not create favourable conditions for the project. azerbaijan has been at war with armenia for many years (a territorial dispute over nagorno-karabakh), but its relationship with turkey is smooth. on the contrary, relations with iran have always been marked by a certain nervousness, given that a significant azerbaijani minority lives just beyond the common border. the elections in azerbaijan can be considered democratic in the asian context, in the eu context, reservations are regularly made about the electoral procedure and the implementation itself. i support the conclusion of a protocol to the partnership agreement, even with these limits in mind.

in writing. ‒ today's report from the imco committee is a very important topic, and that is cybersecurity. we live in a digitalised age and technology is developing so fast that society is unable to respond adequately and in a timely manner to new challenges. the so-called hacker attacks and their ingenuity are escalating all the time. i agree that prevention and protective measures are more than adequate. i supported the report, albeit with the caveat that i hope that increased security measures will not lead to the restriction and censorship of the internet as a common means of everyday communication nowadays. we need to find a balanced approach that protects information technology users while not restricting freedom of expression and the right to information.
in writing. i supported the agreement reached by the ep and the council because i consider the resilience and stability of network and information systems to be a fundamental prerequisite for the completion of the digital single market and the smooth functioning of the internal market. existing capacities and mechanisms for ensuring network and information security are unable to keep pace with the rapidly changing nature of threats and to guarantee a common high level of protection in all member states. it should also be noted that, despite the initiatives taken, the level of capacity and preparedness varies widely between member states and there is a fragmentation of approaches across the eu. the eu currently lacks an effective mechanism for effective cooperation and reliable information sharing on risks and breaches of network and information security between member states. as a result, there is insufficient protection against security incidents across the eu. it is also possible that barriers to the internal market and the associated compliance costs may arise for undertakings operating in more than one member state.
in writing. i supported the resulting network and information security directive, which aims at a secure and trusted digital environment across the eu. the directive is the first step towards creating eu-wide measures to counter cyberattacks. they are among the biggest online threats in the global world and their number is growing, therefore there is a need for closer cooperation between member states in the field of network and information security in the first place. i consider it particularly important to establish a network of national cybersecurity incident response teams.
in writing. i was very happy to support the directive on measures to ensure a high common level of network and information security in the union. this directive aims to ensure a high level of security in the european digital area. there is currently no common eu mechanism for effective cooperation in cases of breaches of security networks and information between member states. the new legislation should change this and guarantee security in this area, which is so crucial today. in the future, all member states should be equipped both technically and organisationally to prevent incidents that threaten to disrupt the functioning of entire businesses, public institutions, information servers, internet banking or misuse of eu citizens' personal data. today, at a time when information warfare is more powerful than ground warfare, at a time when russia is using propaganda as one of its most powerful weapons, at a time when the internet is the most powerful tool of terrorism, it is in my view essential to ensure adequate and uniform protection in the area on which the functioning of our entire society is built.
in writing. ‒ while the digitisation of our common economy is bringing unequalled new opportunities, it is essential that we protect its critical infrastructure such as energy, transport, banks, financial markets and health from security incidents and cybercrime. this is why i voted in favour of this report, which sets out measures to achieve a high, coordinated and common level of security of networks and information systems within the eu. it will improve the resilience and stability of network and information systems essential to the smooth functioning of the internal market, and will also increase the trust in and modernisation of ict that are necessary to guarantee the success of the digital single market.
in writing. i voted in favour of the proposal on energy efficiency labelling following the european commission's decision to update the legislation in this area. the original a to c scale, indicating the energy efficiency of appliances mainly white goods (refrigerators, freezers, etc.), needed to be reclassified due to the increase in products with better efficiency and the subsequent existence of a+, a++ or a+++ categories. given the evidence that this labelling is already confusing consumers and discouraging them from buying the most energy-efficient products, i was in favour of modifying the scale to now label products from a to g. the aim of this labelling is to encourage consumers to purchase energy-efficient products, which are therefore less harmful to the environment. accurate, clear and comparable energy consumption information anywhere in the eu is therefore crucial. i also agree with stricter monitoring of compliance with labelling rules and better cooperation and exchange of information in this area.
in writing. energy labels are a very interesting marketing ploy these days, but unfortunately, they're losing their effectiveness. as the energy consumption of individual appliances is reduced, the original scale becomes less clear and the simplicity of the whole marking is lost. consumers are logically asking what could be better than an a-rated device. it's not a secret to the experts that it could be a+, a++, a+++, etc. the fact that the labeling needs to change is obvious to almost everyone, progress cannot be stopped. the high-end appliances of 20 years ago may not be the high-end of today. the question, of course, is whether the period of category changes (shifts) should be 10 years or more or less. this does not change the fact that it is appropriate to simply indicate the degree of economy or lack of economy of new appliances. the form of a regulation is clearly appropriate in this case. i believe that the vast majority of meps will support this material as i do. however, the question is whether extremely energy-efficient electrical equipment will actually have a stable low electricity consumption and will be fully functional, even mechanically, after a few years.
