in writing. ‒ i support the final version of the european border and coast guard regulation and am glad that i was able to vote for it in the ep. i especially appreciate the work of our newsman, who brought this report to a successful conclusion in record time. the proposal is such convincing evidence to voters that the union is able to find common solutions in the area of primary concern ensuring security at the external borders. the new agency will be composed of frontex and national authorities. it's a shared responsibility. the states will thus remain fully responsible for the protection of the borders. new union mechanisms will only be introduced at the request of a state or in the event of unmanageable migratory pressures. the agency will reassess the ability of states to deal with border pressures. after assessing the situation, it shall make recommendations to the member state or, where appropriate, adopt a decision defining specific measures. in cases where border control is ineffective and the schengen system is threatened, the council, acting by a qualified majority, may decide to activate the european border guard. it is good that the original proposal, where the commission itself was to decide on intervention at the borders, has been replaced by a qualified council decision. the regulation does not therefore restrict the sovereignty of states in addressing migration. the agency has also increased its flexibility. it has its own budget, staff, and equipment. it also has a new reserve team of 1 500 border guards, which can be deployed within 5 working days.
in writing. ‒ the regulation, which i strongly supported and for which i was the shadow rapporteur in the committee on foreign affairs, aims to substantially improve the current functioning of the protection of the schengen area. with unprecedented pressure on the external borders at a time when the capacity of individual member states at the union's external border may fail, it is imperative to adapt the rules to allow for a rapid response, even in the face of the unprecedented strain europe is currently experiencing. in particular, a european border and coast guard is hereby established. while the name evokes the idea of a transnational body, the epps actually defines two components. it is the european border and coast guard agency (which will be created from the existing frontex agency with rationally extended powers and staff) and the national authorities responsible for border management. they will continue to fulfil their existing duties, but will cooperate more closely with the agency, etc. the procedure is qualitatively new and can be applied when a situation arises where a failure by one member state to protect part of its external border may endanger the functioning of the entire schengen area. in this case, the council may decide to correct the situation even without the request of the member state concerned. in such a case, for example, a so-called 'reserve rapid reaction team' of 1 500 border guards may also be deployed. they are to be released from the member states within five days. schengen must be maintained.
in writing. i supported the establishment of a european border and coast guard as i regard its creation as an important step towards a future better system of protection of the eu's common external borders. the protection of the external borders remains a competence of the member states, but the transformation of frontex into the european border and coast guard agency will strengthen the elements of the common external border management and introduce new possibilities for the use of agency staff directly in a place where the management of the external borders is not adequately performed by a member state and this lack of performance threatens the proper functioning of the schengen area without internal border controls. the migration crisis as a complex problem will not be solved by establishing a common border guard alone. similar attention should be given to other proposals, particularly in the area of asylum legislation.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of establishing a european border and coast guard, which i see as promising first step towards achieving an integrated european border management. this will allow us to preserve the mobility of people and goods inside the schengen space, one of the most visible achievements of european integration, but which has been threatened by the expansion of irregular migration, security threats and the shortcomings of frontex. the ebcg will consist of the european border and coast guard agency as well as of national authorities responsible for border management. this new agency will be given a monitoring and supervisory role, a new mandate for search and rescue operations, and acquire a rapid reserve of 1 500 european border guards and other relevant staff. i am particularly pleased that the agency’s role in return policy is strengthened, and that the necessary safeguards to guarantee that the fundamental rights of both refugees and migrants are fully respected.

in writing. ‒ as a member of the committee on budgetary control, i note that after long debates and not a very constructive approach on the part of the political group of the ppe in particular, a compromise text was found on the new rules for the functioning of the secretariat of the supervisory committee for the european anti-fraud office (olaf). it is undeniable that we need effective working relations between olaf and its supervisory committee to enhance the protection of the eu's financial interests. these relations had been severely disrupted in previous years and new structures had to be set up. the secretariat of the supervisory committee will now operate independently of olaf's structures, thus strengthening the independence of the supervisory committee. i also consider it essential that the decision taken will have no impact on the european budget. the secretariat's financial allocation has merely been transferred to the budget of the european commission, within whose structures the secretariat will operate. however, i am of the opinion that the change in structure itself is only a framework for improving relations between the institutions in question, not a solution of their own. i will continue to support any steps that lead to the normalisation of relations between olaf and its supervisory committee.
in writing. i supported the report on strengthening the independence of the olaf supervisory committee secretariat and the related amendment to the existing olaf regulation. the potential risk of conflict of interest and the need to strengthen the independent position of the secretariat of olaf's supervisory body have been the subject of calls from the european parliament to the commission and exchanges of views between the council, parliament, the commission and the director-general of olaf in recent years. where the secretariat is to provide direct support to the work of the supervisory committee, which oversees the proper performance of the investigative function of olaf as a whole, the application of procedural safeguards and the duration of individual fraud investigations, it is in the interest of the proper functioning of the office that the secretariat should act independently and without any conflict of interest. however, the independence of the secretariat is undermined by the unsatisfactory wording of article 15 (8) of the regulation, which provides that the secretariat is to be provided by the office itself. as a result, the director-general decides directly on the promotions and promotions of the staff of the authority's secretariat. a possible conflict of interest between the staff of the secretariat of the supervisory authority and the staff of the olaf management authority is therefore not excluded. the new arrangement is designed to avoid conflicts of interest by strengthening the staff and financial independence of the secretariat. the secretariat will not be provided by the office but by the commission and the budget for the secretariat will be transferred from the olaf budget line to the commission budget. i also welcome the emphasis on the confidentiality of the data processed by secretariat staff.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour the resolution on the secretariat of the european anti-fraud office (olaf). the secretariat will now be integrated into the commission’s structure, thus clearly separating it from the committee and its budget that it is mandated to supervise. i believe that this is an essential measure to strengthen the independence of the olaf supervisory committee’s secretariat, thus increasing the effectiveness of the supervisory committee as well as the credibility of our institutions.

in writing. the report of the budget committee on the preparation of the post-election revision of the multiannual financial framework (mff) 2014-2020 shall constitute a recommendation of the european parliament to the european commission. it is expected to present a draft revision of the mff in autumn 2016 which will revise the financial programmes to better reflect current needs. the ep's main recommendations include a call for increased ceilings (in commitments) to deal with the migration and refugee crisis, youth unemployment and competitiveness. the ep also recommends revising the ceiling for payments upwards to avoid a repeat of the eu's insolvency. the revision should not affect the national envelopes for the structural funds or for agricultural policy. the final text of the resolution, however, unfortunately contains a number of problematic points. all of them are mentioned in point 53, which refers to the conditionality of the funds depending on how the member states fulfil their obligations under the compulsory relocation of refugees (permanent quotas), i.e. a bonus malus at european level. in other words, the commission should propose a system whereby countries which fulfil or fail to fulfil these commitments would lose part of the structural funds. this demand is absolutely unacceptable and it led me, along with other points, to not support the resolution in the end.

in writing. ‒ i very much welcome the fact that the european parliament, thanks to my vote, has today passed a number of concrete proposals to combat tax fraud by large multinational companies. the fight against tax evasion and tax havens is one of the key political priorities of the social democrats in the european parliament. the report approved today was the result of a special committee on taxation set up 18 months ago in response to the luxleaks scandal and subsequently strengthened after the panama papers scandal. the report adopted today contains several important proposals, such as the preparation of a single list of tax havens (including a blacklist and specific sanctions), the introduction of automatic sanctions for non-cooperative jurisdictions, and sanctions for banks, law firms and advisers that cooperate with them. the house also calls for a binding law to limit the abuse of so-called patent boxes (special tax incentives for patent holders operating in the jurisdictions of certain eu member states). the proposal adopted today is not only a clear message to multinational corporations that their unfair practices may lead to the termination of their business activities in the future, but also a proposal for a way forward to gradually put an end to harmful tax practices that cost the eu billions of euros a year.

in writing. i voted in favour of the motion calling on japan to end whaling and to respect the conclusions of the international whaling commission (iwc). the whole gue/ngl group is unanimous in supporting this proposal, which was adopted by parliament with 87% of the votes cast in favour. japan's actions violate international obligations to protect marine mammals, violate the iwc moratorium on all commercial whaling, which is intended to protect the whale population from extinction and allow its recovery. however, the iwc contains a special permit that allows the capture of a limited number of whales for strictly scientific purposes. japan uses this special permit, but the vast majority of whales appear on a plate rather than under a microscope. japan continues to disregard the 2014 ruling of the international court of justice to end whaling for insufficiently beneficial scientific research. that is why i support the maintenance of a global moratorium on commercial whaling, i also support the prohibition of international trade in whale products, i call for an end to whaling for scientific purposes and i am in favour of designating sufficiently large areas of oceans and seas as nature reserves where whaling will be banned. japan is our strategic partner, and our relationship is based on shared values, including an unwavering belief in effective multilateralism and a rules-based international order that both sides should respect.

in writing. ‒ in 1982 the international whaling commission (iwc) put in place a moratorium on all commercial whaling, with an exception for scientific research purposes, in order to protect stocks from extinction and allow them to recover. despite this ban that is still in place, japan, amongst other countries, has continued its whaling activities, killing over 20 000 whales up to 2014. in 2015, it announced its decision to resume whaling under a new scientific research programme. this is why i voted in favour of this resolution, which calls on japan to stop its whaling activities and to abide by the iwc moratorium. these activities undermine biodiversity and marine ecosystems, breach the iwc standards and international law, and are based on the unfounded stipulation that genuine scientific research requires the large-scale and regular killing of whales.

in writing. in sub-saharan africa, we have the most extreme forms of persecution, the most extreme human rights violations against people with albinism. they face societal discrimination, verbal attacks, exclusion from public services. they're threatened with death, kidnapping, rape, or maiming. discrimination can lead to lifelong trauma and psychosocial problems. people with albinism often lack access to adequate health care and education. despite international media coverage of the problem and the adoption of new legislation, very few people are prosecuted and convicted, and crimes and torture still occur. the greatest threat to people with albinism in africa is widespread superstition about the special, magical powers of their bodies that bring good luck, wealth and health. this leads smugglers to hunt albino animals and then trade their bodies. in 2015, there were 448 attacks on albinos in 25 african countries, a figure that is likely even lower than the actual number, as authorities do not systematically monitor and document such crimes. it should be remembered that persons with albinism have the right to live as others do without fear, as stated in the 1948 declaration of human rights.

in writing. an estimated 80 million people in the eu are living with a disability. of these, 46 million are women. the charter of fundamental rights and freedoms of the eu explicitly prohibits discrimination on the grounds of disability in articles 21 and 26 and provides for the equal participation of persons with disabilities in the life of society. the eu has ratified the un convention on the rights of persons with disabilities and the un body has therefore monitored how the eu fulfils its obligations in this area. disabled people still face problems in accessing the labour market. the employment gap with non-disabled persons is 22% and with women it is 21%. it makes it very difficult to live an active, independent life. it was noted that the eu did not formally consult organisations representing persons with disabilities in 2015 when drawing up the progress report. it therefore requests the organisations representing these persons to participate actively in the next reviews. the eu is invited to ratify the optional protocol to the convention on the rights of persons with disabilities. the commission is invited to take into account the eu's shared commitment to building a barrier-free europe when assessing the social situation in the member states. the report covers a wide range of demands for barrier-free access in all areas, from transport to political rights to emergency calls. it will not be easy to work out at least a timetable for bringing all the requirements into the eu's life.

mr. chairman, madam commissioner, in the famous series "of course, mr. minister", it is stated that if you do not want the truth to come out and everything to be covered up, you will set up a committee of inquiry. i am very pleased that the european parliament has decided to make full use of the potential of the committee of inquiry. but good intentions often come with a penalty, and so we have to face the commission's non-cooperation, the automobile companies' excuses, the shifting of responsibility, the blaming of others, and so on. the emis investigation committee is trying to uncover what we all know for a long time, that the whole scandal has been known for a long time, but has been covered up by all the parties involved. but we are struck by the resistance of those who should be held accountable, and their arrogance, which forces us to reveal the truth even more. i thank all my colleagues for their cooperation and let me thank in particular the chairman of the committee of inquiry, whose systematic approach proves that it is possible to achieve a successful outcome.
mr president, during the last year we have learnt a lot not about volkswagen, but mostly about the enforcement of eu regulation, about how division of responsibility between the union and the state works, and about the behaviour or ethics of some of the firms. it was very sad to learn all this, and frustrating, but we have got a chance to change things for the better. i am not afraid that industry cannot do it or that it is too expensive: industry just needs to have very clear and simple rules to follow. i do not believe that blaming and shaming should be a key part of the committee work. we should be focused on the future: that is the most important thing. we should start with understanding the basic facts and i will try to describe some of them. firstly, i believe that only cars complying with the rules should be allowed onto the market. that is what we must do: we have proper rules and these are the only way to avoid unnecessary health risks. we know that, by using existing technologies, even current diesel cars can be made clean. what will happen in the future is hard to tell because technology is evolving so quickly. we were late in introducing better laboratory testing. we are now on track. we must make sure that any altering of vehicles for testing will be prohibited. real driving tests and random sampling should be a very important component of a future better system and should be supported alongside independent testing. i believe that this general failure on our part should be turned into victory, namely into a new system that will be better for us all and that we must bring about.
mr president, commissioner, the work being done by the committee of inquiry into emissions measurements is really giving a comprehensive picture of the technical systems of combustion engines, especially diesel engines. we learned a tremendous amount of information, not only about the technical aspects, but also about the processes involved in preparing and approving the necessary legislation. it's really instructive to me personally how the strong political pressure to reduce co2 emissions, which is at the edge of technical possibilities, leads to huge problems. it pushes manufacturers to engage in unacceptable practices, to the point of fraud, as in the case of vw, and it also puts the official controls in a difficult situation. i believe that the outcome of the work of the committee of inquiry will not only be a description of what actually happened with the manufacturers or in the preparation of the legislation, but mainly how to approach any regulations in the future. the legislative regulatory measures adopted must ensure technically achievable conditions for inspection and uniform procedures for the type-approval of vehicles in the various eu countries.
mr president, i supported this report because cohesion policy is, of course, a subject that moves europe, and i think we should not be left behind. in this sense, it is important that we add even more intelligent specialisation, more science, to cohesion policy, this intelligent specialisation should be part of cohesion policy. multi-level governance should be expanded and its capacities increased. the participatory approach in cohesion policy should also be subordinated to regional decision-making. i supported this report, we discussed it in the committee on regional development and i think it is a good basis for further work on intelligent specialisation.
in writing. ‒ i supported this resolution because ris3 will allow our regions to remain competitive, create more quality jobs and achieve sustainable growth by helping them develop in the areas of their strength. put differently, smart specialisation means that these regions will be able to focus in priority sectors where they have the biggest competitive potential. i believe in the participatory approach of this strategy that concentrates on targeted research and innovation programmes but at the same time offers support for regions and businesses to take full advantage of the new technologies and knowledge. this way we will be able to bridge the development and innovation gap in europe.

in writing. ‒ in an increasingly competitive global environment, it is crucial that the eu keeps improving its capacity to innovate. i voted in favour of the report on cohesion policy and research and innovation strategies for smart specialisation, as these strategies will be valuable to overcome europe’s innovation gap and encourage growth. in fact, by combining and bringing together different policies, including those for entrepreneurship, education and innovation, ris3 enables regions to identify and select priority areas for their development and investments. ris3 is also a condition for receiving european structural and investment funds (esif), and therefore contributes to an increased performance orientation on the ground. moreover, i am very supportive of including a review of the strategies after 2017, in order to ensure their continuing relevance and maximise their output.

in writing. on 13 september 2016, we voted on the report on european territorial cooperation best practices and innovative measures at the european parliament plenary session in strasbourg. some 38% of europe's population live in border areas. as i am myself actively involved in the programme of cooperation between the moravian-silesian region and its border regions, and aware of the various problems that often plague this cooperation, this topic is quite close to my heart. the fundamental objective of european territorial cooperation is to reduce the impact of borders in order to reduce disparities between regions, to remove remaining obstacles to investment and to enhance cross-border cooperation, to strengthen cohesion and to promote the harmonious economic, social, cultural and territorial development of the union as a whole. european territorial cooperation, in my view, contributes to peace, stability and regional integration. the rapporteur has succeeded in integrating the need to develop a common approach to cross-border innovation, such as joint research, mobility programmes, joint research infrastructures, etc. the report mentions that cultural cooperation should be one of the objectives of european territorial cooperation and points out that cultural and educational cooperation needs to be promoted in border areas, as people living on opposite sides of the border often share a cultural and linguistic heritage. i think the report is fairly balanced, which is why i was happy to support it.

in writing. ‒ european territorial cooperation, also known as interreg, has been essential in cross-border, transnational, and interregional cooperation. etc currently services 28 member states’ and regional development cooperation programmes outside of the eu. as etc now only represents 2.8% of the cohesion policy budget, i am disappointed in the budget cuts. these cuts will negatively impact areas like the single market, the digital market, mobility, energy, research, education, health, the environment and culture. i hope to preserve etc post-2020 by increasing its funds because of its important role and positive impact on the european integration project. it has played a significant part in enhancing economic, social and territorial potential of the regions, so increasing its future funding is integral in maximising the regions’ full utility. i call on the commission and member states to work together with parliament towards preserving european territorial cooperation as an important tool in the european integration process.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report which looked at best practices and innovative measures for european territorial cooperation (etc), an important instrument of cohesion policy designed to solve problems which transcend administrative borders and require common solutions. while the etc has been proven to be an effective instrument, best practice and particularly innovative measures have the potential to develop the fund even further by encouraging synergies between actors and programmes, reduce the administrative burden on beneficiaries, and simplify the implementation of its programmes. however, the etc budget of eur 10.1 billion represents 2.8% of the cohesion policy budget, which does not match the great challenges that etc has to meet.

in writing. i am very pleased that in december 2015 the european parliament decided to set up a committee of inquiry of 45 members to investigate alleged breaches or maladministration in the application of union law in relation to emission measurements in the automotive industry. the emis committee's inquiry focuses on compliance with the obligations laid down in regulation (ec) no 715/2007, with the task of collecting and analysing information to determine whether the commission and the member states had evidence of the use of disconnecting devices, and to collect and analyse information on the implementation of directive 2007/46/ec by the member states. as a social democrat, i am committed to greater transparency in today's world, and i therefore appreciate the possibility of following expert and witness testimony through a verbatim recording of the hearing in english, which will also be published on the emis website. i believe that the final report of the committee of inquiry will bring new insights which will be useful not only for the evaluation of this case around emissions in the automotive industry but also for the judicial authorities.
in writing. the interim report on the inquiry into emission measurements in the automotive industry confirms the mandate and the continuation of the work of the committee of inquiry beyond the half-term of its mandate. it also calls on the parties concerned, in particular the european commission, to provide timely support and full transparency to the investigation process. that is why i supported the report. in view of the ongoing process of hearing invited guests, this is a purely technical document as the committee does not want to anticipate any conclusions, even partial ones, before the end of its own investigation. a summary of the committee's actual work and the findings will be contained in a final report to be adopted by the european parliament in accordance with its mandate after the year of work.

in writing. natural gas and electricity prices are interesting from a number of points of view. one of the most important reasons why these prices should be compulsorily monitored in the long term is the comparability of the data collected. both gas and electricity supply are typical network industries at present. fortunately, electricity and gas parameters are common across the eu (voltage stability and frequency for alternating current, quality parameters for natural gas). however, the price to the final consumer has at least two components, the price per quantity (normal cubic metres of gas, kwh) and the price per delivery. in particular, for the various 'prices for supply', we see the need to define which charges will be included in the price of energy under the heading of transport, or network use, and which under the heading of the amount of energy consumed. these are in particular excise duties and variously structured network charges. the regulation aims to harmonise the methodology for reporting prices and thus to remove any uncertainties identified. this is how we can obtain reliable statistical information. the reference periods, the frequency of data transmission and the possibility of granting derogations are defined. the report is quite clear, and i hope that the practical application of this regulation will not be subject to any major ambiguities. since the adoption of this regulation repeals directive 2008/92/ec, there is no increase in the number of existing eu directives and regulations. i therefore support the adoption of the report.
in writing. on 13 september 2016, we voted on the report on the draft regulation on european gas and electricity price statistics at the european parliament's plenary session in strasbourg. gas and electricity price statistics are part of the european energy statistics system managed by eurostat. the aim of this regulation is to transform the collection of data on natural gas and electricity prices charged to final customers households from a voluntary basis to a mandatory one. i personally support the idea of collecting data on the prices of natural gas and electricity paid by consumers in different countries, as this will increase transparency and may help protect households and final consumers from the questionable pricing practices of some energy and gas suppliers. this step is also necessary for the quality of the electricity and gas price survey data. however, the report itself is written in the spirit of the eu moving towards a complete, common internal energy market, which i cannot agree with at all. i have long held the view that the issue of energy supply and production is a matter for the sovereign powers of the national states alone and should not be transferred to the pan-european level. the debate on the document itself was not helped by the fact that some of my colleagues tried to insert changes in the text in favour of nuclear energy. that's why i had to abstain.
in writing. - i voted against it. i do not agree with the extension of the scope of mandatory reporting for statistical purposes, which is unnecessarily burdensome for companies.
in writing. ‒ today we discussed a report setting out the procedure for collecting and transmitting statistical data to the european commission and eurostat respectively on gas and electricity prices. the regulation we discussed today aims to make the collection of data compulsory rather than voluntary. i would probably have no problem with that in principle, although i don't see any convincing guarantees of consumer/customer data protection in the regulation. however, i do not agree that the rapporteur is proposing changes to the cost breakdown, nor does the proposal specify who will be responsible for the price breakdown, nor does it define the term 'fees'. these shortcomings are the reason why i abstained from voting.
in writing. i supported the report on the regulation which aims to make data collection compulsory rather than voluntary, so that data are available for the largest possible part of the market and in high quality. since price data should continue to be collected by the competent national authorities, no additional bureaucratic burden should be imposed. some provisions concerning the authorities carrying out the collection and the companies providing the data are being simplified. it should also avoid misunderstandings that could, in the extreme, lead to data sets not being comparable. it is also necessary to define 'charges' in order to correct the current unsatisfactory situation where it is possible to shift charges from the grid to energy and vice versa. the approved changes to the cost structure should better reflect the pricing structure.
in writing. ‒ i supported this report on proposal for a regulation on european statistics on natural gas and electricity prices, i believe that harmonised methodology for data collection in the field of energy will help to recognize differences and disparities between the member states. clear and objective statistics will then be an important basis for setting up an eu-wide policies and appropriate measures in the field of energy.
in writing. ‒ i am in favour of measures that will lead to a better functioning and competitive energy market, and thus lower and more predictable energy prices for our large and small consumers. as it will also improve our cross-border cooperation on energy policy, it will help secure our energy supply and decrease our dependence on suppliers from outside the eu. as this is an important step to achieve our priorities on energy and climate issues, i gladly voted in support of this resolution.
in writing. the langen report is an interesting compromise between the demands of those who want to phase out all non-renewable energy production and those who are aware of the potential pitfalls of doing so. among renewable sources, hydropower is the key in terms of installed capacity, followed by wind power and photovoltaic power. so geothermal energy is the only stable source of energy in the long term. given this instability (sun, wind, water determine the unreliability of these sources), it is necessary to provide either backup sources or stabilising capacities that can be flexibly replenished in the event of a lack of energy in the grid. the report acknowledges the emergence of a new class of energy consumers who are also energy producers, and notes the disconnectedness of the european electricity market both within and outside the eu. the report lacks attention to the poor state of the interconnection of the high voltage networks, which is a key point for ensuring the future security of electricity supply. energy must not only be produced but also transmitted reliably.
in writing. on 13 september 2016, we voted on the report 'towards a new energy market organisation' at the european parliament's plenary session in strasbourg. the electricity market is constantly changing and for electricity produced from renewable sources, the current overall share of electricity produced is expected to increase from 25% to 50% by 2030. the commission initiative discussed in the report aims to improve the functioning of the internal electricity market so that electricity can be moved to where and when it is needed most, while fully integrating the growing share of energy from renewable sources. which is, of course, a laudable effort. unfortunately, the commission is doing it all wrong again. those of you who have been following me for a while now know that for a number of reasons, i'm not a big fan of renewable energy. that is why i also supported the amendments calling for the phasing out of subsidies for renewable energy. i am also not in favour of further strengthening the powers of the agency for the cooperation of energy regulators, as i believe that this area is purely and solely a matter for national competence. since the final version of the report did not pass in a form that i could accept, i decided not to support this report and voted against the wording of the report.
in writing. - i voted against it. the report 'supports the increasing share of renewable energy in the eu', which i do not support. i also disagree with the call for 'a regulatory framework that would lead end-users to self-generate and store energy'.
in writing. ‒ today we voted on a report on the new energy market organisation. the report places too much emphasis on the involvement of the european fund for strategic investments, which our group has always opposed. furthermore, it only emphasises the importance of market forces without any involvement of consumers and their attitudes. strengthening the role of acer and other european agencies in the field of energy is also not an idea i could support. a number of amendments proposed by our group, such as a greater focus on renewable energy sources, were not adopted. that is why i voted against the report.
in writing. ‒ i supported the report, which i consider balanced, since it emphasises, among other things, the right of member states to determine the conditions for the use and composition of their own energy resources. i agree with the call to strengthen acer's role and appreciate that the report places a strong emphasis on the promotion of digital technologies in the context of the development of an ambitious energy sector digitisation strategy, including the deployment of smart grids and smart metering, the development of mobile applications, internet platforms and data nodes.
in writing. i supported this own-initiative report, which relates to the forthcoming legislation on the energy market functioning scheme, which will be published in december. in europe today, the way energy is produced and supplied is changing and the market environment needs to adapt to this. the biggest challenge for the administration will be to define a mechanism whereby national governments will compensate companies for guaranteeing a certain capacity of the energy market in cases of a reduction in energy supply, e.g. in the case of a black out, while at the same time minimising the disturbance of the market environment and/or protecting final consumers from an inadequate increase in the price of electricity. i am pleased that the proposals of our political group, which have set out a set of criteria which must be met before such a mechanism can be introduced, have already been taken into account in the itre committee.
in writing. ‒ this own initiative report endorsed by the european parliament is the first reaction to the commission’s communication from july 2015. as a shadow rapporteur i supported the report on the new energy market design as proposed by the rapporteur w. langen as a result of negotiations between the groups. i consider this text to be well-balanced, with market-based approach, covering all important issues related to the eu’s energy market including reform of ets or role of acer. it is not an easy task to bring forward a solution for transformation of the entire market design, but i believe this report will serve as an good first step towards this target.

in writing. - i voted in favour of this new strategy because cooling and heating represent the largest part of the demand for energy services in the eu and increasing efficiency in their use is essential to reduce the costs associated with them, while achieving co2 reductions and improving the security of energy supply. one of the key steps of this strategy is to financially support building owners to carry out large-scale thermal renovation of buildings. this strategy is therefore not only beneficial for these owners, but also for their tenants and, last but not least, for the environment.
in writing. on 13 september 2016, we voted on the report on the eu heating and cooling strategy at the european parliament's plenary session in strasbourg. i was the shadow rapporteur on the envi sub-report on this document, for which the itre committee was primarily responsible. so i followed the document's further fate very closely. the heating problem is a key factor in ensuring clean air, particularly in the region where i come from. heating and cooling use half of the eu's total energy generated, and much of it is wasted. of the new strategy presented by the commission, the areas on which the eu intends to focus in the coming years are, for me personally, the most important and key: facilitating the renovation and reconstruction of buildings; the integration of electrical systems with heating and cooling systems into a single functional unit and the increased use of waste heat and cold produced by industry. however, what i consider to be the most positive aspect of this report is that the rapporteur also understood the local nature and potential of heating and cooling and in the report he directly stated that more decentralised and flexible energy systems with energy and heat sources located closer to each other and to the place of consumption can facilitate and make overall energy production more efficient. for these reasons, i was happy to support the report.

in writing. i supported the report on a heating and cooling strategy that will enable member states to achieve the eu's climate and energy policy goals through sustainable and cost-effective solutions. efficiently achievable energy savings are a key way to achieve climate goals. given the wide diversity of heating and cooling sectors in the member states, due to their different energy mix, climatic conditions, energy efficiency levels of buildings and industrial intensity, flexibility should be ensured in selecting appropriate solutions according to the strategy. the main focus should be on the security of energy supply problems in the eu related to the security of heat supply. in this respect, the commission should therefore examine ways to further promote the diversification of heating sources and to accelerate the wider use of renewable heat technologies.
‒ energy efficiency is a topic i have been working on for a long time, and i have tabled a number of my amendments to this report and supported the final text in plenary. almost 50% of the eu's final energy demand is used for heating and cooling, 80% of which is used in buildings. moreover, considering that every additional 1% increase in energy savings reduces gas imports by 2,6%, it is natural that this should encourage member states to develop long-term heating and cooling strategies based on an integrated approach, harmonised mapping and evaluation in accordance with article 14 of the energy efficiency directive. it is important to remember that while a large proportion of current buildings in europe suffer from energy waste due to poor insulation and outdated and inefficient heating systems, energy poverty affects almost 11% of the eu population. the best solution to this problem, i see, is to invest in thermal renovation buildings, which is the most efficient way to use energy and reduce co2 emissions. in addition, the need to replace obsolete district heating plants with small, high-performance combined heat and power plants is urgent.

in writing. on 14 september 2016, we voted on the report on social dumping in the eu at the plenary session in strasbourg. the report is based on the consideration that there is a significant asymmetry between the reality of an increasingly developed eu internal market and the inadequate protection of social rights in the eu. unfair economic and social competition not only hinders the maintenance of a high level of social protection in the eu, but above all encourages economic operators to reduce their labour costs, thus progressively undermining social standards and reducing the financial resources needed to ensure a high level of social protection. this asymmetry between economic freedoms and social rights also has a significant political impact, as it rightly fosters the feeling that the eu weakens individuals and entire communities instead of protecting them. so, in my view, the only solution to this generally unhappy area, which has been largely neglected for years and totally ignored by the european elites, is at least partial harmonisation of social rights across the eu with the aim of creating a more social europe. it is the only way to prevent the social tourism that is so much discussed today and the flight of people from eastern europe to western europe. although the original report was weakened considerably during the negotiations, it contains a fairly solid list of concrete steps to prevent social dumping and strengthen social protection in the eu in the future, which is why i supported it.

in writing. ‒ today we discussed a report on social dumping in the eu. the report points out that one of the main principles of eu policy is social cohesion, which means the continuous and ongoing convergence of wages and protection and social security for all workers. unfortunately, it is clear that there are still significant differences in working conditions and wages across the union, which is one of the reasons why workers leave for another country. in the discussion we also highlighted the persistence of the gender pay gap and the minimal progress made in this area despite all efforts. social dumping can only make this situation worse. it should also be borne in mind that the gender pay gap also leads to pension gaps, which is one of the main reasons why older women are more at risk of poverty than men. the report highlights all these negative social phenomena, and i voted for it.
in writing. i did not support the report on social dumping in the eu because i do not agree with its basic premise. it is appropriate to speak of various forms of dumping in relation to trade with third countries such as china, but not within the eu where internal market rules apply. and, moreover, in a situation where the member states have their social policies at a high level. moreover, a significant number of the phenomena mentioned in the report are violations of laws or other standards for which the term 'failure to enforce' should be used. social dumping is not legally defined (nor is it definable, as it is subjective), and juggling with this concept is therefore dangerous and easily exploited by, for example, opponents of the common market and free movement in the eu. i consider fundamental freedoms within the eu to be an inviolable value and it would be very frivolous to violate them with political concepts such as social dumping.
‒ social dumping is a phenomenon closely linked to an increasingly competitive environment. the operators seek to reduce their labour costs as much as possible and resort to unfair competition practices. that's unacceptable to me as a social democrat. the behavioural standards of the actors concerned should be set. actions that deliberately undermine workers' rights and weaken social norms cannot be tolerated. for these important reasons, i welcome the report adopted on social dumping in the european union, which brings with it important measures to combat these unfair practices. this provision, among other things, sets out a definition of social dumping, calls for the strengthening of controls and inspections and encourages the creation of a legal framework for the protection of carers and foreign domestic workers. it is also crucial that the eu and the member states strengthen their cooperation on the exchange of information on the social security of posted workers in order to better enforce existing legislation.
‒ as long as there are huge wage differences between member states in the european union, we will continue to face a competitive environment that builds on these differences. this is another reason why it is so difficult to agree on a definition of so-called social dumping across europe. this report, which describes a number of unacceptable practices towards employees in a different way, has not quite matched this. first of all, however, there is the fundamental problem of economic and social convergence. so we should be focusing on the root of the problem rather than pointing out and trying to solve one of its symptoms. the reality is that, unfortunately, the economic situation of people in different parts of europe is being exploited. these practices are not only being carried out by companies with fictitious addresses, but also by some well-known employers from economically stronger countries, as demonstrated by the testimony of truck drivers that took place here in the european parliament some time ago.
in writing. i voted against the report on social dumping in the eu today because i believe it is very dangerous to debate a concept which has no definition in eu law and whose interpretation, as used by the various discussion forums so far, is very variable. moreover, if that concept can be used as a pretext for restricting the fundamental freedoms on which the common market is based, it must be rejected. the free movement of persons, services, goods and capital is clearly regulated by eu law and any challenge to it is counterproductive and leads only to the breakdown of the common market, not to its further development.
in writing. ‒ in order to create the eu internal market, it was necessary to bring together a group of countries that are socially, economically and politically diverse. while it is essential that we ensure a level playing field, fair competition and fair working conditions across this internal market by harmonising the rules when necessary, i do not believe that imposing certain conditions that are not adapted to the specific dynamics and traditions of each member state will benefit our economy as a whole, as the report advocates. this is particularly true for many of the small businesses across the eu, for whom the imposition of certain inadequate demands could truly damage their competitiveness. this is why i voted against this report, in addition to the fact the practices it describes do not reflect my understanding of social dumping.
in writing. - i've decided not to support this report. this is an owninitiative report by parliament containing a number of measures which i do not think are feasible in practice. if we really want to help the real situation in the labour market, we should look at the real needs, not create more nonsensical regulations. furthermore, i also disagree with the form of the definition of social dumping which appears in the report. the european union should, above all, promote competitiveness and the freedom to conduct business. these are the solutions that i think would help the job market.
in writing. - i voted yes. i agree with the call on the commission to propose a delay in the entry into force of the regulation on 'the processing of key information', which i consider to be confusing and harmful. forcing investors to publish 'key contract information' in addition to their own contract and advertising leaflets is itself questionable. key information can never replace the contract and its mandatory disclosure may discourage customers with confidence in the effectiveness of the regulation from reading the contract itself. i am in favor of any delay in the effective date of this harmful regulation.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the resolution objecting to the commission delegated regulation on key information documents for packaged retail and insurance-based investment products (priips). this is because the delegated act as adopted by the commission contained methodological flaws and therefore fails to provide clear, comparable, understandable and non-misleading information on priips to retail investors. in order for our internal market to function correctly, it is key that consumer information on investment products be comparable in order to promote a level playing field in the market, no matter what type of financial intermediary manufactures or markets them.

rapporteur. – mr president, the best news comes at the end of the day. let me recall that in the parliament we have adopted an innovative approach to the commission’s draft prospectus regulation. before i outline our approach, let me remind you of the objective of the prospectus review. it is the first commission proposal in the context of the capital markets union. currently prospectuses are burdensome documents. an equity prospectus costs on average eur 1 million to produce. therefore, there is a need for less cumbersome prospectuses, both for investor protection and to reduce the burden on issuers. our former colleague, philippe de backer, drafted an ambitious report which had the core aim of moving towards a true capital markets union through harmonising the eu regime for smes and issuers between eur 1 million and eur 20 million by offering them the opportunity to produce a lighter prospectus called the eu growth prospectus, reducing fragmentation and capping the limit of national discretion, reducing the burden and costs on issuers and ensuring investor protection. i fully supported the draft report and, when i took over the file, i was able to work constructively with the other shadows to invent an even more tailor—made concept which fine-tunes the details of the growth prospectus. i am glad that the majority of groups share the same objectives: a truly european regime which harmonises prospectus requirements, a reduction in national discretion in terms of smaller issuances and the focus on reducing burdens for smes, notably strongly supporting a lighter prospectus regime for those issuers. other issues discussed in the shadows meeting included provisions on advertising, risk factors and the prospectus summary. we reached a broad agreement in the committee on economic and monetary affairs, and i would like to think the shadow rapporteurs for their support. i highly appreciate it. i look forward to hearing comments from the vice—president and colleagues.

in writing. i decided to support the report on the proposal for a regulation on a european travel document for the return of illegally staying union citizens to third countries. the available data indicate that the rate of return of irregular migrants to third countries is still very low, while at the same time third countries refuse to accept low-quality return documents issued by individual member states. in order to improve this disadvantage and to limit illegal migration, it is therefore necessary to create a single union document with high-quality technical and security features that can be better accepted by the authorities of third countries. with increased acceptance by third country authorities, such a document can not only become another effective tool to fight illegal migration, but also ensure a place in europe for those who are genuinely in need of asylum. i have only minor reservations about two amendments. i believe that the member states should not seek to obtain a guarantee of recognition of a document, but rather to recognise it directly. the return of irregular migrants should also concern not only those who do not fulfil the conditions for entry and presence in the union, but also those who do not fulfil the conditions for 'staying'.

in writing. as a report by the european commission shows, postal services have changed significantly in recent years. new technologies and electronic services are driving up online purchases, while paper deliveries are declining. despite rapid changes, it is essential that the traditional postal services be maintained and made available to all users. therefore, promoting cross-border parcel delivery and reducing price differences between national and cross-border delivery is essential to the creation of a single european market in postal services. despite the development of new delivery technologies, there is a need to protect postal workers from increasing their workload beyond their control. as the report by mr ferber emphasises, overburdening workers and reducing labour costs should not be seen as flexibility. that's why i supported his report.

in writing. ‒ communication has changed considerably over recent years: communications are now immediate and our communication tools have become access doors to services. those changes have impacted on postal services and, whether we like it or not, we send fewer letters but receive more parcels. innovation in the sector moves swiftly and we must make sure the legislation keeps track and anticipate challenges. i voted in favour of the report on the application of the postal services directive because i share its assessment of the situation and the solutions put forward for the future of postal services regulation. we need a regulatory framework that maintains high-quality universal-service obligations while allowing a certain flexibility: strong and independent national regulatory authorities; increased price transparency and consumer awareness; and, if the competition between historic operators, universal-service providers and newcomers is fair, protectionism. this report is only a first step in the establishment of the next regulatory framework on postal and parcel delivery services, and i will continue monitoring those developments.

in writing. ‒ the european globalisation adjustment fund (egf) was established to support workers who had lost their jobs as a result of the adverse effects of globalisation. it was later broadened to support workers suffering from the global and financial crisis, as well as to self-employed and youth. since its creation, the fund has successfully helped put 49% of workers back to work and provided them with tailored support, which is why i voted in favour of extending the funding period from one to two years. it is important that the fund is carefully coordinated with other eu programmes, that its budget is spent efficiently, and that it focuses more on workers in smes, upon which the impact has remained limited until now.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the ratification of the paris agreement on climate change. i do believe that it is a good step how to face issues related to preserving, protecting and improving the quality of the environment, as well as protecting human health and promoting measures at international level to deal with regional or worldwide environmental problems. i would like to call on all the parties of the agreement to ensure its swift implementation.
‒ the paris agreement is one of the most historic milestones in the fight against climate change. i voted in favour of the eu's ratification because meeting the targets set for combating climate pollution and taking a responsible approach to the environment are the foundations for preserving a clean planet for future generations. the eu's 2030 agenda for sustainable development targets, which include reducing greenhouse gas emissions by 40% compared to 1990 levels and increasing the share of renewable energy to at least 27%, are an ambitious commitment by which the eu demonstrates its commitment to maintaining its position as a global leader in the environment and to leading by example.
‒ the paris agreement is a logical follow-up to the kyoto protocol, since it is essential that at least as many parties to the agreement join the agreement as possible so that their total greenhouse gas emissions account for at least 55% of the global total. the ep, in cooperation with the ep, seeks to promote ratification of the protocol through its resolution. in addition to the eu countries, norway and iceland have expressed their intention to participate in the joint action. article 4 (16) of the paris agreement requires that the emission level allocated to the union is in line with the emission level commitments of the member states. the commission shall submit to the european parliament and to the council a report on the implementation of this regulation. the union and the member states shall be jointly responsible for preparing an agreement, in accordance with article 4 (18), on the notification and maintenance of the nationally determined emission reduction contributions they wish to achieve. the objective is to achieve at least a 40% reduction in greenhouse gas emissions by 2030. the paris agreement commits the parties to evaluate the results and to adapt the tools necessary to achieve the best possible effect every five years, starting in 2023. the long-term objective of the agreement is to keep global temperature rise well below 2°c compared to pre-industrial levels. i hope that parliament will support the objectives of the draft council decision by a large majority.
in writing. environmental protection is becoming a more and more frequent topic for one simple reason. humanity is at the point where it is theoretically possible to save the vital ecosystems that we need to survive on this planet. ratification of the cop21 agreement is a step in the right direction and i am glad that the european union is taking the lead in this regard, but as we all know very well, this is only the first step. moreover, it must be acknowledged that the agreement does not provide any binding guidance to states on how to achieve the objectives. moreover, there would certainly be conflicting arguments as to its actual legal enforceability. it's in the hands of the individual states, where the agreement will have to go through the proper constitutional ratification. but i personally think it is essential that we immediately follow up this great act with activities to fulfil it and to try to effectively address the pressing problems of our time. i believe we are capable of moving in this direction, which is why i voted yes in the cop21 decision.
in writing. ‒ the contract is vague, it contains no measurable obligations or mechanisms for their enforcement, so that even with the contract life will go on as before, one could say that the contract is toothless and useless. yet it is dragging the participating states into the mess we know from the eu: action plans, gender policies, regulations, contributions and subsidies. these policies have failed and have already caused much damage, destroying the soil with rapeseed and solar panels, raising energy and food prices, raising taxes and stunting economic growth. what should be done, then, if these contracts are ineffective in my view? when countries get rich, they naturally reduce their pollutant emissions and want more forests and parks. and that's good. we must not regulate countries to stagnation. economic growth, natural care for the environment, safe nuclear energy and the development of modern technologies are the best way to limit greenhouse gases.
in writing. i supported the endorsement of the paris agreement on climate change, which will allow the eu to become an official signatory to the agreement and, as a result, to enter into force. it is a responsible, ambitious, balanced agreement, with cost-effective commitments to reduce co2 emissions on a global scale. the implementation of the commitments will allow the world to avoid dangerous climate change, which in the czech republic, for example, is a particular risk of drought. the agreement recognises that global greenhouse gas emissions should peak as soon as possible and climate neutrality should be achieved by the second half of this century. the development of new technologies and their decreasing price create the conditions for even fairly ambitious climate protection objectives to be achieved at a cost that does not threaten, and in many cases can even strengthen, the stability and growth of economies. i believe in the success of the agreement, which has been signed by the eu and other major co2 emitters such as the us, russia and china. the basic premise is the political will of all parties to translate commitments from paper to reality.

in writing. i supported the legislative resolution by which the european parliament endorses the council decision on the conclusion, on behalf of the european union, of the paris agreement adopted under the united nations framework convention on climate change. significant progress has been made in ratifying the agreement, which can therefore enter into force, with the consent of the european parliament. for the eu, the world's third largest emitter and a major global leader in the fight against climate change, this also means that it will not be a mere observer at important negotiations, but will allow it to discuss the details of the implementation of the paris agreement with other parties, in particular other emission giants such as china and the us. the paris agreement will enter into force on 4 november 2016, before the cop22 climate change conference in marrakech. the czech republic supports the ratification of the agreement on behalf of the eu as a whole. the czech government has already given its consent as part of the national ratification process. the agreement will now be submitted to parliament for approval and then to the president for signature. i trust that the other member states will also take a responsible stance on ratification.
‒ protecting the environment is a global challenge for all of humanity and our obligation to future generations at the same time. that's why i voted for the paris agreement on climate change. the eu's acceptance of the agreement will bring it into force and the signatory countries will be able to start working systematically to meet the commitments they have jointly set. the agreement is already a historic success in its early stages, as for the first time, other major co2 producers besides the eu have joined, notably china, russia and the usa. its main objective is to keep global warming below 2°c, but as close to 1.5°c as possible, and thus prevent further dangerous climate change. the second commitment is to reduce greenhouse gas emissions gradually so as to achieve climate neutrality by the second half of this century. the agreement is, in my view, a bold and balanced text. it should not only deliver environmental successes, but also serve as an opportunity for new technology development and economic growth. i appreciate that the agreement works with real economic stability not compromised by the cost of implementation. i trust that all signatory countries will respond responsibly to this global commitment.
in writing. ‒ the paris agreement has now been signed by 191 countries, and the eu ratification will officially bring the agreement into force. the agreement aims to limit global temperature increases at national level through climate pledges. the eu’s contribution to the reduction of greenhouse gas emissions will account for a 40% reduction from levels in the 1990s. i voted in favour of the eu ratification of the paris agreement to ensure the quick entry into force of the agreement. the eu has played a significant role in combatting climate change and must now work hard to implement internal policies that will bring to light the promises made. i believe that it is our duty as europeans to ensure not only a clean and safe environment for us here in europe, but equally to set an example by promoting environmental ambitions and conscientiousness to other nations who share with us this one world.

in writing. ‒ within the framework of the treaty on the functioning of the european union, judicial cooperation in criminal matters in the union should be based on the principle of mutual recognition of judgments and judicial decisions. however, practice shows that the procedures in the member states vary widely in this respect. this problem thus represents a major obstacle to mutual and effective judicial cooperation. i therefore welcome the commission's proposal to harmonise the minimum levels of legal aid in all member states. at the same time, i am very pleased that the original commission proposal has been extended to all types of legal aid in criminal proceedings. i also supported the requirement that persons subject to a european arrest warrant have the right to legal aid and a lawyer both in the issuing member state and in the executing member state.
in writing. i supported the report on the draft directive on provisional legal aid. the report as amended reflects the reality of the criminal process and the practical aspects of providing free legal aid better than the original proposal. in particular, i welcome the extension of the substantive scope of the directive to ordinary legal aid, and not just to provisional legal aid, which only applies to the first stage of criminal proceedings before the final decision on legal aid is taken. the right to legal aid will now be guaranteed not only at the initial stage but at all stages of the criminal proceedings. only in this way can the right to a fair trial be fully guaranteed throughout the criminal proceedings. i also support the inclusion of a review of the financial circumstances of persons and the justification of legal aid. only in this way can it be assessed whether a person is in fact without the financial means to pay for legal aid or whether the provision of legal aid is in the interests of justice. the proposal also adds basic interpretative rules for such assessment and the possibility for member states to recover costs related to legal aid if persons do not meet the criteria for its granting or have intentionally provided false information to the competent authorities about their financial situation.

in writing. ‒ enshrined in the european convention of human rights, the right to legal aid and representation for all persons, regardless of their socio-economic position is a fundamental human right. this service is essential to strengthening the rights of suspects and accused persons. by establishing minimum rules on the protection of procedural rights of suspects or accused persons, the proposal aims to guarantee the effectiveness of the right of access to a lawyer at an early stage in the criminal proceedings for suspects, accused and vulnerable persons. i voted in favour of the proposal because i believe that, although all eu member states have national legal aid schemes, this directive will mean that eu citizens have the same minimum rights wherever they are in the eu. further, i believe that this directive represents a positive step to ensuring faire trials and access to justice for all eu citizens, not just those who can afford it.

in writing. - i voted yes. i consider the hague convention on the civil aspects of international child abduction to be a useful instrument for international cooperation, especially in cases of mixed marriages where one of the parents takes the child to his or her country of origin. austria and romania are hereby authorised to approve the accession of peru to the convention. sadly, austria and romania need eu approval for this.
in writing. ‒ the hague convention on the civil aspects of international kidnapping is of fundamental importance and has already been ratified by all the states of the european union. i am therefore very pleased that peru has also decided to take this step, thus significantly broadening the scope for cooperation in the field of child abduction, given the large number of peruvian citizens living in the european union. the hague convention aims to protect children from abduction, which occurs in particular in cases of divorce between parents of different nationalities. if one parent decides to take the child to his or her home country, and that country is not part of the international child abduction cooperation, it can easily take custody of the child. the courts in a non-cooperating state usually decide to give the child to the custody of the parent who is a national of that state. however, if the state is a party to the hague convention, the situation can be dealt with at international level and the courts and legislation of the state in which the child is domiciled will be determined to have jurisdiction. today, the european parliament called on austria and romania, the last two countries not to have ratified the agreement, to do so. i supported that motion, of course.
in writing. ‒ the hague convention (1980) on the civil aspects of international child abduction is a vitally important instrument, ratified by all eu member states. the convention created a cooperative system between the signatory states in the goal of resolving cases of international child abduction. most often, reports of child abduction are the result of a couple separating, where the mother and father are from different states. states often are unwilling or unable to cooperate with one another during instances of child abduction as a result of national bias of differing legal systems. parents frequently exploit these legal and judicial disparities in order to secure full custody of the child in a particular state. i voted in favour of the accession of peru so that child abduction at the international level can be resolved through the competent courts of the state of residence of the child.
in writing. ‒ in recent years, we have seen an increase in cases of international child abduction, as it is common for the mother and father to come from different countries. in case of disagreement, they try to win their offspring back by taking them to their country of origin, because they rely on the fact that the countries are not cooperating and therefore it will be more difficult for them to get the child back. i therefore believe that there should be a unified system of cooperation between states to find solutions to international child abduction. at present, there may still be cases where the courts of both countries give the child into the custody of the parent who is a national of that country. the hague convention, which has been ratified by all eu states, addresses these situations and also establishes a system for the immediate return of a kidnapped child to his or her home country. i therefore welcome peru's accession to the hague convention and am confident that this step will help to better protect children in the event of their abduction across national borders.

‒ the eu and all member states must be able to effectively combat financial fraud that harms their interests and thereby protect taxpayers. eu countries also face a growing problem of crossborder organised crime. in this respect, i consider eurojust to be a key instrument, which makes cooperation between member states' investigative authorities more efficient and helps to build mutual trust and to overcome differences between a wide variety of legal systems and traditions. however, to improve the fight against any kind of organised crime and to increase mutual assistance in investigations, further steps are needed. that is why i also support the creation of an effective and independent european public prosecutor's office. however, before the new investigating authority is established, it is necessary to ensure that it is independent and effective. in order to ensure that the powers of the prosecutor are sufficient, it is first necessary to approve the directive on the fight against fraud to the union's financial interests by means of criminal law, which lays down the criminal offences for which the office will have jurisdiction. the eppo will also be able to provide the necessary legal assistance to the eppo in the event of a dispute arising from the application of this regulation.
in writing. ‒ the european public prosecutor’s office, intended to act as an independent eu body that is able to prosecute crimes affecting the eu’s financial interest, would help fill in the current institutional gap that currently exists, as only national authorities can prosecute eu fraud by means of criminal law, however not across national borders. i voted in favour of the eppo because of its independent nature, which will make way for improved efficiencies in the prosecution of eu fraud cases. it is estimated by the european commission that fraud against the eu’s financial interests costs around eur 3 billion every year. the creation of a european public prosecutor’s office is essential to ensure that fraud against the eu’s financial interests is tackled equally in all member states.
