in writing. i supported the motion for a resolution on the regulation on the use of materials intended to come into contact with foodstuffs, given the lack of specific eu action in this area. the european union dominates the global ranking with its high standards of food quality and consumer protection. emphasising compliance with standards to protect the health of eu citizens is one of its priorities and the proposal for this regulation will contribute to ensuring increased food safety. in order to protect consumers' health, there is a need to re-evaluate the regulatory framework and thereby facilitate the implementation of the legislation.
in writing. on 6 october 2016, we voted on the resolution on the application of the regulation on materials intended to come into contact with foodstuffs at the european parliament's plenary session in strasbourg. food contact materials are widely used in our daily lives, most commonly in the form of food packaging, kitchen utensils, utensils, etc. different materials can behave very differently when in contact with food, often transferring their constituents directly to the food. in such cases, those chemicals may endanger human health by adversely altering the composition of the food. as i have said for a long time on the issue of endocrine disruptors, with which packaging materials are also closely linked, we need to be very careful about what chemicals manufacturers are putting into our food and into the environment. the current situation is that european legislation only covers certain selected materials and the source regulation is already quite outdated. for example, it does not reflect in any way the key scientific findings concerning the harmfulness of the endocrine disruptors already mentioned. the rapporteur is therefore right to call on the european commission to revise it. i have tabled an amendment to the text with my colleagues concerning the prohibition of bisphenol a (bpa). i was happy to support the document because i think it is going in the right direction.
in writing. - i voted against it. while it is important that food packaging does not endanger the food packaged in it, i do not agree with the call to the commission to prioritise 'preparing standards for paper and cardboard', as this would only lead to unnecessary regulation.
in writing. ‒ one area where the eu should focus on food contact materials is to improve the traceability and compliance of those imported from third countries by requiring the presentation of proper and complete identification documents and declarations of conformity. imported food contact materials must comply with eu standards to protect public health and ensure fair competition. as regards products originating in the eu, i do not think that we need new or stricter regulation at eu level. it will be enough to be able to harmonise the level of enforcement of food contact materials legislation within the eu, where there are still often significant differences between countries. improved data exchange between member states is a prerequisite.
in writing. when in contact with food, different materials may behave differently depending on their composition and properties and their constituents may be released into food. this may endanger human health or adversely affect the composition of food. i therefore supported the report by mrs schaldemos and her call for the current eu legislation on food contact materials to be amended to provide a higher level of health protection. in my view, the emphasis should be placed, for example, on risk assessment and enforcement and control of compliance with the relevant rules.
in writing. the european parliament voted today on an own-initiative report on the application of the regulation on materials intended to come into contact with food, which i decided to support. the ep's initiative, which calls for a revision of the current framework regulation (ec) no 1935/2004 on materials intended to come into contact with food, is important, in my view, especially in the context of protecting human health. materials intended to come into contact with food (food packaging, kitchen utensils, tableware, etc.) contain a number of harmful chemicals that are released into food from these materials. eu citizens are thus exposed to a high risk of endangering their health when consuming food. i therefore welcome this recommendation, which seeks to maintain a high level of consumer protection while ensuring the effective functioning of the internal market for these materials. the recommendations rightly emphasise the call to promote further research in this area, to ensure adequate control of goods and compliance and enforcement. the text also points out the need to comply with the standards laid down for goods imported from third countries.
in writing. ‒ food contact materials (fcms) are largely used in everyday life in the form of food packaging, kitchen utensils, tableware, etc. when in contact with food, and depending on their composition and properties, the different materials may behave differently, transferring their constituents to the food. in such cases, chemicals emanating from fcms may endanger human health or adversely change the composition of the foodstuffs. the most pressing issue is the need to adopt eu specific measures for food contact materials that are widely used in europe, such as paper and board, both virgin and recycled, and for materials that may pose a significant risk to human health, such as inks, metals or coatings. i voted in favour of the report and i fully support the call for the revision of current eu rules on food contact materials. many substances are currently not harmonized at eu level, a goal that is in the interest of both consumers and operators. consumers would benefit from the higher eu-wide standards of consumer protection and operators from the legal certainty that uniform rules bring.

in writing. the 2014 annual report on the monitoring of the application of union law presented by the commission indicates that the highest number of cases concerning infringements of the treaty were opened repeatedly in the areas of environment, transport and internal market policies and services, including consumer protection. a fair internal market, including consumer protection policy, cannot be built without the timely and correct transposition of eu legislation into national law, a clear legal framework and enforcement. the commission's report highlights that the number of formal infringement procedures has decreased over the last five years, and that this decrease is the result of effective dialogue with member states under the eu pilot. however, the juri report notes that the enforcement of eu law is not yet sufficiently transparent and asks whether the declared reduction actually corresponds to better compliance by member states with eu law. i therefore support the idea that a procedure be set up within parliament's competent committees to monitor the application of eu law in the member states, which would be able to analyse the issue of non-compliance in a factual manner, but also to pass on this knowledge to national parliaments. in this respect, i welcome the call for the commission to share information also in the context of the informal eu pilot procedure.
in writing. ‒ european union law is a system of rules operating within the member states of the european union. eu law, which has equal force with national law, confers rights and obligations on the authorities in each member country, as well as individuals and businesses. the commission’s 32nd annual report on monitoring the application of eu law contains interesting information on the implementation and practical application of eu law. the report on the application of union law, a pilot procedure aimed at increasing effectiveness in the application of union law, expresses doubt that the enforcement of eu law is sufficiently transparent. i voted in favour of the proposed amendments, which would see the european parliament play a more structured role in the analysis of how both countries in the eu and accession countries comply with eu law and aid in developing appropriate support in this respect for those countries.
in writing. i support this 32nd annual report of the commission on monitoring the application of eu law. the report contains, in my view, a lot of interesting and stimulating information on the current state of compliance with european legislation. for example, it is noted that the environment, transport and the internal market and services remained the sectors where the highest number of infringement cases were opened in 2014. on the other hand, it is interesting to observe that the total number of formal infringements of the treaty has been steadily decreasing over the last five years. nevertheless, i stress that the commission must continue to play an active role in monitoring compliance with the law and develop tools to help better implement european legislation at national level. the role of parliament should instead be primarily political oversight of the commission's enforcement activities. i therefore personally find the proposals on administrative procedure put forward by the working party set up by the committee on legal affairs particularly useful in the report, as i believe they can be an inspiration for the commission in the future.

mr president, the fight against terrorism and organised crime cannot be tackled at the level of the member states alone, and citizens therefore rightly expect the european union to ensure their security from within its powers. in the last two years, we have adopted two regulations that allow for the collection of passenger data, the collection of information on money transfers that could be used to finance terrorism. at europol, the amount of data shared is multiplied and the european counter-terrorism centre is created. we are aware of the need to prevent, combat radicalisation and also the need to not tolerate manifestations of radical islam, to monitor content on the internet, and therefore we also want to prevent its dissemination through audiovisual services. ladies and gentlemen, the list of these activities that we are undertaking at european union level is not exhaustive, it is not sufficient, but it is a clear signal that the safety of citizens is our priority.

in writing. i supported the report presenting the agreement of the ep and the council at second reading. under the pressure of the ep, the element of objective responsibility, which does not require a degree of culpability, has been removed. however, the directive should provide a framework to ensure that member states have a uniform perception of mitigating and aggravating circumstances, from voluntary reporting to non-cooperation. the provisions on strict liability are contrary to that approach and, moreover, call into question certain fundamental principles of law, such as the presumption of innocence, since they do not require an element of culpability for which a sanction is imposed. it is essential that the directive approximates non-criminal sanctions, while leaving the adjustment of criminal sanctions to the member states.
in writing. ‒ the proposal for the union legal framework for customs infringements and sanctions aims to establish a framework for breaches of the union’s customs legislation and provide for penalties applicable where there are infringements. although customs legislation is fully harmonised, its enforcement and the lawful imposition of sanctions lie within the competence of member states' national law, rendering the effective management of the customs union much more difficult to harmonise. for economic operators, the differences in the treatment of infringements of union customs legislation have an impact on the level playing field, thus providing an advantage for those who breach the law in a member state with more lenient legislation for customs sanctions. i voted in favour of the proposal because i believe that in a true single market, we cannot let companies face different treatments depending on the country where they will be sanctioned. in the single eu market, the law should be the same for everyone.
in writing. ‒ i support this proposal, which aims to harmonise the approach of member states to the enforcement of customs rules and sanctions. since the european union has a single customs union, i believe that there should also be a single customs sanction, which is the same for all eu members. i believe that this proposal will lead to a more comprehensible and transparent environment, especially for smes, which form the backbone of the european economy.

in writing. - i voted against it. i consider the resolution to be legally dilettante and contrary to the principles of the rule of law. the resolution calls on the member states to adopt specific legislation and appropriate measures to prevent and combat the activities of professionals, banking institutions, officials and politicians at all levels who, although not members of criminal organisations, support them at various levels. in this respect, calls for criminal sanctions to be imposed on managers and banks involved in cases where there is evidence of large-scale money laundering. criminal sanctions are to be imposed by the court on the basis of law and not on the basis of an ad hoc resolution of the european parliament. a manager or a banker, like anyone else, should be convicted if they have committed a crime, not on the basis of a vague ruling of involvement in cases.

in writing. i did not support the report on human rights and migration in third countries because i think that a number of the proposals that the ep supported went too far. the report calls, among other things, for too broad protection and support for migration, including illegal migration. for example, the emphasis on the need to recognise the right of all migrants, including illegal migrants, to form and join workers' rights organisations, such as trade unions.
‒ migration is a global and highly complex problem with diverse origins, arising for example from adverse economic conditions, but also from a violent and conflict-ridden environment. the unhcr report estimates that more than 65 million people have been forced to flee their country of origin because of instability or a humanitarian crisis caused by internal conflict. i realize that there is no simple solution to this problem. on the contrary, measures must be taken that are effective in the long term. the adopted report seeks to address an important aspect of the migration crisis concerning respect for the dignity and human rights of refugees and calls on member states to abolish criminal law regimes that criminalise migration. it also places great emphasis on the need to assess each application individually and to identify and subsequently grant international protection to migrants. the rights of refugees should also be ensured by improving their quality of life, in particular through their access to healthcare, education and employment. in this regard, attention must be paid in particular to the most vulnerable, namely women and children, whose numbers among migrants and refugees are constantly increasing. while i fully agree with all the above requirements, i cannot support a text that again refers to the mandatory distribution mechanism and weakens the return policy in my view. that is why i abstained.
in writing. i did not support the resolution on rights and migration in third countries in the final vote. the european parliament's initiative, which expresses concern at the serious human rights violations faced by many migrants in transit or destination countries, could be a useful appeal if it did not contain proposals that violate the principle of subsidiarity. i agree that the dignity and human rights of every human being, including migrants and refugees, must be respected and that illegal migration and trafficking in human beings must be prevented by all means possible. however, i regret to say that the report, whose main purpose should be the one mentioned above, contains a number of unnecessary recommendations with which i cannot agree. the report, for example, pays special attention to specific groups such as lgbti, seeks to mainstream gender issues into migration policies, or calls for the establishment of permanent and mandatory resettlement programmes. moreover, the report often uses and confuses the two different terms 'migrant' and 'refugee' in an inappropriate way, which can be confusing in its overall context. the passage which talks about the social and economic rights of migrants can also be read as calling for the payment of social benefits to all migrants, which is unacceptable. the text is also reflected in the fact that the resolution was adopted by a very narrow majority of 339 votes to 333.
in writing. i did not support the adoption of the report on human rights and migration in third countries, because, while i agree with some parts of the report that migration is a complex problem, i no longer agree with many of the other starting points and proposals for solutions mentioned. i believe that in the current migration crisis, which is currently affecting the mediterranean region in particular, it is particularly important to distinguish between migration in the broadest sense and the movement of people, many of whom are subsequently granted international protection, either in the form of asylum or subsidiary protection. the geneva convention should be applied. but i think that, for example, to quote the part of the universal declaration of human rights that says that 'everyone has the right to leave any country, including his own, and to return to his country' should be interpreted in the light of, for example, our experience with restrictions on freedom of movement in socialist czechoslovakia, not as the right of anyone to move anywhere regardless of, for example, visa requirements, length of stay, etc. such interpretations do not contribute to the exercise of the right of asylum by those who are entitled to it.
in writing. ‒ migration is a global, multidimensional phenomenon caused by a wide variety of factors, such as economic conditions, social and political conditions, labour conditions, violence, security, and environment. if the eu and its member states must lead by example in protecting the human rights of asylum seekers, economic migrants must be return to their country when their security is guaranteed. however, in this report, all the dimensions and the complexity of the migration issues are not covered and i believe that this report does not reflect the reality. if i believe that the eu, in keeping with its own value and norms, has the obligation to play a strong role in the protection of human rights, the migration phenomenon must be addressed in a coherent, balanced manner, based on a comprehensive approach, which is here not the case and this is the reason why i voted against this report.

in writing. on 25 october 2016, we voted in plenary on the report on the eu strategy for liquefied natural gas and gas storage. the proposal under discussion is another in a series of eu efforts to create a slow-moving energy union. this time, it is aimed at defining a single strategy for lng for all eu member states. i have long been very reluctant to build a single energy union, because i believe that energy, the energy mix and security are matters which are the exclusive responsibility of the individual member states. however, i'm trying to be very open about this issue. the proposal is moving towards a single gas market, which is not necessarily a bad thing. but it also mentions the transatlantic trade partnership, which i strongly disagree with. moreover, like most energy union documents, it omits the fundamental issues of access to and availability of energy, does not consider energy as a public good of a social nature and does not try to combat so-called energy poverty, which is a fundamental error for a commodity such as gas, the price of which is still a socially sensitive issue in many countries. in addition, the proposal takes a very benevolent approach to the issue of gas produced by so-called hydraulic fracturing, which destroys both our waters and biodiversity and the environment in general. for all these reasons, i abstained from voting.
in writing. - i voted against it. lng is a technology that allows the transport of gas that can be used for both transport and electricity generation. this technology is being used and expanded naturally and we don't need an eu strategy for that. i do not agree with the call for the eu and the member states to create 'preventatives' for the distribution of liquefied biogas. biogas as a renewable source must be marketable without subsidies and tax breaks if it is to be competitive, otherwise there is a risk that support for biogas will end, as will support for solar and wind power plants , thus placing a huge burden on consumers and taxpayers.

in writing. ‒ natural gas has great potential within the eu energy system and plays an important role in industrial production. i supported the report on the strategy for liquefied natural gas as it is one of the elements of the proposed energy union. this is a further step towards a sustainable, secure and competitive energy system. in order to achieve this objective, the potential of lng needs to be fully exploited and the union market needs to be made more attractive to suppliers. the key aspect of the report is in particular the recommendations concerning the creation of the necessary infrastructure, but also the emphasis on the use of existing lng terminals. the eu should also focus more on working closely with international partners to promote free and transparent global lng trade. lng also has a high potential to become an alternative fuel to more polluting conventional fuels, both in road and maritime transport. however, although natural gas is a cleaner alternative to other fuels and a flexible back-up for electricity generation, it should not become a full-fledged substitute for renewable sources. this is because it is not completely environmentally friendly and there is a continuing need to minimise transient methane emissions released throughout its life cycle.

in writing. ‒ i stayed because the czech republic has no sea and i left it to the representatives of other states to decide on the regulation of fishing.
‒ fisheries controls are an important tool for achieving the objectives of the reform of the cfp. despite the fact that fisheries policy is one of the most integrated union policies, there are huge differences between member states, especially in the scope and procedures of controls. in addition, the means and instruments used to carry out individual checks differ, as do the penalties and the legal procedures. the european fisheries control agency has the main responsibility for ensuring that european standards in control and inspection are met and for coordinating action between member states. however, its mandate is currently limited and its powers and funding are insufficient. i therefore highly appreciate the work of my colleague isabelle thomas, the rapporteur of this report, who has attended a series of meetings to document the current situation in each country and then to identify the main obstacles to the unification of fisheries controls. i believe that direct talks with fishermen, representatives of the european fisheries control agency, but also with national and regional inspectors are essential for realistically assessing the situation and subsequently establishing an effective control framework.
in writing. ‒ the eu fisheries control regulation (2010) modernised the eu’s approach to fisheries by creating a common fisheries policy. in particular, it brought the system into line with the strong measures the union had adopted at international level in 2008 to combat illegal, unreported and unregulated fishing. however, at the national level, member states and their fisheries control authorities are responsible for the implementation of the policies. the report pointed to several areas for revision, including the necessity to respect the fishery rules, ensuring that all member states are on a level playing field with regard to respecting the rules, the prevention of inequality or mistrust among the member states, the creation of culture of compliance, and the need to improve uniformity. i voted in favour of the report because better implementation, cooperation and, where needed, homogenisation of control standards is a far better option that allowing further derogations from the current fisheries controls in the eu.
in writing. ‒ i supported the report on improving the connection and accessibility of the transport infrastructure in central and eastern europe because high quality transport links are fundamental for the economic activities in europe and for the quality of life of our citizens. transport networks have to cover the local regional, national and cross-border dimensions, because only a well-connected europe will achieve economic, social and territorial cohesion in and between member states in the eu.
in writing. the report on improving the connectivity and accessibility of transport infrastructure in central and eastern europe addressed a very important topic, but it lacked the necessary balance. from the very beginning it seemed that the polish rapporteur wanted to celebrate polish achievements and lobby for polish national needs in this area in the first place. while i am pleased that the report recalls that the development of crossborder roads is essential to facilitate cooperation between people and businesses in border regions, and that it calls on member states to continue to modernise roads, build missing links and safe and accessible parking areas, and to strengthen regional and local connections to the ten-t network, as ten-t networking is an important foundation for the economic growth of regional centres, i would expect much more from a report like this. that's why i abstained during the vote.
in writing. - i voted against it. the development of the road and rail networks is a matter for the member states. i do not agree with the call for 'member states to further promote the digitalisation and automation of all modes of transport' and, in this context, for 'investment infrastructure projects to include transport solutions that reduce the risk of death and serious injury from road traffic accidents'. i take it as a challenge to the state's inadequate control of drivers. the eu should leave this to the individual member states. the use of cameras and digitalisation to monitor drivers may, in my view, lead to more bullying of drivers for minor speeding and to drivers being in constant fear of their own speed over the surroundings and the safety of driving.
in writing. improving the connectivity and accessibility of transport infrastructure in central and eastern europe is urgently needed, as transport infrastructure in most regions of central and eastern europe remains underdeveloped compared to transport infrastructure in other european regions. in this context, work on important projects such as via carpatia and rail baltica, as well as the construction of the eastern and eastern mediterranean corridor, the baltic-adriatic corridor and the adriatic-ionian corridor, should be intensified. however, i abstained in a separate vote in favour of the full navigability of the labe, as i have serious doubts about the environmental sustainability and economic viability of such a solution.
in writing. i supported this report on the lack of transport infrastructure in central and eastern europe, because this is reflected in our daily lives. well-connected transport networks are a key element in promoting economic, social and territorial cohesion between member states. although much progress has been made in this area, particularly in re-establishing links to and from the western eu countries, many shortcomings still remain in the countries of eastern and central europe. the adopted report covers all modes of transport, but places particular emphasis on multimodal transport. it is crucial to complete major projects relating to road infrastructure, high-speed railways, inland waterways and to improve connections between regional airports. i am pleased that the european parliament is aware of the need to give particular attention to central and eastern europe and i trust that it will take these needs into account in future priorities for funding from the european structural and investment funds.
in writing. i supported the report by mr poręba. the current lack of adequate connectivity of transport infrastructure in the cee region supports the call for member states to focus on closing bottlenecks and missing sections of the ten-t core network to be completed by 2030. the rapporteur also points out in his report the importance of a coordinated approach by member states, which should consult their transport master plans with neighbouring member states. this approach, in my view, can help to link the missing cross-border sections. the completion of the ten-t core network requires sufficient funding and i am therefore pleased that the report calls on the commission to ensure synergies and complementarities between the european funds in this regard, as this is crucial for the member states in our region.
in writing. i voted today for the report on improving the connectivity and accessibility of transport infrastructure in central and eastern europe, which stresses the need to improve the connectivity and accessibility of transport infrastructure to, from and within the central and eastern parts of the eu. this report supports the modernisation of roads, the construction of missing links and safe and accessible parking areas, within the ten-t network. the development of transport hubs is a key element for interconnecting long-distance, regional and urban transport and, consequently, for promoting efficiency, intermodality and business development at regional level, also taking into account the extensive possibilities of digitalisation to increase the efficiency of the entire logistics chain. it also stresses that the european structural and investment funds can be used to build missing links in border areas in central and eastern europe, and calls on the central and eastern european member states to ensure a high level of transparency and rigorous control of the spending of eu funds.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on the connection and accessibility of transport infrastructure in central and eastern europe. the report points at the specific development of transport infrastructure in the region and underlines, among other things, the need to promote intermodality as well as cross-border connections in the region. in particular, i supported the provisions inviting the member states and the commission to ensure synergies and mutual complementarity of the funding instruments used in the region in order to improve their utilisation.
in writing. - i voted for this report. the level of transport infrastructure in central and eastern europe has clearly improved in recent decades, largely thanks to eu funding. however, there is still room for improvement, in particular as regards the modernisation of existing infrastructure, the completion of missing links and other elements of the ten-t network. i consider the development of infrastructure in the cee region to be important not only because of the improvement of the situation at member state level, but also because it is an important factor in strengthening the security and stability of the eu's eastern border.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report as i believe there is a case for considering a mechanism through which democracy, rule of law and human rights are monitored. these are a very core value of the eu and should be duly respected, these are the values the eu is known for on international level. the pact should prevent or correct potential breaches of these values and would allow much-needed discussion over it. i also believe there is room for imposing sanctions in case the democratic principles are not respected.
in writing. ‒ during the vote on the report containing the recommendation to the commission to establish an eu mechanism for democracy, the rule of law and fundamental rights, i decided to abstain. i am not entirely convinced that the european union needs another expert group paid for with taxpayers' money, and i believe that this mechanism is intended as a sort of whip for states whose policies are not accepted by the eu institutions. i am fully aware that the rule of law is being dismantled in poland, for example, but he thinks it is a sign of political weakness to pay public money to a group that will tell us what we already know, but we will be relieved of political responsibility. moreover, the selection of these experts can become a highly politicized issue, which would rather damage the whole thing.
in writing. - i voted against it. i do not agree with the call for 'the establishment of a democracy foundation to award grants and support local actors who promote democracy, the rule of law and fundamental rights within the union'. i see it as another subsidy to human rights organizations, which often promote their political ideas. the constitutions of the member states are the basic framework for human and civil rights. we're not going to promote democracy and human rights by subsidizing certain entities.
in writing. ‒ i myself have lived through a period of lack of freedom, and therefore i know that democratic values, the rule of law and human rights must be constantly protected and ensured that they are not violated. although the eu has legally established mechanisms to uphold these values, a report by ms int veld on the establishment of an eu mechanism for democracy, the rule of law and fundamental rights was presented to the european parliament. i did not support this report and its proposals for a number of reasons, and i will mention some of them. in cases where there are indications that respect for democratic values may be threatened in a member state, a constructive diplomatic dialogue should be established with that state and existing instruments should be used in accordance with the treaties. this process is also ongoing, see the current situation in poland. we must continually cultivate in the citizens of the union a faith and a commitment to these principles, above all through education and by the exemplary conduct of the european institutions themselves. education, diplomatic dialogue, diplomatic pressure where appropriate, and allowing time for the development of existing contractual instruments to protect these values may be more effective in the end than the creation of new and additional mechanisms. we can consider rationalizing the procedure, which is certainly not flawless, but not in the way that this report proposes.
in writing. ‒ while the eu has a several existing instruments to ensure the principles on democracy, the rule of law and fundamental rights are upheld, substantial gaps remain and in practice certain instruments are often limited in scope, inadequate and ineffective, or they are unlikely to be used. in some cases, their uneven application is perceived by many as politically motivated, arbitrary and unfairly targeting certain countries. further, there is no integrated mechanism for the systematic, impartial and complete monitoring of all eu member states and institutions. the report outlines the establishment of a comprehensive union mechanism for democracy, the rule of law and fundamental rights in the form of an interinstitutional agreement aligning and complementing existing mechanisms. i voted in favour of the report because i believe that it is of primary importance to reaffirm the common values on which the european project is based upon and to adopt a mechanism that will guarantee democracy, rule of law and fundamental rights are upheld in practice, not only on paper.

spur growth and jobs and to provide sufficient funding to tackle the still ongoing refugee, migration and security crisis. at the same time, it was the council’s explicit wish to create sufficient margins to enable us to cope with the unforeseen situations that we will certainly have to face in the course of the next year. i take due note of the various amendments to the council’s position that rapporteur. – madam president, today marks a day when we can say that we are one step closer to dignity and respect for all of our citizens, including those with disabilities. this is because of the hard work of this house and thanks to the true leadership of the dutch presidency, which understood that this piece of legislation is vital. europe is now not only on the cusp of a digital revolution, but we are in the middle of it. it is the policy of the union that every sector, both private and public, should be digital, and that by going digital we will renew growth in europe and make life easier for our citizens. if our digital services are not accessible to all of our citizens, we are not helping them but are instead holding many back and introducing new barriers. there are more than 80 million europeans with a disability. as we age, every one of us will have either a temporary or permanent disability at some point. this is as true for those digital natives among us as it is for those born before the internet. making digital information accessible is as much in our own individual interest as that of society as a whole. i am proud that, as of tomorrow, web accessibility will be the law of the land in europe. every government website and – maybe more importantly – every government application will have to be accessible. this law applies not only to the public, but also to internal government websites, meaning that it will help the millions of government employees with disabilities and help open new job opportunities for others. this law means that all online and digital forums and all payment systems will have to be accessible. it will end the outlandish situation whereby we require people to pay their taxes online, only to create a website that not all people can use. today, we are saying that e—government must be open and service all citizens. for this reason, i am proud. is this the final step? no, mr commissioner, it is not. there are still some limitations to making this law proportional, but, if something is not accessible, governments will now be accountable to give a clear reason why it is not, and that reason cannot be that it would simply cost too much. every citizen will have a right to challenge such a decision. it is also not the last step because the digital world is more than government websites alone. we still need a strong european accessibility act that covers both the digital and physical worlds. parliament has a good voice for this in my colleague, mr løkkegaard. we need to adopt the accessibility act as soon as possible. when it has been adopted, the two combined will mean that we can say that we have served our citizens well and done everything we can to help all of them. i am proud to have my name attached to this legislation, and i look forward to its adoption tomorrow.

in writing. i welcome the initiative of my colleagues and support the reduction of industrially produced trans-fatty acids in food. since the adoption of regulation (eu) no 1169/2011, it has been confirmed that such restrictions have a positive impact on public health. the commission's december 2015 report furthermore assessed that this is a quick and efficient way to achieve this. this is certainly good news, given that the intake of trans fat remains one of the main risk factors for the development of ischaemic heart disease, but there is a need to continue to improve prevention. it is estimated that this disease alone is responsible for around 660 000 deaths per year in the eu, about 14% of all deaths. cardiovascular diseases kill 4 million people in the eu every year, and still account for almost half of all deaths. it is therefore striking that the commission has not assessed, within its mandate, the need to present a legislative proposal aimed at excluding trans-fatty acids from the eu food supply chain in the long term by introducing either mandatory labelling of trans-fatty acids or a union legal upper limit of industrially produced trans-fatty acids for all foods. the immediate introduction of eu-wide legislation has long been supported by leading experts, notably the european association of cardiologists, consumer organisations and manufacturers.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the draft budget of the european union for 2017. the total budget of the european parliament for 2017 will be about 1.2% of the eu budget, according to our proposal. it could be even less if parliament did not have to move to strasbourg for a week every month, which i have been fighting for for a long time. i welcome the request to increase the budget of the erasmus+ programme, which i am working on as vice-chair of the cult committee. i strongly believe that further support for erasmus plus will result in increased mobility of pupils and teachers between eu member states. this programme should continue to improve opportunities for teaching foreign languages, sharing examples of good practice and building partnerships between schools. its extension should also allow more scope for the use of activities prepared by youth organisations and the european voluntary service. in the light of the current security situation, i also very much welcome the fact that the eu budget for 2017 allocates a significantly higher share of security resources than last year, to support security institutions such as europol, which not only help to address the migration and refugee crisis, but also fight terrorism.
in writing. i supported the ep resolution on the draft eu budget for 2017. i am pleased that the text has been able to incorporate a substantial increase in funding for the european agencies europol, eurojust, easo and others. these agencies, among other things, are working hard to improve the eu-wide security situation and are making a significant contribution to addressing and managing the current migration crisis. europol, for example, launched a new counter-terrorism centre this year, has made a significant contribution to improving the exchange of information between member states and continues to provide the eu's basis for much-needed cooperation between member states. i also support the increase in the budget for erasmus plus. the programme, which contributes to deepening european integration and creating a common european culture and identity, is one of the most fruitful initiatives in today's europe of populism and xenophobia. i was also very pleased to express my support for the new interrail initiative of the european people's party. this is a project whereby eu citizens would receive a monthly rail ticket across the eu on their 18th birthday. i would also like to reiterate my support for the idea of a single seat for the ep. i therefore supported this point in the resolution, but i am also aware that the ep does not have the power of initiative in this matter. the agreement of the member states is required to change this established practice. members may only express their disagreement with the two seats by means of a non-binding initiative.
i could not support the eu budget for next year as a whole because it contains a number of redundant items. on the contrary, i support investments in research and development and other areas for future growth, such as projects linking private and public capital under horizon 2020.
in writing. ‒ i supported the motion for resolution on the mid-term revision of the multiannual financial framework which calls for a real revision of the mff to address eu current challenges. i welcome the fact that the commission presented a revision of the mff, which was too restrictive, to deal with the security and migrations challenges we are facing. this ambitious reform reflects eu political commitments and ensure european money is spent where it is most needed. it was essential for the european parliament to link the revision of the multiannual financial framework to the 2017 annual budget, as the decisions on the former one are expected to be integrated into the latter. that is why in the ep position the 2017 budget reflects the smart proposal of the mid-term review made by the commission.

in writing. i supported the resolution on the mid-term review of the mff, which highlighted the lack of resources under the current mff in relation to the migration and refugee crisis, crisis events abroad and internal security issues. i am pleased that our group has succeeded in putting into the text the emphasis on the mobility of young people in the face of the threat of populism and the spread of disinformation and in supporting the implementation of the new initiative 'european interrail network ticket for the 18th birthday', which consists in giving every european citizen a free interrail network ticket when he or she turns 18. the most appropriate and budget-friendly way of financing this initiative will still have to be found, but it is important to express political support for it at this stage.
in writing. ‒ the current multiannual financial framework no longer meets the current needs and challenges facing the union. that is why i supported the motion for a resolution on the review of this budgetary instrument. in 2013, when the framework was adopted, it was not yet known to what extent the old continent would be affected by the migration and refugee crisis, nor for how long it would be possible to restart investment activities and mobilise young people and their employment. i voted in favour of this report, even though the resolution is based on the content of its predecessor, i.e. the resolution on the mff of 6 july 2016. however, unlike the aforementioned earlier report, the return regulation does not properly address the migration crisis causing further disintegration on the european continent. it is necessary to recognise that the european budget needs more flexibility to be able to respond to current and future challenges. i hope very much that the council will reflect on the outcome of the vote in parliament and give the slovak presidency a mandate so that the interinstitutional negotiations can take place as quickly as possible, in line with the adoption of the future budget. if the representatives of the member states are to hesitate, they alone will be to blame for the fact that the union budget continues to face several serious problems. the european parliament is ready to actively seek solutions, as stated in the current framework regulation.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the mff resolution backing the main elements of the commission’s proposal to revise the multiannual financial framework (mff) 2014-2020. indeed, i welcome the proposals in the mff package as regards extending the budgetary flexibility and i believe that the proposal to create an eu crisis reserve as an instrument to make it possible to react swiftly to crises and other events with serious humanitarian or security implications is important.

in writing. - i voted against it. i do not agree that estonia should receive €1 million from the european globalisation adjustment fund to pay redundant workers at the gas company esti energia. social policy should be a matter for member states, governments should not ad hoc help individual firms and workers. i consider the whole european globalisation adjustment fund to be a socialist redistribution of money, and i think it should be abolished.
in estonia, as many as 1 550 workers were made redundant in three chemical companies. that is why i voted for the necessary release of funds from the european globalisation adjustment fund, which was created specifically for such situations. the estonian economy has been shaken by developments in the global oil market and by alternative and cheaper imports of products from outside the european union. estonia has fulfilled all the necessary criteria for support from this fund. i voted to give the redundant employees some eur 1.1 million in assistance. more specifically, it will provide individual assistance and support for the follow-up of further studies, training, counselling and allowances for transport and accommodation during self-development. i also supported the involvement of not only central authorities but also regional authorities in the implementation of the measures. also representatives of employees and employers. i believe that these funds will help the most vulnerable group of redundant workers to find new jobs and thus contribute to the diversification of trade, which accounts for more than three quarters of the estonian economy. i also believe that the funds provided to estonia until 2019 will mitigate the impact of redundancies in the chemical industry on other sectors, including the processing, mining and energy sectors.
in writing. ‒ estonia is a small open economy with a high reliance on exports of goods and services. as a result, the estonian economy highly suffered from the recent volatility in the global oil and a general decrease in europe’s international trade. the high concentration of industries dependent on oil and gas prices in northern area of estonia was in particular badly hit by redundancies in the manufacture of petroleum and chemicals products. i voted in favour of the mobilisation of funds, eur 1 131 358, which will benefit 1 550 estonians in need of assistance to find employment and social security.

in writing. plant health is a hot topic and it is clearly a subject that needs to be protected. i therefore support this text on protection measures against harmful organisms. diseases and pests that spread between plants do not respect national borders and can spread unstoppably throughout the european union. i therefore believe that we need a common approach and appropriate tools to help us prevent such cases. the problem is compounded by the fact that many plants are imported into europe from third countries, and it is therefore necessary to have clear rules for their importation in order to avoid the introduction of undesirable organisms into the eu and damage to european agriculture as such.

in writing. ‒ the european semester is the eu’s annual cycle of economic policy guidance and surveillance. i am pleased to share the european parliament’s input into the second phase of the semester 2016 focusing on the country specific implementation of priorities agreed within the annual growth survey 2016 report in february. last year’s heavily right-wing report was replaced by socially balanced structural reforms and increased investment as supported by the s&d group. thankfully, the report now clearly focuses on the need to increase investment in the eu in order to create more growth, convergence, quality jobs and fight poverty and inequality. also following the inclusion of the opinion from the employment and social affairs committee, the report now calls for a social imbalance procedure to be introduced into the economic coordination and a european minimum income framework to fight social exclusion in the eu. i urge that the eu and the member states better implement the revised economic policy mix which aims at increasing investment linked to eu2020 policies objectives including quality employment, education, innovation and growth enhancing policies.

in writing. ‒ industrial trans fats can be found in anything from fast food to bakery products, chips and margarine, however scientific research has linked the excessive consumption of them with obesity, diabetes, infertility, alzheimer’s and cardiovascular diseases. with 660 000 deaths annually in the eu, heart disease is one of europe’s biggest killers. given that trans fats bring more risk of heart disease than any other macro-nutrient on a per-calorie basis, it is important that we limit their consumption and that consumers know when they are eating them. currently, no eu legislation regulates the content of trans fats in food products or requires their labelling, although some countries do. imposing limits proved efficient and reduced death caused by heart disease significantly, like in denmark. i believe the eu should follow this path, which is what the text calls for.
in writing. on 26 october 2016, at the european parliament's plenary session in strasbourg, we voted on an oral question to the european commission with a subsequent resolution on trans-fatty acids. trans fatty acids in food have been shown to increase the levels of unhealthy cholesterol in consumers, contribute to cardiovascular disease and diabetes, as well as to certain cancers and allergies. they're even linked to alzheimer's and infertility. it is found, for example, in various ointments, margarines, baked goods, confectionery, chocolate substitutes, potatoes, biscuits, and mayonnaise. so in a fairly wide range of everyday foods. the resolution calls on the european commission to propose as soon as possible a binding limit for industrially used trans-fatty acids in order to reduce their intake among all groups of the population. in addition, the text mentions several very important related facts such as the proper labelling of packaged foods containing trans-fatty acids, the lack of information for consumers and even the alarming trend towards unhealthy food choices in low-income households. i'm very glad i could support such a proposal.
in writing. - i voted against it. the report calls for eu regulation of the percentage of so-called trans fatty acids in food, i believe that a european-wide regulation on the maximum percentage of so-called trans fatty acids in food would be difficult to control. i would leave it to the member states to decide whether they want to and can control the content of so-called trans-fatty acids in food. different national practices might then show which type of regulation is most effective.
in writing. i supported the motion for a resolution on the harm and health risks associated with the consumption of food containing industrially produced fatty acids. for example, these substances are found in foods sold in many fast-food establishments, as trans-fatty acids are cheaper and can be reused. it is no secret that eating such foods can have serious consequences for human health, causing cardiovascular disease, gallstones, and, not least, various cancers. i therefore fully support parliament's call for the member states to introduce legal limits for industrially produced trans-fatty acids in order to protect the health of their citizens. a positive example in this respect is denmark, where the introduction of similar measures has had a positive impact on reducing the number of deaths due to cardiovascular disease.
in writing. the current situation with regard to trans-fatty acids in food is largely incomprehensible. the negative impact of trans-fatty acids on human health has long been highlighted by both health and consumer organisations. consumers often consume them against their will, because legislation prohibits their presence on the packaging. first, the commission ignores the legislative obligation to subsequently publish, with a one-year delay, a report that heart disease is the number one cause of death in the eu and that high intake of trans-fatty acids significantly increases the risk of heart disease. it also acknowledges that food products with high levels of industrially produced trans-fatty acids are available on the market and that there is scope for improving public health if their intake is reduced. the european solution is out of sight, and some member states are introducing national legislative restrictions in the meantime. i believe that it is high time to adopt common rules on the internal market, i.e. a legislative proposal to restrict trans-fatty acids in food, and that is why i supported this resolution.
in writing. ‒ industrial trans fats have harmful health effects and are not well understood by many consumers in the eu. the best way to mitigate the risk that trans fats cause consumers would be to effectively lower the consumption of unhealthy trans fats by establishing legal limits for them, an effort which was already tested and found to be successful in denmark. i voted in favour of the motion for resolutions because i believe the eu needs to protect its citizens, who are often ill-informed, against a lethal and under-regulated product that is found hidden in nearly every food product on the shelves.

observations on the joint use of european funds to which citizens of all 28 member states contribute and should therefore be of substantial interest to them. at first sight, the conclusions of the report do not differ significantly from those of previous years in terms of legality, correctness and error. there is one difference i feel very strongly about. the trend is to take account of the added value of individual projects and investments, in addition to the factual accuracy of the use of european funds. i have also worked in this spirit on my report on the european commission's 2014 budget last year, and i appreciate that, little by little, this effort is being integrated into the other activities of all the european institutions. this time, the court's report has used the results-oriented approach more widely in horizon 2020, the largest programme of its kind in the world. this programme is concerned with science and research, where results are expected almost automatically, as support is directed towards projects of high quality and standard. in the context of future european court of auditors reports on the commission's management, i can imagine that budget chapters will be evaluated not only on the basis of error rates but will also take into account or use integrated and comprehensive result indicators. evaluating the effectiveness of projects in terms of outcome and performance is a new way forward. the priorities to be financed from the european budget change substantially over time, as do the conditions around us. and the use of the budget must respond to them. the european union must be more flexible, more focused on european added value, more simple and more focused on achieving results, not just on paper. if our common objective is to achieve, in particular, the added value of each euro invested, we must change the established rules (both withdrawal and controls) and set new ones that respond to the real needs of europe in the 21st century. i thank both institutions, the commission and the european court of auditors, for the path we are taking together, slowly but surely.

for the ppe group. in october of 2001, american planes started bombing afghanistan. that same year, american ground troops entered the country. in 2002, there was a sudden shift in the demographics of afghanistan. within months, some 5 million people who had fled the soviet occupation and the subsequent mujahideen war with the taliban returned home. they were mostly returning from iran and pakistan. the return of refugees was spontaneous, no one organized or ordered their return. five million people understood that the american intervention had ended 25 years of devastating wars. after foreign troops began leaving afghanistan in 2013, the flow of refugees reversed again. people started leaving afghanistan. afghans have thus become the largest group of refugees seeking eu membership and asylum in the eu, after syrians. i would like to draw your attention, ladies and gentlemen, to one crucial fact that the eu should be addressing. during the us presence and the presence of isaf international forces, several tens of thousands of afghan citizens have cooperated with these armed forces. because of the withdrawal of international forces, these people are being laid off and losing their jobs. they and their families are often branded by the taliban as traitors to their faith and nation, and their lives are in direct danger. these people, ladies and gentlemen, have been our direct allies in the armed struggle against the islamists and we cannot leave them to their fate. they're a big part of the afghan refugee wave. we cannot allow a security vacuum in afghanistan. if we allow it, nothing will stop young people from making the dangerous journey to europe. europe, together with the international community, must not let up in its support for the afghan national defence and security forces. the continued presence of nato, us troops and an eu military presence, for example through a police mission in afghanistan, is inevitable.

in writing. ‒ in reaction to recently started operation to liberate the city of mosul in northern iraq from so-called isis/daesh and extremely worrying humanitarian situation in the territory, i voted in favour of this resolution. it urges the european union, united nations and the whole international community to continue to support sustainably the iraqi government with humanitarian and military assistance. the republic of iraq has the right to defend its sovereign territory and the european union should support it in the fight against isis/daesh. the long-term aim must be then the reintegration of all iraqis including all ethnic and religious displaced minorities.
the situation in northern iraq is very dramatic. on the one hand, there is, and has been for quite some time, a stable autonomous kurdish territory, and on the other hand, to the south and southwest of this territory, in the places that were the core of ancient assyria, in the predominantly sunni part of iraq, where there used to be a very diverse community, there is only chaos. the failure to agree on a new government quickly enough after the last election in iraq created a power vacuum, which the islamic state took advantage of. the disbanded army of the former iraqi regime became a rich reservoir of trained military forces. the bloody suppression of the sunni part of iraq was just another trigger. the deployed iraqi army has evacuated mosul and the central part of the country virtually without a fight. she left behind weapons, ammunition, and virtually intact government buildings and documents, as well as money in bank houses. the yazidis and christians are in a critical situation, with forced conversions, kidnappings, enslavement of women and children threatening the very existence of these communities. from a relatively advanced iraqi functioning state, the intervention of the us and its allies has managed to threaten the existence of the entire community. it is also the fault of the eu and it is high time that we took effective action, otherwise we would continue to be complicit.

in writing. ‒ youth policies, although not the exclusive competence of the eu, are the backbone of the future generation. it is vital that the proper implementation of youth policies be made and that youth are included in the decision-making process at all levels so that decisions are targeted for the next generations. the eu youth strategy aims at doing just that. i decided however to abstain from voting on the report on the assessment of the eu youth strategy because, although i support the report’s initiative, calling for improvements in efforts to integrate eu youth, i found some of the wording in the report dubious, so i could not vote in favour.
in writing. i supported the report which deals with how the cap can improve job creation in rural areas, even though it could contain more forward-looking perspectives. rural areas account for 77% of the european union's territory, and i therefore consider it important to develop them dynamically and to reduce the gap in employment opportunities between urban and rural areas. the report highlights challenges in tackling rural labour supply issues, such as low wages and population decline, and looks at the potential for improving job creation.
in writing. rural areas form a substantial part of the eu's territory. for many years, more than 50% of the eu population has lived in cities. after the second world war, there was a decline in the agricultural and forestry workforce, and in the last 10 years, it has been a quarter of jobs. some rural areas have become virtually depopulated, while agriculture is the key to the appearance of a substantial part of the union's territory. small and medium-sized settlements are growing in suburban areas, where there are usually few job opportunities but where the necessary services are relatively available. in more remote areas, it is difficult to provide these services. the age structure of those running farms is also consistent with this. the european commission recommends redirecting cap direct payments towards small farmers. national governments often also provide support from their national budgets or regional funds. the commission considers that environmental legislation should be simple and understandable and easy to implement. it offers support to producers and farmers who grow local varieties and breed local breeds to develop employment opportunities. it is interesting that the commission is not aware of the dangers of adopting ceta, ttip and the mercosur community agreements. the recommendation to promote tourism-related services seems realistic. curiously, i see the promotion of the creation of specialized enterprises with more than 200 hives, this will not solve the lack of beehives.
in writing. i supported the report on 'how can the cap improve job creation in rural areas?', in particular because of the following points: whereas the commission, in its own impact assessment on the consequences of ttip, finds that predominantly rural areas, which are focused on specific activities and have limited alternatives, are more vulnerable; whereas rural areas and rural jobs are threatened by the shift away from traditional agricultural models that this agreement will bring; whereas trade agreements currently under negotiation, such as the transatlantic trade and investment partnership (ttip), the eu-canada comprehensive economic and trade agreement (ceta) and the eu-mercosur free trade agreement, pose a threat to job creation and the creation of conditions to support livelihoods in agriculture; and whereas the european parliament is concerned about the potential impact of agreements under negotiation, such as the transatlantic trade and investment partnership (ttip), the comprehensive economic and trade cooperation agreement (ceta) with canada and the eu-mercosur free trade agreement, on agriculture. this report shows that trade agreements such as ttip and ceta can be a complete disaster for european agriculture, and this report was adopted just days before ceta was signed.

in writing. ‒ although agriculture and the agri-food sector account for 6% of the european union's gdp, the demand for employment in this sector is steadily declining. in many european countries, there is a long-term outflow of labour from the agricultural sector and farmers' incomes are constantly falling. therefore, a comprehensive strategy for overall generational renewal in agriculture is needed. it is necessary to make full use of all the possibilities offered by the cap to support young and beginning farmers and to promote these more effectively. it is also necessary to create opportunities for young farmers, for example in terms of access to land. special attention should be paid to the involvement of women.
in writing. ‒ for a long time, eu rural areas have been suffering from high unemployment rates and depopulation. the report seeks to find out what are the options and possibilities that the common agricultural policy can offer to improve the situation in rural areas, particularly for farmers. european rural development is one of the main tools to help to make rural areas more attractive for living there. although the subject matter is pertinent, i voted to reject the report based on the very poor quality of content, which i felt lacked much added value with regards to proposing viable solutions to improve the unemployment situation in rural areas.

in writing. - i have supported a report aimed at ensuring the sustainable exploitation of cod stocks, whose stocks need to be restored and maintained at a level that will provide maximum sustainable yield. this is crucial from an environmental point of view, as the new regulation abolished the fishing effort regime, or the number of days a fishing vessel can spend at sea. in practice, this means that vessels with a very limited number of days no longer need to fish close to the coast, where the juvenile fish population is predominantly concentrated. this is an important measure to conserve fish stocks and i believe it is another step towards the stability of the marine biological environment and the prevention of further climate change. on the other hand, the decision to abolish the fishing effort regime will allow fishermen greater flexibility. it will enable vessels to no longer be forced to fish close to shore or in areas with a lower cod stock. in the present case, parliament has been engaged in a long-running dispute with the council over the choice of legal basis. last year, the court of justice ruled in favour of parliament and declared council regulations invalid. the social democrats have done an excellent job of negotiating to get this amendment of the regulation passed as soon as possible. i welcome the fact that we have succeeded in providing fishermen with greater legal certainty.
in writing. ‒ as a result of the serious depletion of four of europe’s cod stocks in the early 2000s, the eu imposed strict rules on the fishing industry through a recovery plan in 2004. the new regulation amends and updates the existing regulation of 2004 and 2008, in the aim countering problems currently existing in the plan, as well as to align the provisions of the regulation with the treaty of lisbon. i voted in favour of the amendments to the regulation because it is important the eu regularly revises and evaluates its regulatory measures to protect europe against any further depletion of one of the its most important resources.

in writing. i supported the report adopted under the consultation procedure, which aims to improve the fight against tax evasion, tax avoidance and aggressive tax planning. the mandatory automatic exchange of information in the field of taxation is internationally recognised as the most effective tool in the effort to achieve international tax transparency. the report confirms that there are strong reasons for further extending administrative cooperation between tax authorities to cover beneficial ownership information and that automatic exchange of beneficial ownership information can be integrated into the binding tax transparency framework already in place in the eu. the reality of these considerations is demonstrated by the fact that all member states are already participating in a pilot project on the exchange of information on beneficial ownership of companies and trusts. at the same time, however, only well-functioning tax authorities will use effectively acquired information to improve tax collection.

in writing. the urmas paet report as a whole is a call for the building of a joint intervention army of eu countries. we shall find it difficult to find in it a call for a radical solution (i.e. the elimination) to weapons of mass destruction at european and world level. the european defence agency is to play a major role in preparing eu states for aggression against third countries, according to the report. it's absurd that russia is considered a major threat alongside the islamic state. the proposals aim, in addition to a significant increase in national military spending, at specialising the armies of individual countries and at pooling joint purchases and maintaining forces and equipment to ensure compatibility. the european parliament is invited to set up a new committee on security and defence, with the creation of a joint military industrial and technological complex as a background. the proposal also requires that part of the expenditure for operations in this area be reimbursed from the eu budget. although the proposal in many places lays claim to nato as the basis for collective defence in europe, it calls for the acceleration of the creation of forces for common security and defence policy missions. since there are no references to territorial defence in the report, but the whole defence strategy is clearly geared towards intervention outside the eu, i am forced to reject the report in its entirety. defence and security cannot be based on preparing for interventions outside the eu.
in writing. ‒ i am convinced that we live in a world that raises new security questions and that it is our duty as directly elected representatives to respond to them. but i fear that a common european army would be a step in the wrong direction if it were merely a supplement to nato, which would not work anyway. given that the eu combatant force, which reached full operational capability in 2007 and whose mission is to engage in military action of a humanitarian, peaceful and peace-building nature, has not yet been used for procedural, financial and political reasons, despite the opportunity and the need to do so, we see that the eu is unable to agree to even a small number of combat units and now wants to build a common european army. i was somewhat struck by the fact that the european parliament considers that, with the growing integration of internal and external security, it is essential that the common security and foreign policy go beyond the resolution of external crises, to provide for a common security and defence and to enable the union to be involved in all phases of crises and conflicts using the full range of instruments at its disposal, as i personally see in this a call to arms that should be alien to the european peace project. i voted against it.
in writing. i supported the report on the european defence union because i believe that, in view of the risks and threats that exist in europe, a european defence union should be created, especially in view of the continuing deterioration of the security situation on the borders of the european union, especially in the eastern and southern neighbourhoods. i am therefore pleased that this report has been discussed and has received clear support. i believe that a european defence union should be based on regular joint security threat assessments by member states, but at the same time flexible enough to address the individual security challenges and needs of member states. all available instruments, including the involvement of the european budget, should be used to strengthen european cooperation between member states in the field of defence, which i consider to be a priority agenda for today (including structured cooperation based on the principle of voluntary participation).
in writing. security is the number one issue in europe today. following the conclusions of the bratislava summit, this report supports the idea of creating a european defence union, so that europe can respond quickly and effectively to threats and protect the interests of its citizens with sufficient vigour. this report supports the establishment of permanent structured cooperation between eu countries in the field of defence, supports the creation of an eu operations centre, supports increased support for the defence industry. at the same time, member states should commit to spending at least 2% of gdp on defence. i am convinced of the need to confront the growing threat of terrorism and the overall deteriorating security situation in europe and its environs. we can't ignore the geopolitical developments. the creation of a european defence union is, in my view, the right step, although its implementation and final form will certainly be the subject of far-reaching debate.
in writing. i supported the european parliament's own-initiative report on the european defence union, drawn up by the former estonian foreign minister urmas paet. i am convinced that security and defence are precisely the common tasks that citizens expect from the european union. it is also the area most sensitive to the influence of many factors on member states. the current security threats in europe's neighbourhood therefore make it all the more necessary to address the issue of common defence. the possible weakening of nato due to the change of priorities by the new us administration also encourages us to think more about europe's military capabilities and budgets (the target is a level of 2% of gdp for defence spending). the legal basis for the defence union is provided by the lisbon treaty, with the possibility of permanent structured cooperation and funds which have not yet been fully used. the resolution recalls most aspects of defence policy, from the institutional framework, through enhancing the interoperability of the armed forces, to the previously marginal but now important elements such as defence against cyber attacks. it also does not forget the key role of nato, although it works with the idea that europe will have to look after itself more on its own. the resolution makes a clear call for strengthening mutual defence and overall solidarity in the event of an attack.
in writing. - this report comes from the subcommittee on defense and security, of which i am vice-chair. it defines the substance, the legal context and the future steps towards the progressive establishment of a european defence union. i support that idea. i am convinced that they will significantly strengthen europe's ability to promote security within and beyond its borders. taking greater responsibility for our own security is essential in the face of the new global challenges that surround us. the eu's strategic independence requires a range of political instruments as well as a strong and modern military capability. the imperative is to create a framework for a european defence union in full association with nato. it must lead to more effective cooperation, fair burden-sharing and a meaningful division of labour between nato and the eu. a defense union doesn't happen overnight. i consider the most important immediate steps in this direction to be the launch of the proper process of the white paper on security and defence, the establishment of a permanent council of defence ministers and the review of the athena mechanism so that eu missions are financed by the union from common resources. member states should establish multinational forces within the framework of permanent structured cooperation (pesco) which will be available for the purposes of the csdp to maintain peace, prevent conflict and strengthen international security. the level of defence spending should reach 2% of gdp, of which 20% of the budget is for equipment. a permanent headquarters for the command and control of csdp military operations should be established.
